Copula sensitivity analysis showed that coefficient dependence was weak and model-selection uncertainty was substantial; therefore, the Gaussian copula was used only as a parsimonious working copula and was evaluated against the independence copula. Cross-site application showed that reservoir-derived and ensemble-based coefficients retained part of the temporal co-variation driven by meteorological forcing, but they also produced non-negligible magnitude errors and systematic bias under stream conditions. At Andong, the Yongdam-derived coefficients and copula ensemble showed relatively high correlations but substantially degraded bias and RMSE compared with site-specific calibration, indicating limited coefficient transferability and reservoir-stream aerodynamic regime mismatch. Overall, the proposed framework is best interpreted as an uncertainty-aware baseline estimation approach for data-limited environments, while direct calibration remains the benchmark for reliable in-stream evaporation estimation.

title: Seasonal regulation of dissolved organic and inorganic carbon in shallow groundwater of arid inland river basins: roles of recharge, evaporation, and hydrological processes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ayong Jiao, Jia Xu, Dongsheng Zhai, Bin Gao, Mingjiang Deng, Hongbo Ling
abstract: Groundwater systems play a critical role in the global carbon cycle. In arid inland river basins, the absence of hydrological pathways connecting to the ocean promotes the accumulation and storage of dissolved carbon (DC) within groundwater. However, the spatial distribution patterns and underlying controls of groundwater DC remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the Tarim River Basin was selected as a representative arid inland basin. Based on data from 72 monitoring wells, together with hydrological, hydrochemical, climatic, and remote sensing datasets, the spatial variations of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) were examined across wet and dry hydrological periods. Results showed that DOC concentrations in the lower reach increased with distance from the river during the dry period, whereas this spatial gradient weakened during the wet period due to recharge-related dilution. DIC showed relatively weaker spatial variation but clear hydrological-period differences, with lower concentrations during the wet period. DOC and DIC were positively correlated across river reaches and hydrological periods, suggesting coupled variation under changing hydrological and hydrochemical conditions. Redundancy analysis indicated that DOC was primarily associated with groundwater-table position and evapotranspiration, whereas DIC was closely related to total dissolved solids, Ca2⁺, and carbonate-related hydrochemical conditions. Ecological water conveyance affected recharge processes and the river–groundwater connectivity, thereby influencing groundwater carbon storage and transport in the lower reach. Overall, groundwater DC dynamics in the Tarim River Basin were jointly shaped by hydrological connectivity, evapotranspiration, evaporative enrichment, and hydrochemical evolution.

title: Regime shifts in European basins detected from the water budget and the Combined Climatological Deviation Index
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Monika Birylo
abstract: Climate regime shifts in Europe are abrupt and statistically robust, whereas hydrological regime shifts are smoother, delayed, and basin-dependent. However, these changes require continuous monitoring to enable a quick response to emerging disturbances. The study aims to assess the water regime and changes in the ten major basins in Europe, using water budget series, the Combined Climatologic Deviation analysed with the Pettitt and Bai-Perron tests. Based on the research, basins exhibit evidence of hydroclimatic reorganisation after approximately 2015, although the timing and magnitude vary substantially between regions. The proposed framework investigates whether independently derived climatic forcing and total water storage observations reveal coherent hydroclimatic regime shifts at the basin scale. This approach provides new insight into the timing, persistence and physical interpretation of hydroclimatic transitions across major European basins.

title: Constrained stochastic data sampling for deep learning–based time-lapse hydraulic tomography under reactive-induced permeability evolution
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Zi-Yan Chou, Jui-Pin Tsai, Bo-Tsen Wang, Chia-Hao Chang, Ying-Fan Lin, Tian-Chyi Jim Yeh
abstract: Most neural-network-based inversion methods are trained under specific statistical conditions, and their performance often deteriorates when the statistical properties of the target parameter fields deviate from those represented in the training dataset. This issue is particularly critical when employing neural-network-based inversion in remediation sites, where reagent injection may induce nonstationary permeability evolution through pore clogging and precipitation. To address this challenge, this study proposes a constrained stochastic data sampling strategy (SDSS) integrated with a three-dimensional Hydraulic Tomography Neural Network (HT-NN) for post-injection hydraulic conductivity (K) estimation. By using prior structural information from the pre-injection field and systematically resampling conditioning locations and conductivity values within physically constrained bounds, SDSS generates nonstationary training realizations that span a broad range of plausible post-injection K-field configurations. This strategy enables the generated training ensemble to span diverse statistical properties rather than being restricted to fixed statistical conditions, thereby reducing the mismatch between the training and target domains. The proposed framework was evaluated using field-informed semi-synthetic realizations and a field case study. The field-informed semi-synthetic validation results show that the SDSS–HT-NN framework can capture nonstationary K-field patterns. The field results indicate that, compared with the Successive Linear Estimator (SLE), HT-NN reproduces a more continuous band-like low-K structure near the injection region, shows a stronger near-field permeability decrease, and yields more accurate predictions of an independent hydraulic head dataset. These results demonstrate that the proposed SDSS–HT-NN framework provides an efficient approach for time-lapse K-field estimation under nonstationary reactive perturbations.

title: Reservoir releases and land cover interact to drive event-scale nitrate export in a large agricultural basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Camden Hatley, Erin C. Seybold, Sam Zipper, Amy J. Burgin, Dustin W. Kincaid, Li Li, Julia N. Perdrial, Donna M. Rizzo, Kristen L. Underwood
abstract: Understanding the drivers of nitrate export in rivers is critical for developing effective nutrient management strategies. However, few studies have explored event-scale drivers of export in large river basins with human modifications like reservoirs. Here, we analyzed nitrate concentration-discharge (C-Q) relationships from 215 events at the outlet of the Kansas River Basin, USA (155,690 km2) from 2014 to 2022 to (1) characterize event-scale nitrate export behaviors in a large agricultural basin, and (2) determine how different event characteristics are linked to these behaviors. We found that C-Q behaviors varied greatly, with 60% of events producing nitrate enrichment (n = 130) and 40% of events producing nitrate dilution (n = 85). These behaviors were correlated with complex spatial interlinkages between climate and land cover: across most of the basin, nitrate enrichment was correlated with drier antecedent conditions, but in wetter areas with higher proportions of urban and forested land cover, enrichment was more strongly correlated with precipitation magnitude/intensity. This difference in hydroclimatic controls on nitrate export might be related to differential distributions of nitrate sources within these land covers. Upstream of major reservoirs, however, neither variable was strongly correlated with C-Q behavior, suggesting that nitrate attenuation within reservoirs decouples event-scale concentration signals in upstream waters from those downstream. Reservoir outflows had variable impacts on C-Q behavior, reflecting reservoir-specific variations in nitrate attenuation efficiency. Together, these results identify specific complex interactions between hydroclimate, land cover, reservoir positioning, and individual reservoir properties that control event-scale nitrate export from large basins.

title: Climate change projections of probable maximum precipitation over large areas through depth-area-duration analysis: A case study in Brazil
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): João Paulo Lyra Fialho Brêda, Walter Collischonn, Pedro Torres Miranda, Rodrigo Cauduro Dias de Paiva
abstract: Extreme rainfall events can be catastrophic if not anticipated. Global warming is expected to intensify such events, thus any kind of human settlement must be planned and adapted to the emerging climate conditions. In this study, we investigated projections of rare extreme rainfall in large areas (>50,000 km2), consistent with the horizontal resolution of global climate models (GCMs). This spatial scale is particularly suitable for assessing extreme flood hazards in large river basins, providing insights into the evolving risks due to global warming. The analysis was conducted by comparing the envelopes of Depth-Area-Duration curves between the historical and future periods of 23 GCMs, considering the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, across four extensive and relatively homogeneous regions in South America. Regional aggregation allowed the detection of statistically significant signals for rare extreme rainfall. Through a spatiotemporal assessment, we conclude that: (i) stronger temperature increases lead to greater intensification of extreme rainfall; (ii) there are no significant differences in the magnitude of intensification among the four regions; (iii) rainfall events of different area size exhibit similar degrees of intensification; and (iv) shorter events present greater intensification. In particular, the 1-day extreme rainfall exhibit an increase consistent with the Clausius–Clapeyron relation. These results are in line with literature and provide a clear and robust summary of what to expect for rare rainfall events in large basins.

title: Tidal groundwater flow drives dissolved nitrogen cycling: linking internal transformation to interfacial flux
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ao Li, Yan Zhang, Zhenyang Li, Man Zhao, Jingjing Lyu, Lingwei Xu, Zhenyan Wang, Hailong Li, Guangxuan Han, Kai Xiao
abstract: Tidally driven groundwater flow creates dynamic redox gradients in coastal sandy aquifers, yet how these hydrodynamic conditions regulate nitrogen transformation and subsequent interfacial export remains poorly quantified. In this study, we investigated how tidally forced groundwater flow influences dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) cycling and interfacial nitrogen export in a sandy tidal flat by combining field monitoring, laboratory nitrogen incubation experiments, and groundwater numerical modeling. A two-dimensional SUTRA model calibrated with observed hydraulic heads was used to resolve groundwater-surface water interactions, including groundwater flow paths, velocity fields and exchange fluxes. The results showed that tidal groundwater flow generated distinct hydrodynamic zones differing in water exchange intensity, oxygen renewal, and residence time. Over a spring-neap tidal cycle, the modeled total submarine groundwater discharge flux (SGD) reached 102.6 m3 m−1, with fresh groundwater discharge contributing 27.2%. The potential nitrogen transformation rates and pathways were strongly zone-dependent: nitrification dominated in the intermediate low-velocity circulation zone, attaining rates of 9.9 × 10-7 to 4.2 × 10-6 mmol L−1 s−1. In contrast, DNRA occurred only locally and at much lower rates (2.5 × 10-9 mmol L−1 s−1)， with a localized hotspot in the high-velocity seaward discharge zone rather than in the low-velocity circulation zones. Bayesian relative-importance analysis further resolved how these zone-specific transformations governed interfacial nitrogen export: the high-velocity discharge zone served as a NO3 – source to coastal waters via submarine groundwater discharge (SGD), while the low-velocity circulation zone sequestered nitrogen as NH4 +. These results demonstrate that tidal groundwater flow dynamically links internal nitrogen transformation to interfacial nitrogen export through selective pathway activation.

title: Coupling reservoir supply potential with load allocation: A framework to enhance water supply security in multi-reservoir systems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Shuncai Zhang, Minglei Ren, Wei Xu, Te Zhang, Lanlan Zhao, Xiaoqin Hu, Zaichao Xie, Mi Zhou
abstract: Increasing water demand is intensifying spatial mismatches between reservoir capacity and supply obligations in regional water-supply systems. Existing studies mainly optimize reservoir operation under fixed supply loads, whereas the distribution of those loads among heterogeneous reservoirs is less often treated as a decision variable. This study presents an integrated regional decision-support framework that links reservoir water-supply potential (RWSP) with reservoir water-supply load allocation (RWSLA) in multi-reservoir systems, providing a pre-operational load-configuration complement to conventional operation simulation. Reservoir-specific ecological water demand is reserved as a non-adjustable priority requirement before socioeconomic load redistribution. RWSP defines feasible allocation ranges for the residual urban and agricultural demands, and candidate schemes are generated by truncated normal sampling within those bounds. Long-term joint operation simulations and multi-criteria evaluation are then used to assess reliability, resilience, vulnerability, water stress, and allocation equity. The framework is applied to five medium and small reservoirs in northeastern Chongqing, China. Results show that RWSP exhibits a clear hierarchy shaped by active storage capacity, mean annual runoff, total available water volume, and dry-period runoff reliability. System performance improves when loads are aligned with reservoir potential: overloading low-potential reservoirs increases vulnerability, whereas assigning higher loads to high-potential reservoirs improves reliability but may reduce equity. Threshold-like responses are observed within the tested load-allocation ranges, and partial-correlation and sensitivity analyses indicate weak competition-complementarity among reservoirs. The framework supports regional screening of spatial load configurations as a pre-operational complement to temporal reservoir-operation rules, while the derived allocation ranges and thresholds remain case-specific.

title: Photovoltaic panel arrays reshape soil erosion patterns and hydrodynamic processes on hillslopes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Nufang Fang, Rui Fan, Yue Du, Yi Zeng
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) installations on hillslopes alter rainfall redistribution and create spatially heterogeneous erosion patterns, yet the underlying hydraulic mechanisms remain poorly quantified. Using simulated rainfall experiments, this study evaluated the effects of PV panel installation height (0.4, 0.6, 0.8 m), tilt angle (30°, 35°, 40°), and arrangement type (linear, block) on runoff, sediment yield, hydraulic parameters, and rill morphology across 18 configurations. PV coverage reduced cumulative sediment yield by up to 56.6%, yet spatially disaggregated measurements revealed localized erosion intensification beneath panel drip lines. Transverse rills perpendicular to the slope formed exclusively beneath drip lines in all configurations, with spacing largely controlled by panel geometry rather than by hydraulic self-organization. Installation height was the dominant variable, as lower heights (0.4 m) maximized slope-scale sediment reduction (46.3%) through rainfall interception, whereas higher heights (0.8 m) intensified drip-line erosion through greater impact energy. Flow velocity, Reynolds number, shear stress, and stream power all amplified stepwise across successive covered zones, confirming a progressive downslope intensification of erosive force. Targeted drip-line mitigation with turf mats and gravel strips reduced localized sediment yield by 74% and 32% relative to untreated PV slopes. This study identifies a geometrically forced erosion regime beneath PV arrays and provides a hydrodynamic basis for erosion-resilient siting and design of hillslope solar installations.

title: TS-PINN: a dual-branch physics-informed neural network based on two-source theory for evapotranspiration estimation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Xing Rong, Chunlin Huang, Feinan Xu, Jinliang Hou, Peng Dou, Ying Zhang, Qiang Bie, Tianwen Feng, Zhihua Zhang
abstract: Accurate estimation of surface energy fluxes and evapotranspiration (ET) is essential for understanding land–atmosphere interactions. While data-driven methods efficiently fit observations, their “black-box” nature makes it challenging to guarantee physical interpretability and reliable extrapolation from instantaneous to daily ET. To address these limitations, we propose the Two-Source Physics-Informed Neural Network (TS-PINN), driven by both physical structure and physical constraints. The model constructs a vegetation–soil dual-branch architecture structurally aligned with the Two-Source Energy Balance (TSEB) theory, embedding partitioning mechanisms as structural inductive biases. For optimization, we design a multi-constraint physical loss that integrates instantaneous energy balance, component energy balance, the Priestley–Taylor (P–T) upper bound, and daily-scale consistency. We also adopt an adaptive weighting strategy to balance data fitting and physical consistency. Validation against eddy covariance (EC) data in the Heihe River Basin (HRB) (2015–2021 growing seasons) shows that TS-PINN significantly outperforms Random Forest (RF) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) baselines. Its root mean square error (RMSE) values are 31.22 W/m2 for sensible heat flux (H) and 44.03 W/m2 for latent heat flux (LE), with corresponding coefficients of determination (R 2) of 0.79 and 0.85, respectively. Ablation experiments reveal that the structural inductive bias enhances component-level representation, while the physical loss terms effectively constrain prediction boundaries. Specifically, the instantaneous energy balance constraint dominates H prediction accuracy, and the P–T constraint guides LE estimation. Daily ET converted from LE also presents good consistency with observations, with a Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of 0.88 and an R 2 of 0.81. Overall, TS-PINN offers a novel, accurate, and physically interpretable approach for simulating surface energy fluxes and ET.

title: Lagged global relationships between teleconnection indices and hydrological drought: a continental-scale analysis using ERA5-Land runoff data
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Mohammad Mahdi Nikta, Ahmad Sharafati, Alireza Hadian, Siyamak Doroudi, Reza Farzad, Yusef Kheyruri, Zaher Mundher Yaseen
abstract: Climate change and rising global temperature have made investigating drought and its characteristics more important than ever. This study investigates the relationships between hydrological drought and teleconnection indices by comparing the Pearson correlation coefficient between the Standardized Runoff Index (SRI) and five teleconnection indices at lags of 0 to 12 months globally, using runoff data from 1980 to 2024. This data was obtained from the ERA5-Land dataset with a spatial resolution of 9 km. In order to find the best lag for each teleconnection index, average correlation for each index was calculated both globally and for each continent. Additionally, the leading teleconnection index for each region was calculated by identifying the optimal lag for each index on each continent and using it to determine the index with the strongest correlation with SRI for each region. Furthermore, regions on the map where each teleconnection index at its best lag in each continent had meaningful correlations with SRI were identified. Moreover, probability densities of the correlations at the overall best lag for all teleconnection indices in each continent were investigated. Subsequently, the behavior of each pair of teleconnection indices compared to each other at a 1-month lag was analyzed. Results indicated that optimal lags at the continental scale are generally shorter than those at the global scale, and strong correlations between teleconnection indices and SRI are observed in many regions at these lags. Therefore, selecting the appropriate teleconnection index with its optimal lag can help identify early signs of hydrological drought and support proactive water resource management.

title: Reshaping of the active layer by retrogressive thaw slump in permafrost regions: coupled soil structural, hydrological, and thermal responses based on high-resolution in situ observations
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Zhongyang Zhang, Yibo Wang, Yingpu Liu, Yiran Tang, Hu Tao, Xinyu Chang, Zhanchao Hai, Zeyong Gao
abstract: Retrogressive thaw slumps (RTS) are typical thermokarst landforms in permafrost regions. Their development substantially reshapes the structure and functions of the active layer, thereby influencing the stability of the underlying permafrost. By integrating in situ monitoring of a representative RTS on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau with computed tomography (CT) scanning and hydrothermal observations, this study investigates the mechanisms through which RTS modulate soil structure, hydraulic properties, and thermal processes within the active layer. The results indicated that RTS development was associated with an overall decline in soil structural quality (36.8%), soil water storage capacity (11.5%), and soil thermal stability (19.3%). These changes were more pronounced in deep soil layers compared to shallow horizons. Furthermore, the reshaping of the active layer by RTS followed a progressive sequence: initial thermal enhancements triggered structural responses, which were subsequently amplified by hydrological feedbacks. During the active stage (headwall), heat exchange between the active layer and the external environment intensified substantially. This was accompanied by significant increases in soil thermal conductivity and thermal diffusivity, whereas volumetric heat capacity decreased markedly (P < 0.05). These thermo-physical alterations intensified freeze–thaw cycling and concurrently reduced soil shear strength. A distinct shift in mechanisms emerged during the stable stage (the collapse area). Macroporosity and the number of isolated pores increased sharply in the deep soil, while both water storage capacity and saturated water content decreased significantly (P < 0.05). Moreover, the thermal properties of the deep soil in the collapse area were significantly enhanced (P < 0.05). This condition accelerated downward heat transfer to the permafrost and contributed to sustained thermal disturbance. Ultimately, this study elucidates the micro-structural mechanisms underlying active layer reshaping by thaw slumps and offers new insights into the evolution of thermokarst landscapes.

title: Simulation of rainfall-runoff flow using three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Xin Yan Lye, Akihiko Nakayama
abstract: The three-dimensional (3-D) Weakly Compressible Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (WCSPH) has been reformulated to simulate overland flow on real terrains due to rainfalls. The rainfall is lumped into discrete particles falling over the terrain and the overland flow is simulated as three-dimensional free surface flows over topography following the WCSPH framework. The terrain and objects on it such as buildings and other structures are represented by boundary particles that are distributed over the combined surfaces having normal directions and roughness height used for setting dynamic boundary conditions, and the actual and potential moisture contents used to set infiltration conditions. The basic method is verified with experimental results of rainfall runoff from laboratory model plots and compared with existing runoff models. Then it is applied to a simulation of rainfall runoff over real terrains in Malaysia. It is found that the simulation by the present method gives details of overland flows that would not been obtained by the existing two-dimensional methods.

title: Hydraulic tomography for characterizing subsurface heterogeneity in fractured rocks: implications for in-situ recovery mining
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ning Luo, Chad Sorba, Cristina Ramirez, Mikkel Tetland, Xavier Lu Dac, Walter A. Illman
abstract: In-situ recovery (ISR) mining demands reliable forecasts of groundwater flow and solute transport, which are highly sensitive to subsurface heterogeneity. This study evaluated alternative modeling approaches for characterizing heterogeneity using data from Denison’s Wheeler River Property, Saskatchewan, Canada. Spatial distributions of hydraulic conductivity (K) and specific storage (Ss ) were characterized using four modeling cases: a homogeneous case, a geology-based zonation case, and two hydraulic tomography (HT) cases. All models were calibrated against 16 cross-hole aquifer tests, with one HT model additionally constrained by the long-term feasibility field test (FFT) completed at a larger scale. The estimated K and Ss fields were validated against independent tracer test data. Results revealed systematic improvements in predictive performance with increasing model complexity, with HT models reproducing observed hydraulic responses and breakthrough curves with higher fidelity. Without using structural data as conditioning information, the HT inversions revealed high-K features aligned with a known shear fault (WS shear) and positively correlated with fracture frequency. Incorporating FFT data further resolved large-scale hydraulic connectivity and improved transport prediction at the more distant extraction well. These findings underscore that accurately characterizing spatial K and Ss heterogeneities through HT is essential for ISR wellfield design, recovery optimization, and environmental protection.

title: Spatiotemporal variation of extreme precipitation and its terrain modulation in the Hengduan Mountains: machine learning and interpretable analysis
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Qiyan Duan, Guokun Chen, Xingwu Duan, Qingke Wen, Haijuan Zhao, Fengyuya Jing, Zhiyuan Chen
abstract: Extreme precipitation events have a significant impact on hydrological processes and disaster risks, especially in mountainous areas with complex topography, where precipitation patterns exert stronger exacerbating effects. However, existing studies mostly focus on statistical trends, and the understanding of the spatial organization, propagation characteristics, and topographic control mechanisms of extreme precipitation is still limited. This study uses high-resolution daily precipitation data from 2005 to 2024, along with ten ETCCDI indices, to systematically examine the spatiotemporal evolution of extreme precipitation in the Hengduan Mountains. Through event synchronicity and lag analysis, the regional variations and propagation paths of extreme precipitation events are characterized. Additionally, a spatial homogeneity index is introduced to quantify the spatial organization of the extreme precipitation field. Furthermore, this research applies the XGBoost regression framework, complemented by SHAP, CP-PD, and permutation feature importance (PFI) analysis, to investigate the nonlinear influence of topographic factors on different types of extreme precipitation. The results indicate that extreme precipitation in the Hengduan Mountains primarily exhibits a gradual evolution rather than abrupt changes, with a significant increase in intensity during the rainy season. Specifically, intensity-related indices such as PRCPTOT, Rx5day, and R95p show consistent positive trends, with slopes ranging from 0.35 to 1.71 in most regions, indicating stronger and more frequent precipitation events. Spatially, extreme precipitation demonstrates a clear southeast-northwest contrast, with higher intensity observed in low latitudes and orographically uplifted areas. Event synchronicity analysis reveals significant regional variability during the monsoon season, while lag and spatial evenness analyses identify a stable south-to-north propagation pattern, showing a south-to-north statistical sequence that is seasonally consistent with the background monsoon circulation and regional topographic organization. Machine learning results show that elevation provides the largest predictive contribution within the XGBoost models the spatial distribution of extreme precipitation, with elevation scores (SHAP analysis) reaching up to 0.70 for extreme indices such as R99p, while slope, curvature, and elevation play significant roles in modulating moderate-intensity extreme events. In contrast, the model attribution becomes increasingly concentrated on elevation for the most extreme events like R99p.

title: A national-scale comparison of carbon dioxide emissions from lakes and reservoirs in China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Danni Yuan, Zifan Wang, Y.Jun Xu, Ping Jiang, Siyue Li
abstract: Lakes and reservoirs are the two dominant lentic ecosystems worldwide, yet their respective contributions to large-scale CO2 emissions remain poorly constrained. Here, CO2 evasion from 165 inland water bodies across five limnological regions of China, including the Northeast Plain and Mountain Lake (NPML), Eastern Plain Lake (EPL), Inner Mongolia–Xinjiang Lake (IMXL), Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau Lake (YGPL), and Tibetan Plateau Lake (TPL) regions, was quantified during 2021–2023 using a random forest model to predict water alkalinity for subsequent CO2 calculations. Total annual emissions were estimated at 7.41 ± 1.04 Tg C, with lakes contributing the majority (7.02 ± 1.09 Tg C yr−1) and reservoirs accounting for a much smaller fraction (0.39 ± 0.01 Tg C yr−1). Lake emissions displayed a non-monotonic inter-annual pattern, declining from 2021 to 2022 before increasing in 2023, whereas reservoir emissions showed limited interannual variation. Strong spatiotemporal contrasts further distinguished the two systems, with lake emissions peaking in summer–autumn in the NPML and EPL regions, and reservoir emissions maximized in winter in the YGPL and NPML regions. These findings reveal fundamentally different spatiotemporal emission regimes between lakes and reservoirs, indicating that aggregating the two systems can mask key variability in inland-water carbon fluxes.

title: Hierarchical prediction of streamflow and organic carbon at event scale using a physics-guided AI hybrid framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Venkatesh Budamala, Euiyoung Choi, Minchang Kim, Sangchul Lee, Hyunglok Kim
abstract: Agricultural watersheds are major contributors to storm-driven export of streamflow (Q) and organic carbon, including particulate organic carbon (POC) and dissolved organic carbon (DOC), which strongly influence downstream water quality and aquatic biogeochemical processes. However, accurate prediction of event-scale hydro–carbon dynamics remains challenging because process-based models require extensive calibration, whereas purely data-driven models often lack physical consistency. This study presents a physics-guided spatial–temporal hybrid framework (PhyST-HC) that integrates uncalibrated Soil and Water Assessment Tool–Carbon (SWAT-C) simulations with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Transformer-based attention mechanisms for hierarchical prediction of Q, POC, and DOC. Distributed SWAT-C-derived hydrological and carbon-state variables serve as physics-guided watershed descriptors, while GNNs capture upstream–downstream connectivity and the Transformer learns temporal watershed memory. The framework was evaluated in the agriculturally dominated Tuckahoe Creek Watershed (TCW), USA. Results showed that PhyST-HC achieved Q performance comparable to a SUFI-2-calibrated SWAT-C model (KGE = 0.82) without watershed-specific calibration, while substantially outperforming both SUFI-2 and SWAT-LSTM for organic carbon prediction (POC: KGE = 0.68 vs. 0.04 and 0.34; DOC: KGE = 0.74 vs. 0.43 and -0.05, respectively). Ablation analysis confirmed the importance of physics-guided SWAT-derived watershed-state variables beyond standalone GNN and Transformer models. The framework also improved representation of event-scale POC flushing, delayed DOC transport, and watershed connectivity under contrasting storm conditions. These findings demonstrate the potential of physics-guided hybrid learning for accurate and transferable event-scale hydro–carbon prediction in agricultural watersheds.

title: Effect tracking and flux tracking to quantify preferential flow responses at the hillslope scale
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Jaromir Dusek, Tomas Vogel
abstract: Understanding runoff generation and water dynamics in hillslopes exhibiting preferential flow effects remains a persistent challenge in hydrology. In this study, we combined effect and flux tracking with a two-dimensional dual-continuum model to investigate hillslope runoff generation and water age composition in runoff components (stormflow and deep percolation), root water uptake, and hillslope soil water storage. The model, previously validated against observed discharge and isotope data, was used to simulate water flow and virtual tracer transport during a sequence of five rainfall–runoff events. Effect tracking showed that stormflow responded rapidly during large rainfall events through activation of preferential flow paths, whereas smaller events produced weaker and delayed responses. Hillslope storage exhibited pronounced soil moisture memory, with earlier events conditioning subsequent flow responses. Flux tracking indicated that stormflow was largely composed of pre-event water, with event water contributing both during the event itself and through remobilization in subsequent storms. Root water uptake accounted for a substantial fraction of event water loss, with sustained contributions over multiple events, whereas deep percolation showed the longest delays. Ensemble analysis indicated that approximately 60% of the cumulative stormflow response occurred within five days, whereas only about 40% of the event water recovered in stormflow was exported during the same period. This finding demonstrates a clear decoupling between rapid hydrological responses and much slower event water turnover, reflecting substantial subsurface storage and mixing. By combining effect and flux tracking at the hillslope scale, this study quantified process-specific hydrological memory and the remobilization of event water in stormflow, deep percolation, root water uptake, and soil water storage.

title: Improving water pixel detection in SWOT Pixel Cloud (PIXC) data over small reservoirs using machine learning methods
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Shayan Shirafkan, Mohammad Ali Sharifi, Mohammad J. Tourian
abstract: This study presents a machine learning-based framework to improve water pixel detection in SWOT Pixel Cloud (PIXC) data for reservoir monitoring applications. Unlike general land-cover classification, the primary objective is to reduce false positive and false negative water detections in PIXC products, thereby improving the accuracy of derived reservoir surface area and volume estimates. The proposed framework integrates PIXC-derived features with an external long-term water occurrence prior (based on Landsat 5–8 observations) to refine pixel-level water detection. Three supervised learning algorithms, namely K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), are used not only as predictive models but also as diagnostic tools to investigate the behavior of PIXC-derived inputs within the feature space. These inputs include radar backscatter observables, interferometric coherence, detection quality indicators, and geometry-dependent parameters. The models are trained and evaluated across three reservoirs in Iran (Dez, Shahid Rajaei, and Agh Chay), selected to represent distinct hydro-climatic and geomorphological conditions, and are subsequently applied to eight reservoirs to assess their spatial transferability. Performance is quantified using pixel-level Intersection-over-Union (IoU), together with hydrological consistency metrics including correlation coefficient, Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE), and Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) against in-situ observations. Beyond predictive performance, the results provide interpretability insights into PIXC input features. In particular, features related to detection uncertainty, interferometric coherence, and imaging geometry consistently show strong influence on water detection performance, suggesting that these components of the PIXC processing chain play a critical role in misclassification patterns. This finding highlights potential directions for improving uncertainty representation and quality control within future SWOT PIXC products. Results indicate that all machine learning models improve agreement with both SWOT PIXC and LakeSP products in terms of water detection performance and consistency with in-situ-derived reservoir area estimates. Overall, the findings suggest that incorporating physically meaningful PIXC features together with external hydrological priors can significantly enhance water pixel detection reliability. This approach provides practical guidance for improving downstream SWOT-derived reservoir products and offers insights that may support future refinements of the PIXC processing chain without requiring modifications to the original satellite data stream.

title: How do branches modulate litter hydrology? Disentangling their effects on water retention and temperature-sensitive evaporation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Zhen Han, Jiangwen Li, Yaying Feng, Minzhe Liu, Nufang Fang
abstract: The forest litter layer is a key hydrological interface that regulates water retention, infiltration, and evaporation, yet the role of branches, an often‑overlooked component, in modulating these processes remains poorly understood. This study investigated the water retention dynamics and temperature-dependent evaporation of litter from three typical vegetation types (Pinus massoniana, Magnolia grandiflora, and Osmanthus fragrans) in the karst regions of southwestern China. A fully controlled experiment was conducted using five leaf-branch mixing ratios (0%, 15%, 30%, 45%, and 100% branch mass proportion). The results showed that water-holding capacity increased logarithmically with immersion time (R 2 > 0.84), with M. grandiflora exhibiting the highest maximum capacity (2.08 kg·m−2), followed by O. fragrans (1.54 kg·m−2) and P. massoniana (1.16 kg·m−2). Increasing branch proportion significantly reduced water retention in broadleaved species but had no significant effect on P. massoniana. Water absorption rate followed a power-law decay function (R 2 > 0.79), with initial absorption rates ranging from 0.79 to 19.92 g·g−1·h−1; leaves generally showed higher rates than branches. Evaporation was strongly temperature-driven, with rates at 30°C significantly higher than those at 0°C, and followed a power-law relationship with time (R 2 > 0.95). A significant negative correlation emerged between water‑holding capacity and evaporative water loss (p < 0.01), a relationship that intensified at higher temperatures. Collectively, these findings quantitatively demonstrate how litter composition and temperature jointly regulate hydrological functions, providing critical parameters for improving forest hydrological models and guiding function-based ecological restoration in fragile karst ecosystems.

title: Physical continuous-simulation SWAT + framework to develop flow duration curves within the contiguous United States
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Jungang Gao, Natalja Čerkasova, Michael J. White, Peter Allen, Jeffrey G. Arnold, Katrin Bieger, Mazdak Arabi, Ryan Bailey
abstract: The flow duration curve (FDC) is a fundamental tool in hydrology representing the cumulative distribution function of streamflow with time. As such, it is a valuable indicator of watershed performance, being controlled by rainfall, runoff, and storage. The shape of the FDC represents the complex interactions of climate, geology, topography, vegetation and human activities. This study is a novel effort to predict the FDC using a continuous simulation daily time step model calibrated to mean annual flow for CONUS (Contiguous United States of America). Model performance was evaluated using long-term USGS streamflow records from relatively undisturbed gages, while sites substantially affected by major reservoirs and water diversions were excluded. Model outputs are compared regionally to modeled FDCs and gage data. Output is compiled by NHDPlus reach for CONUS. Evaluations based on representative FDC quantiles demonstrate the model’s ability to simulate high, medium, and low flows with average Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values of 0.69, 0.84, and 0.56, respectively. The significant advantage of employing a continuous simulation model lies in its ability to simulate diverse climate and land use scenarios, offering valuable insights beyond historical data limitations.

title: A river-augmented highly parameterized linear inverse method for enhanced water table estimation across China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ailin Liu, Jianying Jiao
abstract: Large-scale groundwater assessment in China is fundamentally constrained by the scarcity of in situ well observations, leading to prohibitive uncertainties in water table mapping. To overcome this limitation, we use river-stage information as additional hydraulic-head constraints along river corridors, based on the hydraulic connection between rivers and shallow aquifers. Here, we present a river-augmented highly parameterized linear inverse method (HPLIMRG) that extends a groundwater-only formulation (HPLIMG) by incorporating river-stage observations, together with well measurements, as additional hydraulic-head constraints. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated across scales. In synthetic experiments, HPLIMRG reduces root mean square error (RMSE) from 0.68 m to 0.55 m compared to HPLIMG, without compromising uncertainty quantification. In the High Plains Aquifer, RMSE drops from 0.79 m to 0.35 m, while the median standard deviation of the water table decreases from 0.37 to 0.097 m. Critically, in a data-sparse, continental-scale application to map water table depth across China for December 2024 and March 2025, HPLIMRG yields a similar accuracy gain (RMSE from 5.04 m to 4.22 m) and a dramatic reduction in uncertainty (from 1.29 m to 0.06 m). Collectively, these results demonstrate that incorporating river-stage observations into the HPLIM framework improves water table estimation accuracy and reduces uncertainty, with the largest gains in sparsely monitored regions, as shown across China. By converting rivers into a dense, physically constrained observational network, this framework, applied here at 1 km resolution for large domains, offers a robust and scalable pathway for water table mapping where well observations are scarce.

title: Multi-objective storage optimization for the cascade sluice group canal system based on hydraulic response relationships and feasible search space
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Quan Li, Xiaohui Lei, Chao Wang, Pengyu Jin, Zhao Zhang, Xiaonan Chen, Zhongzheng He
abstract: The operation optimization of a Cascade Sluice Group Canal System faces two core challenges. The conventional volume compensation model fails to incorporate hydraulic response characteristics, leading to a lack of effective water-level constraints and a fitness function of high-dimensional optimization problems that makes convergence difficult. We propose FSS-MOSOM, a multi-objective storage optimization model (MOSOM) that incorporates hydraulic response relationships to ensure compliance with water-level constraints. The model introduces a feasible search space (FSS) to reduce the search space before optimization, thereby alleviating the computational burden and improving computational efficiency. FSS-MOSOM is implemented on the final 13 canal pools of the South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project. Compared with volume compensation scheduling, the proposed FSS-MOSOM scheduling reduces the maximum water-level deviation from −0.15 to −0.04 m at the end of the prediction period and the maximum average absolute deviation from 0.12 to 0.05 m. FSS-MOSOM exhibits superior optimization performance compared to MOSOM without search space reduction. This includes improved stability of the optimization results, accelerated convergence speed, and the ability to find quasi-optimal solutions. The proposed model substantially narrows the search space and enhances water-level regulation, providing a method for scheduling decisions for water transfer projects.

title: Large-scale circulation anomalies at drought occurrence over northern China during El Niño developing stage
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Hao Yin, Zhenchen Liu, Zhiyong Wu, Hai He
abstract: El Niño-induced droughts over northern China have been extensively studied regarding their interannual variability. However, the spatial heterogeneity of their occurrence regions (e.g., the upper-middle Yellow River Basin, North China, or Northeast China) and their specific large-scale circulation anomalies remain unknown. In this study, we identify El Niño-induced northern China droughts with diverse spatial distributions, investigating their drought-inducing circulation patterns and associated phase transitions. The key findings are as follows. Despite diversity in El Niño developing stages and associated spatially heterogeneous drought locations, these summer-autumn droughts consistently exhibit a local dynamic structure resembling the first baroclinic mode, characterized by upper-tropospheric convergence and enhanced mid-low-level northerly anomalies. Three principal large-scale circulation pathways are delineated: the Eurasian Mid-Latitude Pathway featuring Rossby wave trains propagating from North Atlantic, the Pacific-East Asian Pathway through large-scale upper-tropospheric convergence over tropical regions and associated meridional circulation, and the North Pacific Pathway where a negative North Pacific Oscillation (NPO) prior to El Niño establishment fosters mid-latitude anticyclonic anomaly pattern and northerly flow over northern China. Meanwhile, rapid phase transitions of typical mid-latitude teleconnection indices at the drought occurrences are defined and investigated. Positive-to-negative phase transitions of the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and NPO can potentially trigger drought occurrence over northern China. A persistent negative NAO, often coupled with specific North Atlantic sea surface temperature patterns (e.g., a negative North Atlantic Tripole), promotes the propagation of mid-high-latitude wave trains, ultimately enhancing drought-inducing circulation anomalies over northern China. These achievements contribute to improving seasonal drought prediction skills.

title: Evaporation, energy balance, and paleohydrology of the lakes along the Dead Sea rift
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): G. Tau, Y. Enzel, I. Sirota, N.G. Lensky
abstract: Lake evaporation is a dominant yet poorly constrained component of water and energy budgets. This uncertainty critically undermines necessary paleoclimate reconstructions, particularly for terminal lakes, whose levels are considered the best direct indicators of the precise balance between catchment precipitation and evaporative losses. We address this by applying a physically grounded framework for lake evaporation based on a hybrid approach of direct measurements and theoretical analysis of lake energy-balance and its thermal-equilibrium solution, combined with calibrated bulk formulae. High-resolution data from long-term eddy-covariance measurements at three adjacent Dead Sea Rift lakes—spanning wide gradients in salinity (freshwater to hypersaline), climate (Mediterranean to hyper-arid), and thermal structure—were used to calibrate bulk formulae relating environmental forcing to heat fluxes. We show that the thermal equilibrium approach depends on the lake’s thermal response time; shallow lakes reach equilibrium at intra-annual timescales, whereas deeper stratified lakes require annual forcing. These observations, combined with accurate bulk formulae that relates to the environmental conditions, provides tools for modeling global lake evaporation using only standard environmental data and for reconstructing paleo-evaporation. Applying this framework to the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) highstand of Lake Lisan (the Levant), we bound evaporation rates and determine that a minimum annual water inflow approximately four times greater than modern levels was required to stabilize the lake. These results indicate significantly higher precipitation in the Dead Sea watershed during the LGM.

title: Locally relevant streamflow reanalysis using ensemble data assimilation and a gauge-based adaptive localization scheme
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ved Prakash, Manabendra Saharia
abstract: Accurate, high-resolution streamflow estimates are crucial for effective water management, flood risk assessment, and mitigation planning. However, predicting streamflow using integrated hydrologic-hydrodynamic models remains challenging due to model errors and uncertainties in initial conditions. This study presents a novel streamflow Data Assimilation (DA) framework that combines Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) with two key innovations: a gauge-based covariance localization derived from historical tuning aligned with a dense river network and targeted covariance inflation at gauge stations. The DA framework is implemented within a modeling chain comprising the Noah-MP land surface model and a vector-based streamflow routing model, MizuRoute, covering 553,312 river reaches across the Indian subcontinent. Results show that the assimilation framework significantly improves streamflow simulations, increasing the median Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) by 0.22 and the median KGE skill score by 0.15 across both gauged and ungauged stations at the daily scale. The DA also enhances key hydrological signatures and exhibits strong performance during peak flow conditions. Notably, during peak flow events, the median probability of detection (POD) increases from 0.22 to 0.39 at gauged and from 0.16 to 0.29 at ungauged stations. The model demonstrates greater improvement in smaller catchments, which are more susceptible to flash floods. Furthermore, the mean peak flow and timing error for correctly predicted (“hit”) events are reduced by over 9% and over 1.5 days, respectively. This first-of-its-kind study in the Indian subcontinent on streamflow DA using a large-scale hydrologic-hydrodynamic model at a daily time scale offers a robust foundation for enhancing flood forecasting systems and informing sustainable water resource management under changing climate scenarios.

title: Rainfall frequency analysis and its uncertainty analysis in Taihu Basin: Bayesian inference of four-parameter Kappa distribution based on specially-formulated pivotal quantities
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Weiqiang Zheng, Shuguang Liu, Zhengzheng Zhou
abstract: Four-parameter Kappa (FPK) distribution is widely recommended in rainfall frequency analysis, whose complex distribution function makes reliable parameter point estimation and confidence interval construction very challenging. In the current study, we establish a novel Bayesian framework to estimate the parameters and return levels of the FPK distribution and to perform uncertainty analysis. By introducing three specially formulated pivotal quantities, the proposed framework avoids the need to explicitly specify parametric prior distributions for all parameters. Instead, only the prior of one parameter (h) is required, while the joint distribution of the remaining parameters is induced through the pivotal transformation. On this basis, statistical inference for the four parameters and return levels is conducted using the maximal data information prior. The proposed framework is applied to annual maximum daily rainfall series from 36 rain gauges in the Taihu Basin. For reference, results obtained using conventional bootstrap methods are also presented. Interval estimates of both the parameter and design rainfall depth are obtained for all gauges. The results show that the spatial distributions of uncertainty levels for parameter and design rainfall depth are complex. In the middle and northwest of Taihu Basin, the design rainfall depth is relatively large and the associated uncertainty level is high, which requires additional attention in practical applications. Compared with the conventional Bootstrap methods, the parameter realizations generated by the proposed pivotal quantity method tend to retain relatively high likelihood values, leading to more reasonable point estimates and confidence interval estimates. The proposed framework is flexible and substantially simplifies prior specification for the FPK distribution, since only the prior distribution of h needs to be explicitly specified, while the distributions of the remaining parameters are determined through the pivotal quantities.

title: Attribution of the 2021 record-breaking compound drought-heatwave extreme in Central Asia to anthropogenic warming, atmospheric circulation, and NAO
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Liangwei Li, Yaqi Yang, Xiang Zhang, Sijia Luo, Yansong Guan, Xihui Gu, Lunche Wang
abstract: During the spring (April–June) of 2021, Central Asia experienced its most severe compound drought‑heatwave extreme (CDHE) in nearly 60 years, causing severe impacts on the regional environment, economy, and society. Anticyclonic circulation anomalies, anthropogenic warming, and the negative phase of the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) have been recognized as potential triggers of this CDHE, yet the quantitative contributions of each factor to its intensity and occurrence probability remain poorly understood. By introducing a storyline‑probability‑based attribution framework and leveraging reanalysis data and model simulations, this study finds that the CDHE intensity was jointly dominated by the anticyclonic circulation anomaly (contributing 44.08%) and anthropogenic warming (contributing 36.06%), while the NAO negative phase played a substantial modulating role. These factors increased the probability of CDHE by approximately 6.75, 32.30, and 3.44 times, respectively. Future projections indicate that the probability of a 2021-like CDHE depends strongly on the emission pathway and evaluation baseline. Under a moving baseline, the warming–wetting trend may attenuate drought intensity as defined by precipitation deficit, thereby reducing the probability of a 2021-like CDHE relative to the contemporaneous climate background. However, under a fixed historical baseline, the dominant role of heatwaves is accentuated, and the cumulative effect of anthropogenic warming yields a consistent upward trend in the probability of a 2021-like CDHE across all emission pathways. Our findings underscore that climate adaptation planning in Central Asia must account for the nonlinear and divergent responses of drought and heatwaves within the future context of regional warming-wetting trends.

title: Analysis of cross-sectional solute concentration profiles from pulsed point sources in 3D steady flow
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Ran Gao, Min Pang, Juncai Gao
abstract: Analytical characterization of cross-sectional solute concentration distributions remains limited for key theoretical models involving pulse point-source releases in three-dimensional aquatic environmental flow systems. This gap hinders the understanding of fundamental transport mechanisms by obscuring distributional divergences between source release scenarios, particularly the essential differences between pulse point- and area-sources. Addressing this, we develop an analytical framework for spatial solute distributions under steady 3D pulse point-source releases. Combining dispersion-diffusion theory with solutions of concentration moment equations, we derive a first-order approximate solution for cross-sectional concentration. This framework enables comparison of concentration distributions between pulse point source (high initial inhomogeneity) and pulse area-source (initial uniformity) releases at varied streamwise positions, quantified by a dimensionless discrepancy index r. The results demonstrate both the strong initial spatial non-uniformity of the solute and its release location significantly affect the resulting cross-sectional concentration distribution. Theoretically, directly applying classical area- source models to point-source pollution induces significant prediction errors in cross-sectional concentrations. Using a real pollution case study, we further examine parametric dependencies of concentration distributions and environmental risk mechanisms under point-source releases, highlighting the critical importance of water quality monitoring and emergency planning. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for analyzing pulse solute transport in complex 3D flows, advancing methodologies for pollution forecasting and wetland conservation.

title: Slope-weighted cost distance for modeling flood dynamics: a physics-informed random forest approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Takumi Sugahara, Tatsuro Sato, Yasuhiro Mitani
abstract: Rapid flood inundation forecasting is a crucial tool for disaster mitigation; however, physically-based models are computationally intensive, and conventional data-driven models often exhibit poor generalizability and limited interpretability. To address these deficiencies, we propose a novel physics-informed random forest framework that incorporates a slope-weighted cost-distance feature to represent spatiotemporal flood dynamics and validate the framework using data from the Kinugawa River Basin, Japan. By weighting the distance with the terrain gradient, this feature approximates gravity-driven flow paths, enabling the model to significantly outperform the static baselines (F1-score improvement from 0.507 to 0.893). To improve performance for hydrographs withheld from training but drawn from the predefined 31-scenario set, we introduced a hydrograph feature-space sampling strategy. The strategy selects representative training cases by clustering peak discharge and total volume; using only four training cases, it achieved an F1-score of 0.904 for the withheld scenarios. Furthermore, a SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided quantitative evidence that the model learned statistical relationships consistent with flow-path selection and volume-related flood expansion. The proposed framework offers a transparent and computationally efficient alternative to black-box deep learning models for real-time forecasting, while its reliability for hydrographs beyond the sampled discharge-volume and waveform range remains untested.

title: Performance analysis of the OS LISFLOOD hydrological model using nearly three decades of satellite laser ranging data
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part B Author(s): Filip Gałdyn, Laura Jensen, Radosław Zajdel, Krzysztof Sośnica, Henryk Dobslaw
abstract: We evaluate the performance of the OS LISFLOOD hydrological model by comparing its terrestrial water storage (TWS) estimates with long-term geodetic benchmark products derived from Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR), GRACE, and DORIS, over the period 1995–2022. Our analysis focuses on the 100 largest river basins, assessing the model’s ability to capture both seasonal and interannual variability. We find that OS LISFLOOD outperforms a model widely applied in geodetic studies, the Land Surface Discharge Model (LSDM) in representing large-scale TWS variations, particularly in tropical and subtropical basins and in seasonal and low-frequency dynamics of TWS. Comparisons with SLR-based gravity field models extend the evaluation into the pre-GRACE era (1995–2004), highlighting OS LISFLOOD’s robustness in depicting long-term hydrological changes. We also find that combined SLR+GRACE and SLR+DORIS datasets provide useful long-term geodetic benchmarks for assessing hydrological model consistency, particularly in large tropical basins. This work contributes to advancing long-term reconstructions of the global water cycle and supports geodetic applications, including environmental loading corrections and studies of Earth rotation. The results emphasize the importance of high-resolution hydrological models in improving the accuracy of TWS simulations and their application to geophysical research.

title: CO 2 degassing and subsequent carbonate precipitation behind the outage of geothermal water cooling infrastructure in southern Tunisia: an integrated diagnosis
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Hiba Kefi, Mohsen Henchiri, Giovanna Della Porta, Lahmadi Moumni, Mehmet Cihat Alçiçek
abstract: The geothermal water-cooling infrastructure in southern Tunisia is experiencing operational problems related to the precipitation of carbonates throughout the cooling systems, driven by CO2 degassing by flowing water. During the flow from the feeding well to collecting ponds, the decrease in water temperature is commonly associated with an increase in pH and saturation state with respect to carbonate minerals. The precipitated carbonates consist dominantly of fibrous aragonite, displaying morphologies and microfabrics resembling natural travertines. Carbonate precipitation is primarily regulated by physical factors such as inorganic CO2 degassing, decreasing from 21 to 8 mg/L, temperature cooling gradient from 67 to 25°C, pH variations (pCO2-induced) from 7.8 to 9.1, water flow hydrodynamics from riffle-flow and splashing to more laminar flow, and secondly facilitated by microbial mats dominated by filamentous cyanobacteria and green algae (diatoms, Oocardium) that colonize the diverse components of the system. The thickest carbonate precipitates were recorded in lower pools, where the water had already undergone intensive degassing. The calculated sedimentation rates of these carbonate precipitates range from 1 to 6 mm year-1 (occasionally reaching 2 cm/year), which is significantly high. The sedimentation rate is not uniform and depends on both extrinsic (wind directions, rain, intermittent cooling operations) and intrinsic physico-chemical parameters of flowing water. For the study of travertine depositional processes, the geothermal cooling towers of southern Tunisia, which can be assimilated to large-scale water softeners to make it suitable for human uses, represent reliable artificial counterparts of natural travertine-depositing systems (waterfalls, terraced slopes, and pools).

title: A segmented surrogate model for THMC responses in the near-wellbore zone of super-long gravity heat pipes
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Wanli Wang, Honglei Shi, Guiling Wang, Fangming Jiang, Wei Zhang, Linxiao Xing, Wenbo Huang, Lu Liu, Chuan Lu
abstract: The super-long gravity heat pipe, as an emerging technology for deep geothermal exploitation, has attracted considerable attention owing to its "pumpless" heat extraction feature. The heat extraction process involves complex coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical (THMC) Multiphysics processes in the near-wellbore region. Constrained by the extremely large length-to-diameter ratio of the heat pipe and the need for detailed characterization of near-wellbore fractures, conventional simulation methods face inherent trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency. To address this challenge, this study proposes a segmented THMC coupled modeling strategy that captures the dynamic evolution of fracture aperture under coupled thermal, mechanical, and chemical effects. A deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model is further developed based on high-fidelity numerical simulations to accelerate calculation. The proposed method achieves high accuracy with an overall MAE of 2.786 W/m and R² of 0.998 against numerical benchmarks. The DNN surrogate reduces computation time from 847 min to 98 min, representing an 88% reduction. Field validation against the Xiong'an 4200 m gravity heat pipe test yields an average relative error of 6.11%, confirming the model's practical applicability. By synergistically integrating segmented modeling, THMC coupling with dynamic fracture aperture evolution, and DNN-based acceleration, this work provides a high-fidelity and computationally efficient solution for refined numerical simulations in deep geothermal exploitation.

title: Optimization of time-window selection in the Epidemic-Type aftershock sequence analysis for accurate estimation of fluid-related reservoir variations in geothermal development
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Naoki Aoyagi, Kyosuke Okamoto, Yusuke Mukuhira, Hiroshi Asanuma
abstract: Microseismic monitoring is one of the practical methods for indirectly tracking fluid migration within reservoirs with high temporal resolution in near real time. In geothermal fields, the background seismicity rate μ of the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model can be interpreted as fluid-induced seismicity, and its temporal variation may provide useful information for reservoir monitoring and operational management. Temporal ETAS analysis using moving time windows is therefore expected to support more accurate and timely geothermal operations and may contribute to traffic light systems based on seismic activity. However, when the number of events extracted from the catalog is limited, ETAS parameter estimates may become unstable and deviate from true values. In this study, we investigated the effects of event number and time window length on ETAS parameter estimation using synthetic catalogs based on the ETAS model of the Okuaizu geothermal field, Japan. The results show that the number of events within a time window is sufficient (e.g., ≥ 100 events) and the event occurrence rate within the time window (event density) is comparable to or lower than that of the full catalog and is not excessively low, estimates of μ remain within the confidence interval derived from the standard deviation under the 8000 event condition, which is close to the total number of events in the full catalog. These results indicate that appropriate control of the number of events within a time window and event density is essential for reliable temporal ETAS analysis using moving time windows in geothermal fields.

title: Spatiotemporal characterization of a ground heat exchanger (GHE) operating in partially saturated clay formation
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Aditya Deshmukh, Anand J. Puppala, Alireza Fakhrabadi, Puneet Bhaskar, Xinbao Yu, Hiramani Chimauriya
abstract: One of the key challenges in shallow geothermal technology is improving the thermal performance of ground heat exchangers (GHEs) while reducing operational costs. Existing enhancement techniques are typically applied uniformly along the GHE depth, despite field data showing non-uniform thermal performance. This paper presents a spatiotemporal characterization of a single u-pipe GHE, consolidating theoretical framework, laboratory characterization, and numerical modeling to identify where and when coupled heat and moisture transfer becomes significant within the GHE geometry. The coupled model is validated against a laboratory column test under ambient, and non-insulated boundary conditions and applied to characterize the three-dimensional axial and radial extent of soil drying and wetting around a GHE operating in heat rejection mode. Results reveal an asymmetric temperature and moisture distribution, with greater desaturation near the inlet leg, concentrated in the upper 40–50% of the GHE depth and extending 1.21 m - 1.52 m (4 - 5 ft) radially from the pipe. This desaturation is self-limiting, stabilizing within one to two months of operation, and corresponds to an approximately fivefold increase in matric suction near the pipe, from approximately 348 kPa (7268.13 psf) to approximately 1851 kPa (38,658.94 psf) over four months. The associated reduction in thermal conductivity and heat capacity substantially alters the heat exchange capacity of the surrounding soil. These findings establish the spatiotemporal basis for future design and operational strategies, such as targeted use of high-conductivity materials near the GHE inlet and periodic flow reversal, to improve the cost-effectiveness of shallow geothermal systems.

title: Coaxial tube heat exchangers for medium-deep geothermal utilization: numerical analysis and layout optimization
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Jianling Ye, Chicheng He, Yaowen Cao, Gang Liu, Lei Shi, Jiajun Chen, Tian Zhou
abstract: Medium-deep geothermal energy resources have been extensively researched all over the world owing to their environmental friendliness, large reserves and renewability. However, the lack of field experimental data remains a major obstacle to model validation and engineering application. Based on field measurements, a model for a single well of a medium-deep coaxial tube heat exchanger (MDCTHE) was established in this study via the application of the finite element method. The impacts of key parameters, including fluid inlet temperature, volumetric flow rate, and thermal conductivity, on thermal performance were systematically investigated. Simulation results reveal that as the inlet temperature rises from 14 °C to 44 °C, the heat transfer capacity significantly drops by 74.6% (from 603.52 kW to 153.28 kW) due to the diminished thermal driving force. Conversely, while increasing the inlet volumetric flow rate reduces fluid residence time, the enhanced convective heat transfer coefficient dominates, leading to a net increase in total heat extraction. Meanwhile, a multi-well pipe group heat transfer model was constructed using the MDCTHE simulation data, and the impact of drilling layout on system efficiency was then examined. This study establishes a theoretical and practical basis for promoting the production and use of renewable energy, and provides the empirical evidence and the theoretical framework necessary for the engineering design and the developmental research of medium-deep geothermal resources.

title: Unveiling a hidden upflow in the Nagasari Area, Dieng geothermal field, Indonesia: Fluid geochemical constraints
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Aditya Yuda Kencana, Niniek Rina Herdianita
abstract: The Dieng Geothermal Field in Central Java, Indonesia, is a high-temperature volcanic geothermal system hosted within the Quaternary Dieng Volcanic Complex. Previous conceptual models interpreted the Nagasari area as an outflow zone fed laterally from the Sileri reservoir. However, recent drilling of wells NGS-1 and NGS-2 toward Mount Nagasari encountered unexpectedly high subsurface temperatures (up to 347 °C), more characteristic of an upflow zone. This study integrates water chemistry, gas composition, stable isotopes, and pressure-temperature data from 14 wells to test the hypothesis of a previously unrecognized upflow at Nagasari and to refine the conceptual model of the Sileri-Nagasari sector. Reservoir fluids are benign, neutral-pH chloride brines with temperatures of 290–345 °C, high chloride concentrations (4000 - 15,000 mg/kg), and low total non-condensable gases (<1 wt%). Stable isotope signatures show significant δ¹⁸O enrichment (6.6–9.1‰) relative to the local meteoric water line, indicating intensive water-rock interaction at high temperature. Conservative element ratios (Cl-Li-B) confirm that fluids from Sileri, Merdada, and Nagasari share a common deep reservoir. Spatial distribution of geochemical indicators, low Na/K and CO₂/H₂, high CO₂/H₂S, gas/steam, and total NCG, delineates three distinct upflow zones beneath Mount Nagasari, Pagerkandang, and Merdada, coinciding spatially with post-caldera I eruption centers (0.46 - 0.37 Ma). Fluids ascend along these upflow zones and flow laterally toward the west, north, northeast, and the central area between them. The integration of fluid geochemistry and subsurface temperature data supports reinterpretation of the Nagasari area as an independent upflow center rather than a marginal outflow. This finding demonstrates that caldera-hosted geothermal systems with protracted post-caldera volcanism can develop multiple, coeval upflow zones corresponding to discrete eruption centers. The developed conceptual model provides a solid foundation for future drilling targeting and resource assessment in the Dieng Geothermal Field and in providing wider views of fluid circulation regimes in volcanic geothermal systems.

title: Multi-objective optimization of groundwater heat pump system integrated with thermal recharge tower in severe cold zone
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Xing Sheng, Kailiang Huang, Yu Zhao, Guohui Feng, Jiaxing Wei, Qihai Sun
abstract: Groundwater-source heat pump (GWHP) systems in severe-cold regions are vulnerable to long-term aquifer thermal imbalance, whereas existing thermal-recharge-tower (TRT) studies remain largely deterministic and component-oriented. This study developed a system-level, surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization framework for a GWHP integrated with an air-to-water TRT. Multi-year field data defined the source-temperature input, model-validity range, and physically admissible decision-variable bounds, and a validated TRNSYS model provided high-fidelity response data. A joint PSO-MSVR surrogate, developed from 255 cases and blind-tested on an independent 90-case set, was coupled with NSGA-II, global Sobol sensitivity analysis, bootstrap-based conservative treatment of surrogate prediction uncertainty, and entropy-weighted TOPSIS. All four surrogate outputs achieved R² > 0.97 and NRMSE < 5%. The representative TOPSIS compromise, re-evaluated by the full annual TRNSYS model, yielded an annual system CO P ann of 4.28 (21.3% improvement), 3,985 MWh of thermal recharge (1.55% below the engineering benchmark), a 15-year life-cycle cost of 279.9 × 10⁴ RMB (6.2% reduction), and a load-weighted grid carbon intensity ( LWCI ) of 0.460 kg CO₂/kWh (7.6% reduction). The framework therefore combines physics-based modeling, independently validated surrogate search, sensitivity analysis, and high-fidelity engineering verification in a reproducible workflow for heating-dominated GWHP-TRT systems.

title: Chemical characteristics of the Bandaiko hyper-acidic hot spring in Kusatsu Town, Gunma prefecture, and evaluation test of scale for binary power generation
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Geothermics, Volume 143 Author(s): Mio Ichino, Toshio Inoue, Yuka Kubotsu, Hideo Takizawa, Yukiko Hoshino, Daisuke Tanaka, Akira Ueda, Hideki Kuramitz
abstract: The Bandaiko hot spring, located in Kusatsu Town, Gunma Prefecture, is characterized by its hyper-acidic nature with a pH level of 1.7 and remarkable flow rate of approximately nine tons per minute. Gunma Prefecture is exploring the possibility of modifying its existing heat exchange system to establish a binary power generation facility utilizing this hyper-acidic hot spring, marking a potential first in the world. However, in the existing heat exchange facility, scale accumulation of the current facility necessitates water washing roughly once a month, but the type of scale and the rate of accumulation rate are still unknown. To address this, hot spring water was sampled and chemically analyzed, and field tests simulating scale adhesion were conducted using this water. For evaluation, quartz glass coupons and a batch-type scale sensor were utilized. The accumulated scale was identified as elemental sulfur. The use of quartz glass coupons did not enable an assessment of the scale deposition rate based on weight changes. By contrast, an 18-d immersion test with batch-type scale sensor indicated a gradual decrease in transmittance over time. The decrease in this sensor's transmittance serves as a proxy indicator for material accumulation under static immersion conditions. As it is not possible to analyze the scale adhering to the titanium heat exchanger during operation, it does not directly indicate the rate of scale deposition. Analysis of deposits on the sensor surface and scale recovered during the water washing of the heat exchanger revealed that the scale was elemental sulfur.
