title: Hydrogen in nominally anhydrous minerals from equilibrated ordinary chondrites and implications for the water budget of their parent bodies
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): S. Desikamani, L.D. Peterson, M.E. Newcombe, C.M.O’D. Alexander, J. Wang, R.D. Ash, S.G. Nielsen, P.M. Piccoli, E.S. Bullock
abstract: Nucleosynthetic isotope signatures indicate that the Earth is predominantly made from inner solar system non-carbonaceous (NC) materials. However, a major uncertainty in models of water addition to the proto-Earth is the extent to which H (calculated in this study as µg/g H2O, but present as H-bearing species) in nominally anhydrous minerals (NAMs) from NC materials could contribute to the bulk Earth water budget. The preserved water concentration of NC meteorite NAMs may also shape our understanding of processes occurring in the solar protoplanetary disk (e.g., implantation of H on the surfaces of NAM grains) and in planetesimals (e.g., metamorphism in chondrite parent bodies). Reported water contents for NAMs from the ordinary chondrites (OCs), the dominant NC material falling to Earth today, range between 100-104 µg/g H2O. In order to better constrain the potential contribution of ordinary chondrites to the Earth’s water budget we have measured water concentrations in NAMs from eight equilibrated OCs, six of which have not previously been investigated for water, and two of which (Chelyabinsk and Bensour) were previously measured in other laboratories. We find that olivine and low-Ca pyroxene from equilibrated OCs contain less than ∼10 µg/g H2O. Based on these measurements, the water content of the NAM fraction of equilibrated OCs is < 10 µg/g H2O (a factor of over 60–120 lower than prior estimates). Combining these constraints of equilibrated OC NAM water contents with published measurements of NAMs and glassy mesostases from unequilibrated OCs, we estimate that NAMs and glass in OC parent bodies could have delivered no more than ∼0.2 ocean masses of water to Earth (∼1% of an assumed total water budget of ∼18 ocean masses). Additional water could have been delivered from phyllosilicates and organics in the most primitive OC material that is not considered in our modeling. The difference in NAM water concentrations obtained here relative to some prior studies may be rooted in analytical artifacts associated with their nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrometric measurements.

title: Shock-induced hydrogen-isotope modification in apatite from the Martian meteorite Los Angeles
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): E. Dobrică, J.P. Greenwood, A.N. Krot, A.J. Brearley, E.P. Vicenzi, S. Itoh, N. Sakamoto, H. Yurimoto
abstract: Hydrogen isotopes in apatite are widely used to constrain the origin and evolution of water in Martian magmas and crustal reservoirs. However, the extent to which shock metamorphism modifies hydrogen-isotope compositions in apatites is poorly understood. In this study, we combine scanning electron microscopy (SEM), cathodoluminescence (CL), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) observations, and secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) measurements of hydrogen isotopes and water contents in apatites from the Martian meteorite Los Angeles. Panchromatic CL imaging reveals distinct bright and dark domains within individual apatite grains. These domains correlate with variations in hydrogen-isotope composition, chlorine abundance, and shock metamorphic microstructures (dislocations, planar fractures, and shock-induced melting) observed at the nanoscale. Bright CL regions show higher defect densities, more abundant melt pockets, lower chlorine contents, and elevated δD values relative to dark CL regions. Defect density correlates positively with δD and melt pocket abundance but shows no systematic relationship with bulk H2O content. These observations demonstrate that hydrogen-isotope modification can occur in heavily deformed apatite without requiring complete melting or recrystallization. Shock-induced defects therefore provide pathways for hydrogen redistribution and isotopic exchange at the micron scale. The results indicate that shock metamorphism can locally modify primary hydrogen isotope signatures in Martian meteorites while preserving bulk water contents within the typical Martian apatite range. Cathodoluminescence imaging provides a rapid and non-destructive method for identifying apatite domains that can correlate with deformation-enhanced and isotopically-modified regions. These findings have important implications for interpreting Martian volatile reservoirs and for future sample-return missions such as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX).

title: Origin of nucleosynthetic isotope variability in the NC reservoir: Evidence from Ti, Cr, and Mo isotopes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Elias Wölfer, Christoph Burkhardt, Gerrit Budde, Christian A. Jansen, Jonas Pape, Thorsten Kleine
abstract: Nucleosynthetic isotope anomalies allow distinguishing between non-carbonaceous (NC) and carbonaceous (CC) type meteorites, and have revealed correlated isotope variations especially among NC bodies. Understanding the origin of this NC trend is important for identifying the processes that produced the NC isotope heterogeneity, and for using these isotope anomalies to reconstruct the early evolution of the solar protoplanetary disk. We report mass-independent Ti, Cr, and Mo isotope compositions for a comprehensive set of previously not or only poorly investigated meteorites, as well as acid leachates obtained from the sequential digestion of primitive ordinary chondrites. Some of the samples investigated in this study fill previously identified apparent gaps in the NC trend, suggesting these gaps reflect unrepresentative sampling of a more continuous isotopic trend. Bulk meteorites and leachates exhibit distinct isotope systematics, indicating that the NC isotope variability does not reflect selective thermal processing of presolar carriers in the disk. The NC trend also cannot reflect the continuous addition of CC dust from the outer to the inner disk, because early- and late-formed NC meteorites display largely overlapping isotopic compositions. Instead, we find that the NC isotope heterogeneity is best accounted for by fractionation and mixing among chemically and isotopically distinct dust components, similar to the processes that produced the isotopic variability among carbonaceous chondrites. On this basis we argue for the presence of substructures in the inner disk, which facilitated fractionation and mixing among distinct dust components, and helped preserve a long-lived dust reservoir from which NC planetesimals accreted over an extended period of time.

title: Fluorine and chlorine abundances in carbonatite melts and implications for REE-enrichment
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Haihao Guo, Fabrice Gaillard, Saskia Erdmann, Zineb Nabyl, Johann Tuduri, Xiaochun Li
abstract: Carbonatites are enriched in halogens and S, and can host rare earth element (REE) and high field strength element (HFSE, e.g., Nb, Zr) deposits. Yet, the role of volatiles like fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), and sulfur (S) in the fractionation of the carbonatite magmas and in the enrichment of their metals remain underexplored. Here, we use previously published experimental data (1) on F, Cl, S and REE partitioning between apatite and carbonatite melt; (2) use the composition of apatite from natural carbonatites to characterize the F, Cl and S contents in the coexisting melts; and (3) weigh the role of F in driving REE enrichment during carbonatite magma differentiation. In combination with previous studies, we show that the partitioning coefficients of fluorine, chlorine, and sulfur between apatite and carbonatite melt are respectively DF = 0.97 ± 0.36; DCl = 0.14 ± 0.11; and DS = 0.031 ± 0.012, across a wide range of pressures (200–800 MPa) and temperatures (725–1050 °C) and for a range of carbonatite melt compositions. Furthermore, our findings indicate no significant influence of melt F, Cl, and S concentration on the partitioning of REE between apatite and carbonatite melt. Using these partitioning constraints combined with > 700 magmatic apatite compositions from carbonatites, we estimate an average of ∼3.1 ± 1.3 wt% F and ∼0.30 ± 0.31 wt% Cl in carbonatite melts, and show that F-rich carbonatite melts do not necessarily have higher REE concentrations. Sufficient compositional data for natural apatite from carbonatites that permit a quantitative assessment of the effect of melt Cl and S concentrations on REE fractionation do not exist. We therefore posit that the degree of REE enrichment in carbonatite rocks is not primarily controlled by melt F concentrations, but may be inherited from the lithospheric mantle sources, can result from immiscibility of variably differentiated alkaline magmas, or involve concentration by hydrothermal fluids.

title: Sedimentary constraints on pelagic iron removal across the low-latitude Pacific
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Zheyuan Zhang, Jianfan Zheng, Xuefa Shi, Weiqiang Li, Yanguang Liu, Jiahui Liu, Zhimian Cao, Tao Li, Tianyu Chen
abstract: Iron (Fe) is a crucial micronutrient that limits primary production over broad regions of the global ocean. While the external Fe inputs to the ocean have been increasingly constrained, the quantitative removal flux of Fe from the water column to the pelagic sediments remains incompletely understood, particularly in the open ocean. The low-latitude Pacific encompasses diverse hydrographic and sedimentary environments, making it a representative region for tracing Fe removal from the deep ocean. In this study, we performed Fe speciation, Fe isotope and burial flux analyses using near core-top sediments from multiple sediment cores recovered across the low-latitude Pacific, partly overlapping with the GEOTRACES GP16 transect. Our results show these sediments could effectively record Fe inputs from the Peru margin, hydrothermal vents, and Asian dust. Specifically, we identified differing Fe speciation, Fe and manganese (Mn) flux as well as δ56Fe of both reactive Fe and bulk sediment that are related to the different sedimentary provinces. In the low-latitude Pacific, δ56Fe of the acid leached reactive Fe species agree well with those of the labile particulate Fe species within the water column of the GP16 transect and the core-top hydrogenic ferromanganese crusts, suggesting the reactive Fe of these sediments represents the sink of the dissolved Fe pool in the deep ocean. Manganese essentially associates with the reactive fraction and shows highly positive correlation with reactive Fe content. Within the east region influenced by hydrothermal venting originating from the Eastern Pacific Rise (EPR), the proportion of reactive Fe oxides is higher, reaching up to 53%. The reactive δ56Fe in this region is as low as −0.5‰, implying a light Fe isotope signature from the hydrothermal endmember and consistent with modern water column studies. Sediment samples outside this hydrothermal zone show “background” Fe sedimentation flux and isotope signatures, pointing toward the influence of non-reductive dissolution from the West Pacific arcs/Asian dust and reductive dissolution from Peru margin. The scavenging residence time of dissolved Fe in the water column estimated by the reactive Fe burial flux in this region is only a few years to a few decades, indicating rapid turnover of Fe in the open ocean. Our study thus offers novel insights into the oceanic Fe sources-sink processes and could help improve biogeochemical models toward a better representation of the oceanic Fe cycle.

title: Lithium and calcium isotopes in various shallow-water carbonates: Disentangling the effects of mineralogy, vital effects, and early diagenesis
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Guang-Yi Wei, Simon V. Hohl, Jack G. Murphy, Ashley N. Martin, Yi-Sheng Yin, Zhuang Xiao, Xiaobin Cao, Hong-Fei Ling
abstract: The isotopic composition of metals in marine carbonates provides a powerful archive of past seawater chemistry, yet these primary signals can be modified by diagenetic alteration and vital effects associated with biomineralization in biogenic carbonates. This study investigates the behaviors of calcium (δ 44/40Ca) and lithium (δ7Li) isotopes across a diverse set of shallow-marine carbonate systems, including microbialites from Hamelin Pool in Shark Bay, Western Australia, and bulk carbonate sediments and biogenic corals from the Nansha Islands, South China Sea, to evaluate how depositional conditions, mineralogy, and early diagenesis govern their isotopic compositions. The microbialites exhibit low average values of δ 44/40Ca (–1.22 ± 0.23‰, 2σ, n = 8) and δ7Li (+21.1 ± 3.5‰, 2σ, n = 8), with their offsets from modern seawater values (δ 44/40CaSW = 0‰; δ7LiSW ≈ 31‰) primarily controlled by carbonate mineralogy. A positive correlation between δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li within different individual microbialites is also identified, which is not regulated by vital effects, salinity, or basin restriction, but likely reflects the modest diagenetic alteration of primary metastable aragonites. Compared with microbialites, bulk carbonate sediments show elevated average values of δ 44/40Ca (–1.09 ± 0.22‰, 2σ, n = 23) and δ7Li (+24.0 ± 1.3‰, 2σ, n = 30), indicating mixing of primary aragonite and high-Mg calcite in these sediments. In contrast, the shallow-water corals exhibit higher average δ 44/40Ca values (–1.02 ± 0.14‰, 2σ, n = 4) and lower δ7Li values (+18.0 ± 0.9‰, 2σ, n = 4), which we interpret as the influence of vital effects associated with isotopic fractionations during transmembrane transport of cations between seawater and the calcifying fluid for coral biomineralization. The agreement of δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li data from this study with published shallow-water carbonate records suggests that the isotopic compositions of primary carbonate sediments are predominantly controlled by carbonate mineralogy, while additional processes, particularly vital effects in biogenic carbonates and early diagenetic alteration in carbonate sediments, can further influence these isotopic signatures. This underscores the need to account for carbonate mineralogy, vital effects, and diagenetic alteration when reconstructing coeval seawater signals from ancient carbonates, which can be done using multi-proxy isotope datasets and a modeling framework. Further, when carbonate mineralogy and diagenesis are well constrained, microbialites may be used to reliably reconstruct δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li signatures of Precambrian seawater, as their isotopic signatures are largely insensitive to salinity, basin restriction, and vital effects.

title: Riverine Li isotopes response to a flood event on the Chinese Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Jianqi Man, Long-Fei Gou, Zheng Chen, Wenqi Zhang, Jiayuan Ren, Zhiyuan Zhao, Chengfan Yang, Haoqiang Dong, Chenyuan Kang, Jun Xiao, Zhi-Qi Zhao, Zhenhong Li, Zhangdong Jin
abstract: Silicate weathering is essential to supply nutrients from land to ocean and to sustain the long-term habitability of our planet via consumption of atmospheric CO2. Riverine Li isotopes (δ7Liriv) are proposed a promising silicate weathering tracer. However, how silicate weathering and riverine Li isotopes respond to an extreme hydrological event has rarely been investigated. Owing to homogeneous geochemical compositions, loess provides a unique setting to understand how riverine Li isotopes trace silicate weathering under an extreme hydrological event. Here, we collected and analyzed river water samples within the Beiluo River catchment that fully covered by loess in the dry and wet seasons, in order to capture the response of silicate weathering to a flood event that accounting 1/5 annual runoff in 9 days. The results showed that δ7Liriv values have distinct seasonality between the regular dry and wet seasons and the flood event. In the regular dry and wet seasons, δ7Liriv values were controlled by two processes: 1) mixing between groundwater and silicate weathering in the upper stream, and 2) Rayleigh fractionation processes caused by loess weathering in the middle-lower reaches. In contrast, mixing between extruded porewater and groundwater controlled the δ7Liriv values throughout the flood event. Our findings provides new clues into silicate weathering processes and the response of δ7Liriv to extreme hydrological events.

title: Structurally controlled Mg isotope fractionation between talc and fluid: implications for the oceanic and mantle Mg cycle
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Chuan Liu, Zhiguang Xia, Shichao An, Weiqiang Li
abstract: Talc and structurally related Mg-phyllosilicates are ubiquitous products of hydrothermal alteration and metamorphism, and play an important role in the global magnesium cycle. However, their Mg isotope fractionation behavior remains poorly constrained, and previous studies on Mg-bearing layered minerals have yielded apparently conflicting results. Here we present the first experimental determination of Mg isotope fractionation between talc and aqueous fluids under hydrothermal conditions (130-188°C). Our closed-system experiments demonstrate that talc preferentially incorporates heavy Mg isotopes relative to coexisting fluid, with Δ26Mgtalc-soln increasing from values + 0.12‰ at early stages to ∼+0.80‰ as reaction proceeds. This temporal evolution correlates with structural maturation of talc, indicating that crystallographic ordering and progressive stiffening of Mg-O bonds are primary controls on isotope partitioning. This finding provides a unifying mechanism to reconcile discrepancies in published fractionation factors for other Mg-bearing layered minerals (e.g., smectite, brucite), suggesting that the variability in natural and experimental data likely reflects different degrees of structural ripening. More broadly, our experiments provide an experimental reference for Mg-phyllosilicates and highlight the sensitivity of the marine Mg-silicate sink to mineral identity and structural maturity. In subduction-zone settings, talc-forming reactions may generate heavy-Mg signatures in talc-bearing metasomatic lithologies at the slab-mantle interface, and these signatures may be retained and redistributed during subsequent talc breakdown, fluid-rock interaction and metamorphic replacement.

title: Submicron-scale mineral weathering and organo-mineral association in the rhizosphere of iron ore tailings
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Zhen Li, Songlin Wu, Ting-Shan Chan, Cheng-Wei Kao, Jian Wang, Gordon Southam, Longbin Huang
abstract: Rhizosphere-driven mineral weathering plays a critical role in generating reactive minerals that stabilize organic matter (OM) and support the development of soil structure and biogeochemical functions in iron (Fe) ore tailings. However, the formation and evolution of organo-mineral association at submicron scale, and the extent to which particle size and tailings aging influence these associations remain poorly understood. The present study investigated how pioneer plant roots influence mineral weathering, reactive mineral formation, and stabilization of OM at submicron scale. Root colonization induced acidification and accelerated the weathering of Fe-K-rich mica (i.e. biotite) in tailings, leading to the formation of reactive phases, including vermiculite, short-range-ordered Fe-Si phases, and goethite. These transformations were mediated by particle size: coarse fractions (> 53 µm) promoted vermiculite neoformation, whereas fine fractions (< 53 µm) favored Fe oxyhydroxide formation. Synchrotron-based scanning-transmission X-ray microscopy with near-edge X-ray absorption-fine-structure-spectroscopy (STXM-NEXAFS) analysis further revealed that in original tailings, root-derived compounds, rich in aromatic, carboxyl, and phenolic groups, were heterogeneously associated with mixed-valence Fe-bearing minerals. In contrast, aged tailings predominantly stabilized aromatic, carboxyl, and aliphatic-rich organics on Fe(III)-bearing minerals. Collectively, these findings provide direct evidence for a previously unrecognized, in-situ coupled process in which root-induced weathering of primary minerals and the concurrent formation of reactive secondary mineral phases were associated with the stabilization of root-derived OM. In addition, tailings’ mineral particle size and aging governs both weathering pathways and subsequent OM stabilization patterns. This rhizosphere driven “Weathering-Organo-Mineral” interaction advances mechanistic understanding of rhizosphere mediated mineral weathering and organo-mineral interactions in Fe ore tailings, with important implications for sustainable eco-engineered pedogenesis.

title: Uranium isotopic constraints on the biogeochemistry of methane-seep environments
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Xiaoming Miao, Jingrui Li, Xiting Liu, Xuexue Jia, Hangyu Nan, Zhiwei He, Jiangtao Li, Hongxiang Guan, Thomas J. Algeo
abstract: Methane seepage alters local diagenetic conditions, influencing the coupled biogeochemical cycles of sulfur, carbon, and redox-sensitive elements such as uranium (U) in the sediment. This study investigates the U-isotopic compositions of carbonate-rich sediments and seep carbonates (Site ROV1-5A) in the Haima Cold Seep of the South China Sea and of non-seep marine sediments (sites DS12 and DS388). Terrigenous debris dominates U sources in non-seep marine sediments (δ234U, –27‰ to +26‰; U/Al, 0.17 mg/kg/wt.%), consistent with upper continental crustal (UCC) signatures. In contrast, seep carbonates (δ234U, +105‰ to +135‰; U/Al, 4.3 mg/kg/wt.%) and carbonate-rich sediments (δ234U, +38‰ to +107‰; U/Al, 1.3 mg/kg/wt.%) exhibit elevated δ234U values and U/Al ratios, indicating authigenic U enrichment. Positive correlations between U and carbonate contents suggest that carbonate is the main sedimentary host of authigenic U in methane-seep environments. In comparison to the UCC and non-seep marine sediments (average δ238U = –0.27‰), carbonate-rich sediments exhibit 238U enrichment (–0.16‰ to +0.01‰) and seep carbonates 238U depletion (–0.45‰ to –0.32‰). Seep carbonates, which lack pyrite and exhibit moderately elevated (Mo/U) values (average 1.9), form under anoxic, non-sulfidic conditions. In contrast, carbonate-rich sediments, which are rich in pyrite and exhibit high (Mo/U) values (average 7.6), form under sulfidic conditions. We infer that the alteration of the redox environment resulting from anaerobic oxidation of methane and the abiotic reduction of U(VI) driven by Fe(II) are the primary factors responsible for the observed differences in δ238U. Our results indicate that U isotopes are a sensitive proxy for local redox conditions in seep environments. The observed isotopic shifts provide insights into how methane seepage, through processes like AOM and associated redox changes, orchestrates the coupling of multi-elemental cycles and oceanic redox changes.

title: The hydrogen isotopic composition and content of the ureilite parent body: constraints from new ungrouped achondrites
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): B.G. Rider-Stokes, A. Stephant, M. Nottingham, J. Gamblin, E. Füri, S.S. Russell, X. Zhao, M. Anand, M.J. Whitehouse, M.M. Grady
abstract: Evidence for SiO2-rich melts on the ureilite parent body (UPB) stems from feldspathic clasts within polymict ureilites and has been additionally preserved and recorded in rare fragments of the Almahata Sitta meteorite suite, which originated from the asteroid 2008 TC3. These unique fragments demonstrated that ancient crust-forming volcanism on small planetary bodies was not simply restricted to basaltic lithologies. Two recent Northwest Africa finds (NWA) 15,820 and NWA 16789 expand the known quantity of SiO2-rich material from the UPB, allowing for a more representative investigation into the chemical and isotopic variations among these unique lithologies. Here, we measured the H abundance and isotopic composition (δD) of NWA 15820 and NWA 16789 to evaluate the bulk UPB water content, resulting in a revised minimum bulk water content of 13 µg/g H2O. Furthermore, we report the δD of water in the UPB. While the D/H ratio of late-stage phosphates and glass is highly fractionated as a result of magmatic degassing, nominally anhydrous silicate pyroxene better records the original δD of the UPB. In particular, the pyroxene within NWA 16789 records a δD value of 83 ± 79‰, which we infer is the best estimate for the original δD of water in the UPB.

title: Evaporation kinetics of forsterite in H 2 -H 2 O gas mixtures
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Shiori Inada, Shogo Tachibana
abstract: Effects of ambient gas are important for understanding evaporation of planetary materials in the protosolar disk. In this study, we experimentally investigated the evaporation kinetics of forsterite in H2-H2O gas mixtures to elucidate the dependences on H2O abundance at P H 2 O / P H 2 of 10−4–10−2, temperatures of 1400–1600 K, and a total pressure of 1 Pa. We found that the evaporation rate decreases with increasing P H 2 O / P H 2 with a reaction order of −1.02 ± 0.12 only above certain P H 2 O / P H 2 (10−3–10−2 depending on temperature). The activation energy increased when the evaporation is suppressed by H2O (497 ± 11 kJ mol−1, while 359 ± 1 kJ mol−1 without the effect of H2O). The P H 2 O / P H 2 dependence of the evaporation rate is consistent with the previously proposed model based on the chemical equilibrium consideration and the Hertz-Knudsen equation. This consistency can be explained in terms of a reaction mechanism. Based on the experimentally determined evaporation kinetics, we evaluated conditions of the protosolar disk where H2O affects evaporation of forsterite dust. This showed that H2O suppresses the evaporation at ≲ 1300 K at P H 2 O / P H 2 of the Solar abundance and ≲ 1600 K under H2O-enriched conditions, which possibly affected moderate-temperature thermal processing of silicate dust and evaporation of chondrule melt under oxidizing conditions.

title: Iron isotopes reveal colloidal release as the dominant sedimentary flux from oxic inner continental shelf
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Liqin Duan, Xiaoqi Liu, Jinming Song, Jiawei Kan, Dongyong Li, Xuegang Li, Huamao Yuan
abstract: Continental shelf and estuarine sediments are critical carbon sinks and significant sources of dissolved iron (dFe). Although the mechanism of Fe reductive dissolution (RD) under low-oxygen conditions is well documented, the processes governing Fe dissolution and supply in oxic sediments remain poorly understood. Here, we combine porewater colloidal Fe (cFe; 0.02–0.2 μm) and the δ56Fe signatures of dFe in China’s largest estuary to reveal distinct dFe speciation patterns. Nearshore oxic-nitrogenous porewaters are dominated by cFe with near-crustal δ56Fe of dFe (∼0‰), whereas porewaters in ferruginous zones of all sites and offshore hypoxic zones are dominated by soluble Fe (sFe, 60% of benthic dFe fluxes and exhibit a positive correlation with bottom-water DO, revealing NRD-generated cFe as the primary dFe source under oxic conditions. Our findings indicate that NRD may be an important mechanism for dFe supply in young, terrestrial-influenced coastal sediments, a pathway that is potentially underrepresented in current oceanic Fe cycle models.

title: Sulfur speciation in silicate melts under varying pressure and redox conditions from first-principles simulations
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Bijaya B. Karki, Yishen Zhang, Rajdeep Dasgupta
abstract: Sulfur (S) in silicate melts exhibits complex behavior as a function of the oxygen fugacity and pressure, and its speciation and dissolution mechanisms are not fully understood. Here we report the results of first-principles molecular dynamics simulations of S-bearing MgSiO3 melts in the pressure range from ∼0 GPa (2000 K) to ∼17 GPa (3000 K) under varying redox conditions as imposed by adjusting the number of oxygen atoms in the supercell relative to sulfur-free composition ( Δ n O ) from 4.2 to −12.5 % (used as redox state proxy). The simulation results and analysis show that sulfur forms dimer ( S 2 ), trimer ( S 3 ), and S O 1 , 2 , 3 radicals, which tend to loosely bind with the cations in the oxidized melts for Δ n O ≥ 0 . However, sulfur dissolves predominantly as sulfide ( S 2 - ) complexes by bonding with cations, preferably Mg 2 + over Si 4 + in the reduced melts with oxygen deficiency ( Δ n O < 0 ). The calculated relative proportions of various sulfur-bearing species are strongly dependent on temperature and pressure. When the sulfur content of the melt is varied from 2.0 to 11.3 wt% under more reducing conditions corresponding to Δ n O = - 2.1 t o - 12.5 % , we find that sulfur shows weak or no self-interactions and instead exclusively bonds with cations. This suggests that several wt.% of sulfur can dissolve in silicate melts as sulfide complexes under highly reducing conditions and the dissolved sulfur tends to suppress the melt’s density and oxide activities. These findings are expected to have significant implications for melt transport and phase relations during magmatic differentiation of sulfur-rich, silicate reservoirs in highly reduced planets, such as Mercury and exo-Mercuries.

title: Chondrule formation in the outer disk from the primary three-dimensional chemical composition of CM chondrules
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Poula Eyðbjørnsdóttir, Anders Johansen, Elishevah van Kooten
abstract: Chondrules and their associated fine-grained rims (FGRs) record fundamental processes operating in the early protoplanetary disk, yet the relationship between chondrule chemistry, morphology, and matrix complementarity remains incompletely understood. Here we investigate the major, minor, and trace element compositions of 66 chondrules and associated FGRs from relatively unaltered CM carbonaceous chondrites Asuka 12236, Paris and Maribo in relation to their three-dimensional morphology, using a multi-analytical approach including femtosecond LA-ICP-MS and X-ray tomography. Our results show that CM chondrules record a systematic process of metal loss and evaporation of Si-rich mesostasis, driving initially CI-like precursor compositions toward more Mg- and Si-rich bulk compositions along the CI ratio line and toward increasingly Si-poor forsteritic mineral assemblages. GEMS-like materials in pristine CM matrices appear to mirror chondrule compositions and likely represent complementary condensates derived from evaporated Si-rich mesostasis. The dust accreted to chondrules is dominantly CI-like but incorporates ∼14 wt% complementary condensate material represented by chondritic amorphous silicates, reconciling the observed Mg/Si complementarity between chondrules and matrix with the preservation of primordial organics and presolar grains. Morphological observations further reveal no significant sectioning bias in chondrule size or plane, consistent with CM chondrule populations being dominated by agglomerates of ∼100 μm sized microspherules rather than larger primary melt droplets. Many chondrules display grape-bunch textures formed by welding of smaller primary chondrules with metal-rich or CI-like rims. This structure may explain the moderate volatile element plateau at ∼0.3 × CI observed for average CM chondrule compositions, reflecting incorporation of primary fine-grained rim material into these aggregates. We propose a “micro-chondrule-first” formation scenario in which localized heating events produced small molten droplets that subsequently accreted CI-like dust and ice, aggregated, and experienced limited in situ aqueous alteration. These observations place new constraints on chondrule formation mechanisms in the outer disk and highlight the importance of localized melting and aggregation processes.

title: Contrasting Mo isotopic signatures in basalts linked to distinct subduction processes in the North China Craton
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Jian-Fang Guo, Qiang Ma, Liang Ma, Yi-Gang Xu, Jian-Ping Zheng, Chao Zhang, Hao Hu
abstract: Subduction is a fundamental process driving mantle evolution and material recycling, yet distinguishing the contributions of oceanic versus continental subduction to mantle heterogeneity remains a challenge. This study examines Mo isotopes, combined with elemental and Sr-Nd-Pb isotopic data of Early Cretaceous basalts in Sihetun (western Liaoning) and Feixian (western Shandong) in the North China Craton (NCC), regions influenced by distinct subduction processes. Sihetun basalts, exhibit light Mo isotopic compositions (δ 98/95Mo = -0.97 to −0.60‰), low Mo contents (0.32 − 0.41 ppm), high Ce/Mo ratios (292 − 426), and EMI-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These characteristics suggest a mantle source containing dehydrated oceanic crust and pelagic sediments, possibly related to the oceanic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. In contrast, Feixian basalts show heavier Mo isotopic signatures (δ 98/95Mo = -0.09 to 0.07‰), higher Mo contents (1.1 − 1.4 ppm), lower Ce/Mo ratios (137 − 197), and EMII-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These features point to the contribution of recycled continental crust and terrigenous sediments in their mantle sources, suggesting that their sources were affected by both deep subduction of the Yangtze continent and subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. These distinct Mo isotopic variations across the NCC reveal that oceanic subduction leads to lighter Mo isotopic signatures, while continental subduction introduces heavier Mo isotopic signatures to the overlying lithospheric mantle. This study highlights Mo isotopes as a powerful tracer for subduction-related processes and provides new insights into how oceanic and continental subduction regimes drive mantle enrichment and global geochemical cycles.

title: The solubility of Nd(OH) 3 (s) and thermodynamic optimization of Nd hydroxyl species in hydrothermal aqueous solutions from 25 to 300 °C
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Yerko Figueroa Penarrieta, Alexander P. Gysi
abstract: The mobilization of rare earth elements (REE) is controlled in many geological systems by the transport in hydrothermal aqueous fluids. Geochemical models are needed to predict their subsurface behavior and speciation in high temperature and pressure fluids. The REE3+ and REE hydroxyl complexes are known to control the solubility of REE in a wide pH range. However, thermodynamic data for the REE hydroxyl complexes are scarce at hydrothermal conditions. In this study, we measured the solubility of Nd(OH)3(s) between 100 and 250 °C at acidic to mildly acidic pH using batch-type solubility experiments. These data were used in combination with new calorimetric data for the Nd3+ aqua ion and previous potentiometric measurements of Nd hydroxyl species from the literature to optimize the standard partial molal Gibbs energy of formation (Δf G°) and the cumulative formation constants (log β1-3) of Nd hydroxyl complexes using the GEMSFITS code package. The formation constants (Nd3+ + nOH– ⇌ Nd(OH)n 3-n, n = 1 to 3) are fitted together with available literature data as a function of temperature (T) in Kelvin between 25 and 300 °C: log β 1 = -46.38 + 0.06681·T + 9620/T; log β 2 = -50.62 + 0.08554·T + 1074/T; log β 3 = –23.92 + 0.05953·T + 6480/T. These thermodynamic data are implemented in the MINES database and the GEMS code package to model the speciation of Nd as a function of pH and the solubility of monazite in hydrothermal fluids. Differences of up to 2 orders of magnitude are observed between the models generated from the revised thermodynamic data and the calculated predictions based on the Helgeson-Kirkham-Flowers equation of state parameters for REE hydroxyl complexes. The optimized thermodynamic properties improve the modeling of Nd speciation and REE mineral solubility.

title: Stable Mg-Zn isotope compositions in Mangaia HIMU lavas as tracers for ancient recycled carbonate
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Si-Yi Yang, Yongsheng He, Oliver Nebel, Jon D. Woodhead, Yang Wang (汪洋), Ying Han, Shan Ke
abstract: Intraplate lavas with heavy Zn isotopic compositions commonly exhibit light Mg isotope signatures, a pattern interpreted as evidence for recycling of Mg-rich carbonate. We report high-precision Mg and Zn isotopic data for lavas from Mangaia, an extreme HIMU OIB end-member thought to be derived from a CO2-rich parental melt. The Mangaia samples display whole-rock δ26Mg values ranging from −0.76‰ to −0.17‰, while δ66Zn varies narrowly between +0.19‰ and +0.39‰. After excluding samples affected by post-eruption alteration processes, we constrain the primary δ26Mg of the Mangaia lavas to −0.241 ± 0.018‰ (2SE, N = 15), indistinguishable from compositions of depleted upper mantle and mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB). In contrast, the primary δ66Zn is +0.35 ± 0.01‰ (2SE, N = 15), significantly higher than MORB, indicating a unique Mg and Zn isotope composition for the Mangaia mantle source. The elevated δ66Zn can be explained by a contribution of subducted altered oceanic crust (AOC), but a major AOC component is ruled out by petrological evidence for a peridotite-dominated source beneath Mangaia. Binary mixing and melting models show that the HIMU peridotite source was metasomatized by ≤ 10% melt derived from AOC containing 5–10% magnesite. The light Mg isotope signature of magnesite is diluted during mixing with the slab-derived silicates and ambient peridotite, whereas its heavy Zn isotope composition is preserved due to the high Zn concentration in magnesite. The ‘decoupled’ Mg-Zn isotope systematics of Mangaia thus reflect an ancient, well-homogenized carbonate-recycling event. In contrast, the light δ26Mg and heavy δ66Zn observed in some other intraplate basalts are consistent with melts generated directly from carbonate-rich portions of young subducting slabs, prior to extensive dilution by peridotitic mantle. This distinction makes combined Mg-Zn isotope investigations of intraplate lavas a useful tool to distinguish between contrasting carbonate recycling regimes, such as low-flux versus high-flux carbonate-rich melt metasomatism in ancient, hot subduction zones versus young, cold ones.

title: Metal and phosphorus accumulation in cryogenic alkaline lakes: Implications for salts in icy planetesimals and phosphate on early Mars
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Shuya Tan, Takuma Kitajima, Keisuke Fukushi, Baasansuren Gankhurel, Shuukhaaz Ganbat, So Fukaya, Davaadorj Davaasuren, Tuvshin Gerelmaa, Masahiro Yoda, Yasuhito Sekine, Yoshio Takahashi
abstract: The geochemical effects of freezing are becoming important in the investigation of closed aqueous environments, such as inland water on Earth and early Mars, and liquid water on planetesimals. Carbonate-bearing alkaline saline lakes in Mongolia are frozen in the cold season, with chemical species being partitioned among surface ice, lake water, and sediments. Freezing of the lakes leads to the accumulation of dissolved carbonate species, thereby decreasing the pH. The lakes are enriched not only in heavy metals, such as As, Mo, and U, but also in phosphorus. However, little is known about how metals and phosphorus are affected by chemical changes during freezing. Moreover, the mechanisms of major chemical changes are poorly understood and reproduced. Here we performed field surveys to investigate the behavior of these elements during lake freezing. Heavy metals and phosphorus accumulate in lake water during freezing, similar to major elements such as Cl−, with Mo and U concentrations reaching ∼1 mg/L. On the other hand, As and P accumulations are limited. Concentrations of heavy metals and phosphorus in ice increase with depth in the ice. We interpret the observed behavior using a geochemical model that accounts for their adsorption reactions coupled with water removal by freezing and carbonate precipitation. The model successfully reproduces the major chemical changes, including the decrease in pH, achieving quantitative accuracy by accounting for the combined effects of freezing and the revised solubility of carbonate minerals. The pH decrease promotes the adsorptions of As and P on sedimentary ferrihydrite particles, suppressing their accumulation in lake water. However, the decrease in pH is insufficient to promote adsorptions of Mo and U, resulting in their accumulations as major dissolved species. Adsorptions of heavy metals and phosphorus by iron oxides may be an important factor in their behaviors at low temperatures near the freezing point of water. Based on our model and observations, we discuss phosphate/carbonate precipitation in freezing porewater of icy planetesimals and phosphate availability in lake water on early Mars.

title: Deep mantle reservoirs of recycled surface carbonates revealed by Mg-Sr-Nd-Pb isotopes in continental basalts
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Yan-Qing Li, Chang-Qian Ma, Xiao-Ping Xia, Bin Liu, Ji-Ping Yu, Xiang-Yun Hu
abstract: Deep carbon recycling plays a pivotal role in redistributing carbon among the Earth’s internal reservoirs and modulating global climate over geological timescales. However, the depth at which subducted carbon is stored in the deep mantle, and the dynamics of its recycling remain poorly constrained. Subducted carbonates, typically characterized by lower δ26Mg values relative to the ambient mantle, make magnesium isotopes a powerful tracer for identifying recycled carbonates in mantle-derived rocks. In Eastern China, widespread Cenozoic basaltic volcanism is thought to be driven by hot and/or hydrous upwellings originating from the mantle transition zone (MTZ). Here, we present new Mg isotope data for Cenozoic basalts from Southeast China. Through a comprehensive comparison of Mg-Sr-Nd-Pb isotopic and elemental compositions of basalts from both Northeast and Southeast China, we identify distinct mechanisms of deep carbon recycling beneath the two regions. The low δ26Mg values observed in the Northeast China basalts are attributed to contributions from eclogites metamorphosed predominantly from ancient carbonated sediments stored within the MTZ. In contrast, the recycled carbon signatures in Southeast China basalts were derived mainly from eclogites metamorphosed from dehydrated oceanic crust, with only minor contributions from recycled sediments stored in the MTZ and possibly the deeper mantle. Considering the contrasting tectonic evolutions of Northeast and Southeast China since the Mesozoic, we propose a dynamic link between western Pacific Plate subduction and regionally distinct deep carbon cycling processes. Continuous subduction of the western Pacific Plate has formed a hydrous, carbonate-rich mantle domain beneath Northeast China, where fluid-induced partial melting acts as the key mechanism for carbon recycling. Conversely, dense, dehydrated carbonated eclogite fragments preserved in the deep mantle beneath Southeast China are difficult to ascend on their own, with local thermal upwellings providing the necessary dynamics for magma ascent. Our findings highlight that mantle hydration critically influences the efficiency of deep carbon recycling back to the surface through volcanism, with broader implications for the long-term stability of Earth’s carbon cycle.

title: Atomic mechanisms of diopside (CaMgSi 2 O 6 ) surface hydroxylation
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Shang Ma, Simon A.T. Redfern
abstract: Understanding how silicate surfaces interact with water is essential for predicting weathering, reactivity, metamorphic reactions as well as interface design. The initial adsorption of water at very low surface coverage governs subsequent hydroxylation, dissolution, and element release. Here, we use density functional theory to compare low-index diopside (CaMgSi2O6) surfaces and their terminations, and then focus on the lowest energy and experimentally relevant (110) facet as a reference for hydration analysis. Upon cleavage and relaxation, the surface develops a pronounced surface–subsurface stratification, with Si and Mg exposed in the outer layer and Ca in the subsurface. Relaxation leads to a local increase in the coordination of undercoordinated Si through short-range interactions with subsurface oxygen atoms, resulting in the formation of protruding SiO4 motifs that act as reactive centres without inducing large-scale structural rearrangement. Early hydration is characterized by configurations in which water-derived hydroxyl and proton species are stabilized at the surface, rather than by intact molecular adsorption. The first water-derived hydroxylation event shows that the hydroxyl group preferentially binds to protruding Si-centred reactive motif, and that the released proton preferred localizes at the neighbouring Image 1001 bridging oxygen. This event restores near-bulk tetrahedral coordination at Si and passivates the protruding site. After this initial dissociation event, the local reactivity is altered: further hydroxylation becomes more favourable at an undercoordinated Mg site, whereas Image 1002 + Image 1003 and Mg-H2O configuration become closer in energy, indicating increased local proton flexibility. These results provide an atomistic picture of the early low-coverage hydration on diopside (110), which is interpreted as a site-resolved mechanistic description of incipient hydration, rather than a full equilibrium thermodynamic description of the aqueous interface.

title: Factors shaping nickel bioavailability and isotopic signatures in marine phytoplankton
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Tzu-Hao Wang, Qiong Zhang, Yu-Te Hsieh, Gideon M. Henderson, Rosalind E.M. Rickaby
abstract: Biological activity in the photic zone is the most plausible mechanism for the regionally variable nickel (Ni) isotope fractionation observed in the surface oceans, but there is scant direct evidence for such biological control. Here we measure Ni isotope fractionation during phytoplankton growth and show that, in contrast to biological isotopic fractionation for most other elements, three cosmopolitan phytoplankton species preferentially take up isotopically heavy Ni from the culture media across a range of Ni availability, with species-dependent magnitudes of fractionation. Our data suggest that fractionation during phytoplankton uptake integrates more than one process, with an equilibrium fractionation at the cell surface via protein binding and a kinetic fractionation through intracellular metal transportation. The net fractionation towards heavy Ni isotopes can be explained in our experiments by the characteristic strong Ni-binding of cellular metal acquisition systems relative to weaker binding by ligands in the culture media. In the surface ocean, the opposite net fractionation is observed with lighter isotopes incorporated into biomass. This contrasts with our culture results, suggesting stronger binding of Ni to ligands present in the seawater relative to that of the phytoplankton. Such strong binding may lower effective Ni bioavailability in the surface ocean. This study indicates the importance of binding competition between cells and ligands in constraining Ni bioavailability and could underpin other metal isotopic signatures.

title: Coupled molybdenum and iron isotopes distinguish seawater and hydrothermal inputs to seep carbonates
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Hangyu Nan, Xiaoming Miao, Hongxiang Guan, Ang Li, Zhilei Sun, Thomas J. Algeo, Davide Oppo, Nengyou Wu, Sanzhong Li
abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) and its isotopic composition (δ98Mo) can serve as robust proxies for reconstructing paleo-oceanographic and paleoenvironmental conditions. Seep carbonates, in particular, hold potential for archiving contemporaneous seawater δ98Mo signatures. However, this application requires that Mo be sourced exclusively from seawater. This prerequisite is complicated by the frequently complex sources of Mo in cold seep environments, particularly within hydrothermally influenced systems. Here, we conducted elemental and Mo isotopic analyses of seep carbonates collected from the middle (MOT) and northern (NOT) Okinawa Trough. Seep carbonates from NOT, in contrast to those from MOT, exhibit distinctive hydrothermal vent signatures, including generally lower δ56Fe values (min: −0.49‰), elevated Fe/Al ratios (max: 2.90) that show positive correlations with the enrichment factors of V, Zn, As, Sb (VEF, ZnEF, AsEF, SbEF), and anomalous U enrichments (UEF max: 53). In addition, NOT seep carbonates show markedly lower δ98Mo (−0.55‰ to +0.99‰) compared to MOT sediments (+1.44‰ to +2.23‰; avg. +1.85‰), a pattern attributed to the incorporation of isotopically light, hydrothermally derived Mo into the former. A corroborating mass balance model demonstrates that the δ98Mo of NOT seep carbonates falls within the field defined by Mo sourced from hydrothermal plumes, whereas that of the MOT seep carbonates is consistent with a seawater-dominated source. Our findings reveal that seep carbonates can reliably record marine chemical signals, and, crucially, they underscore the critical need to account for source influences when interpreting Mo isotopes in sedimentary archives. This work thus significantly advances our understanding of Mo cycling in the ocean.

title: Enhancement of rare earth element bioleaching from regolith by a novel siderophore produced by Streptomyces sp
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Limin Zhang, Hailiang Dong, Tian Huang, Ning Liu, Ying Huang
abstract: Conventional extraction of rare earth elements (REEs) from minerals usually relies on chemical methods that lack selectivity and impose substantial environmental cost. Siderophores, secondary metabolites produced by various microorganisms, can be used as eco-friendly agents to selectively extract REEs. A red soil-derived actinomycete, Streptomyces sp. FXJ1.4098, produced a ubiquitous siderophore desferrioxamine E (DFOE) and a novel siderophore, provisionally named Svf. In this study, we report the ability of Streptomyces sp. FXJ1.4098 to leach REEs via production of these siderophores. Siderophore biosynthesis gene clusters were identified and corresponding siderophore-deficient mutants were constructed. Unexpectedly, the DFOE-deficient mutant ΔdesD1.4098 achieved a significantly higher REE leaching efficiency (44.25 ± 0.28%) from a regolith-hosted REE deposit than the wild-type strain (27.76 ± 1.98%) after incubation for 9 days. This result suggested that deletion of DFOE likely stimulated secretion of Svf and thus enhanced REE extraction. In contrast, the Svf-deficient mutant ΔsvfCD1.4098 leached much lower amounts of REEs than the wild type under the same conditions, with a leaching efficiency of only 21.76 ± 1.71%. This finding suggested that siderophore Svf exhibited a superior capacity for leaching REEs from regolith. Light REEs and Y were preferentially bioleached in ΔdesD1.4098 system at a short-time incubation. Ce was least leached, because it occurred as a refractory Ce oxide. Leached REEs re-adsorbed onto cellular and residual mineral surfaces, thus lowering their aqueous concentrations. In the presence of siderophores Svf and DFOE, adsorption of REEs onto minerals/cells showed a decreasing trend with increasing atomic number. This is attributed to the higher stability of siderophore complexes with REEs of smaller ionic radii. These findings suggest that siderophore-driven REE bioleaching by Streptomyces holds a significant promise for practical application.

title: Impact origin of pink spinel in the Chang’e-6 lunar soils
description: Publication date: 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 429 Author(s): Linxi Li, Guangyuan Yu, Sen Hu, Hejiu Hui, Yi Chen, Qiu-Li Li, Wei Yang, Lihui Jia, Di Zhang, Shitou Wu, Guoqiang Tang, Hao Wang, Lixin Gu, Ziyu Wang, Huicun He, Yubing Gao, Mengfan Qiu, Liang Gao, Zhan Zhou, Yangting Lin
abstract: Pink spinel (Mg-Al spinel) is an enigmatic mineral in understanding lunar crustal evolution. Here, we report the discovery of three pink spinel-bearing fragments in the Chang’e-6 (CE6) lunar soils. The three fragments are mainly composed of euhedral plagioclase, olivine, pink spinel, and interstitial glass. The constituent minerals are usually less than 30 µm, except plagioclase. Some coarse plagioclase particles (> 50 µm) were found in these fragments. The coarse plagioclases exhibit contrast cathodoluminescence (CL) features with the smaller lath-shaped plagioclases, showing bright cores and dark rims in CL images. The CL-bright cores have lower MgO contents (∼0.08 wt%) than the CL-dark rims (∼0.30 wt%), suggesting that they are relic plagioclase from ferroan anorthosite. The occurrences of small olivine and spinel crystals ( 1200 µg/g) and bulk fragments (>500 µg/g), the three spinel-bearing fragments likely represent melt rocks of pre-existing anorthosite lithologies during impacts. Oxygen isotopes in sample olivine grains (δ18O = +5.4 ± 1.4‰; Δ17O ≈ 0‰) are consistent with lunar endogenous minerals. A simple mixing of certain impactors and lunar crustal materials cannot simultaneously account for the compositional and isotopic signatures of the fragments. Therefore, an impact-induced mixing model involving protolith anorthosite with excavated Mg-suite materials is proposed as an alternative scenario to explain the petrogenesis of the fragments. These findings provide direct evidence supporting impact events hybridizing lunar crustal rocks to generate pink spinel-bearing lithologies. These results further strengthen the role of the impact processes in modifying the surficial lunar crust, as melting and mixing triggered by impact can produce hybridization effects comparable to those caused by magma-wallrock interactions at depth. Combining petrographic, chemical, and isotopic datasets are helpful for unrevealing the origin(s) of pink spinel-bearing lithologies on the Moon.

title: The iron mineralogy of Bennu samples: similarities and variations among CI chondritic materials
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kana Amano, Jean-Christophe Viennet, Pierre Beck, Sergey Yaroslavtsev, Dimitrios Bessas, Aleksandr Chumakov, Jean-Philippe Celse, Ludovic Delbes, Tomoki Nakamura, Yuma Enokido, Kanako Sakamoto, Shogo Tachibana, Mathieu Roskosz
abstract: Recent findings from sample-return missions targeting carbonaceous asteroids suggest that CI-like (Carbonaceous Ivuna-type) small bodies are more common in the solar system than previously thought. However, the general redox characteristics and variations among CI materials remain largely unexplored due to their limited availability on Earth. Moreover, CI meteorites have likely undergone irreversible terrestrial oxidation, resulting in modifications of the iron speciation and the redox states. In this context, the iron mineralogy of samples from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu allows us to reassess the redox conditions of CI materials during its formation. We performed X-ray diffraction and Mössbauer spectroscopy of two Bennu particles from the hummocky group, as well as Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. We compare their iron speciation to that of other CI and CI-like materials, including samples from the asteroid Ryugu, Orgueil CI meteorite, and Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. The results show that Bennu particles contain substantial amounts of Fe sulfides (pyrrhotite, mackinawite, and pentlandite), along with Fe oxide (magnetite) and Fe-bearing (Mg-rich) phyllosilicates, similar to Ryugu samples. Cryogenic Mössbauer analysis indicates no significant contribution from ferric oxyhydroxides (i.e., ferrihydrite) in Bennu and Oued Chebeika 002 samples, confirming the previous electron microscopy observations of those samples. These observations imply that Fe3+ forming ferrihydrite observed in historical CI meteorites (e.g., Orgueil, Alais) results from long-term terrestrial oxidation of Fe2+ in sulfides, especially submicron-sized ones. This further strengthens the view that the actual CI materials and their formation environments are less oxidizing than previously estimated from old CI meteorite falls. The Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+) ratios in phyllosilicates in the hummocky particles range from 50 to 70%, indicating local heterogeneity within individual particles. Whereas similar values have been reported for Bennu samples (determined by X-ray Absorption Near-Edge Structure spectroscopy), Ryugu samples, and Oued Chebeika 002 samples (i.e., ∼50–65% of Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+)phyllosilicates), there may be slightly Fe3+-rich sub-regions (close to ∼ 70%) in our Bennu particles. Furthermore, we found two distinct mineral assemblages among CI and CI-like materials: (i) relatively well-crystallized phyllosilicates without mackinawite but with pyrrhotite, and (ii) disordered phyllosilicates coexisting with mackinawite, a metastable Fe sulfide. The latter finding is consistent with recent studies of mackinawite in Bennu and Ryugu samples, which suggest its formation at the early stages of CI alteration. Together with previous studies of Bennu, Ryugu, and Orgueil samples, our results suggest that different phyllosilicate assemblages preserve distinct Fe valence states, potentially recording redox conditions associated with different stages of formation. The CI materials have conventionally been regarded as relatively equilibrated and homogeneous, however, our results demonstrate the potential of combining clay mineral crystallinity and Fe valence states to unravel formation histories at a finer scale.

title: Heavy Rb isotope composition of subduction zone fluids resulting from fluid-rock interaction in continental subduction zones
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Anxia Chen, Yi-Xiang Chen, Dingsheng Jiang, Hans-Peter Schertl, Shouzhen Yang, Fang Huang
abstract: Subduction zone fluids are key agents for the transport of rubidium (Rb), yet the Rb isotope compositions of these fluids and the associated fractionation during fluid-rock interaction remain poorly constrained. This hinders the application of Rb isotopes as a powerful tracer for fluid-mediated mass transfer in subduction zones. To address this problem, we present a systematic Rb isotope study of ultrahigh-pressure whiteschists and their metagranite protoliths from the Western Alps. The whiteschists formed through intense Mg-rich fluid infiltration during deep continental subduction, whereas the metagranites underwent ultrahigh-pressure metamorphism with negligible fluid-rock interaction. The whiteschists show significantly lower and more variable δ87Rb (−1.06 to 0.04‰) than the metagranites (−0.15 to 0.06‰). The δ87Rb values of the whiteschists correlate negatively with MgO and fluid-mobile element concentrations, indicating significant Rb isotope fractionation during fluid-rock interaction. Under extreme fluid-rock interaction conditions, modeling yields a first-order apparent integrated isotope effect (Δ87Rbrock-fluid) of −1.53 to −1.07‰, corresponding to a calculated fluid composition (δ87Rbfluid) of ∼0.47‰. Although this represents an end-member condition under high fluid-rock ratios, the result demonstrates that subduction zone fluids preferentially extract the heavy Rb isotope (87Rb), leaving the residual rocks enriched in the light one (85Rb). Our findings establish Rb isotopes as a sensitive tracer of fluid-rock interaction processes and provide key constraints for understanding Rb isotope variations in arc magmas and mantle heterogeneity.

title: Nickel and magnesium isotopic evidence for rapid melt-mantle interactions in supra-subduction zone settings
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Zhuang Ma, Shui-Jiong Wang, Fahui Xiong, Wenzhong Wang, Kun-Feng Qiu, Long Zhang, Zhenyu Chen, Hanjie Wen, Li-Guang Wu
abstract: Supra-subduction zone (SSZ) settings are characterized by extensive melt-mantle interactions that contribute substantially to the enrichment of economically critical metals. However, the rates and durations of these interactions are not well understood. In this study, we integrate nickel (Ni) and magnesium (Mg) isotopic analyses, first-principles calculations, and chromium-aluminum (Cr-Al) diffusion chronometry of chromite from SSZ-type ophiolites to elucidate the processes and timescales of melt-mantle interaction during chromite formation. Chromite and coexisting olivine from the Luobusa and Yushigou ophiolites exhibit systematically heavy Ni-Mg isotopic compositions (δ 60/58Ni = 0.63‰ to 0.96‰ for chromite and 0.09‰ to 0.36‰ for olivine; δ 26/24Mg = 0.16‰ to 0.61‰ for chromite and −0.26‰ to −0.13‰ for olivine) compared to mantle values, with significant inter-mineral isotope disequilibrium. These features cannot be attributed to subsolidus elemental exchange, but instead indicate that kinetic isotope fractionation during melt-mantle interaction was the dominant process. Diffusion modeling of both Ni-Mg isotopes and Cr-Al zoning in chromite yields consistently short timescales: Ni-Mg isotope diffusion constrains the duration to centennial scales, while Cr-Al diffusion modeling gives a median of decades to centuries (80% < several thousand years). Our findings demonstrate that melt-mantle interactions in SSZ settings are transient but highly efficient, providing a temporal framework to constrain the rapid formation of podiform chromitites.

title: Complexity of baddeleyite microstructure and Pb-Pb age in lunar gabbroic breccias: implications for the NWA 773 Clan chronology
description: Publication date: Available online 9 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Liying Huang, Lee Francis White, Xuchao Zhao, Mahesh Anand, Muhammad Zeeshan Mughal, Yuchen Xu, Yang Liu, Yongliao Zou
abstract: Baddeleyite (monoclinic-ZrO2) is a key accessory mineral for dating mafic rocks and tracing magmatic and impact processes. Although its crystal structure is highly sensitive to pressure–temperature (P-T) conditions, integrated studies linking microstructural response of lunar baddeleyite to P-T histories and Pb-Pb ages remain limited. Here we integrate in-situ Pb-Pb dating with high-resolution electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis of baddeleyite grains in two lunar gabbroic breccia meteorites, Northwest Africa 773 and 3333. Based on crystallographic and petrographic characteristics, baddeleyite grains are classified into five groups, reflecting diverse P-T histories. A notable finding is widespread preservation of cubic heritage baddeleyite, despite relatively lower-T records recorded by coexisting silicates. This feature is attributed to elevated shock pressures that depress stability fields of high-T ZrO2 polymorphs, modification of phase stability by impurities (e.g., Ti and Fe), and grains experienced high-T conditions prior to incorporation into their present host rocks. Clast-hosted baddeleyite yields a coherent weighted mean Pb-Pb age of 3100 ± 8.5 Ma (n = 9), interpreted as the primary magmatic crystallization age, whereas matrix-hosted grains show a broader age distribution around ∼3.1 Ga. Two matrix-hosted grains associated with impact melt veins yield a younger age of 2941 ± 20 Ma, consistent with later ∼2.9 Ga thermal modification. The absence of a systematic relationship between Pb-Pb age and microstructural type suggests that ZrO2 phase transformations alone do not exert a first-order control on Pb mobility. Instead, heterogeneous propagation of pressure and temperature during shock metamorphism, together with the intensity and duration of thermal events, appears to govern isotopic disturbance. These results highlight the importance of integrated microstructural and geochronological approaches for reconstructing complex lunar thermal histories.

title: The importance of deep reactions between ascending komatiite and pre-existing protocratonic lithosphere for the chemistry of Archaean peridotites and greenstone belt volcanics: insights from reaction experiments
description: Publication date: Available online 9 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Rodrigo Freitas Rodrigues, Balz S. Kamber, Gregory M. Yaxley, Emma L. Tomlinson, Sandra Piazolo, Nathan R. Daczko
abstract: The cratonic lithospheric mantle is the buoyant 200–250 km deep root that enabled ancient continents (cratons) to survive for billions of years. The root stabilised due to extensive melting, erupting magnesian magmas at surface. However, peridotite xenolith samples from the cratonic mantle exhibit far more variable olivine/orthopyroxene and MgO/SiO2 ratios than expected from residues after melting of fertile mantle, exemplified by enigmatic dunites and orthopyroxene-rich harzburgites. Similarly, Archaean ultramafic lavas (komatiites) also show wider MgO/SiO2 variability than could be expected from shallow olivine fractionation. In addition, many komatiites have unexpectedly complex radiogenic isotope systematics, inconsistent with high-degree melting of refractory mantle. Thermodynamic modelling has suggested that these complexities could arise during deep (2–5 GPa) melt-solid reactions. Here, we present high-pressure layered experiments (3 GPa) involving the reaction between komatiite juxtaposed against harzburgite. The melt-bearing reactions yielded layered charges, wherein the initial komatiite layer (original, unreacted composition) was transformed into orthopyroxene-rich harzburgite following the reaction, and the original harzburgite layer resulted in the formation of dunite, with mineral modes and Mg-number depending on temperature. The solid residues of the reacted layers (orthopyroxene-rich and olivine-rich) are compositionally and mineralogically analogous to natural cratonic harzburgites and dunites, respectively. Thermodynamic modelling indicates that the MgO/SiO2 variability of the residues could be further increased by reacting the komatiite with fertile lherzolite instead of harzburgite. Solid-melt reactions markedly altered the composition of the incoming komatiite melt, with basaltic komatiite and komatiitic basalt formed at lower temperatures and modified high-Mg komatiites at higher temperatures. The melts exhibit the very wide range of MgO/SiO2 seen in ultramafic lavas in Archaean greenstone belts. Consideration of rare earth element and Hf partitioning suggests that assimilation of protocratonic ancient harzburgite into invading komatiite will be much more strongly seen in radiogenic Hf than Nd (or Ce) isotope ratios. Although both the original solid (harzburgite) and the incoming melt (komatiite) are ultramafic, their chemical contrast is sufficient to drive metasomatic reaction, likely partly due to the presence of a percolating melt. The reactions require higher temperatures than attained in the post-Archaean mantle, explaining both the sharp demise of komatiites after 2.5 Ga and the highly refractory nature of Archaean harzburgites and dunites. Ancient proto-cratonic mantle is one plausible candidate harbouring radiogenic signatures of Hadean silicate differentiation. The reason why these signatures are most commonly found in Archaean mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks may relate to the secular drop in maximum plume temperature, which has compromised the capacity of younger melts to sample this reservoir via assimilation

title: Negative 182 W anomalies in geochemically-depleted kimberlites reveal a common primordial component
description: Publication date: Available online 8 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nao Nakanishi, Andrea Giuliani, D. Graham Pearson, Lori Willhite, Richard J. Walker
abstract: Certain kimberlites from worldwide localities are characterized by small negative μ182W anomalies (Nakanishi et al., 2021), where μ182W is the part per million difference in 182W/184W between sample and standards. This study re-evaluates the origin of the isotopically anomalous reservoir accessed by these kimberlites by analyzing an expanded range of kimberlites. Because Nd-Hf isotopic compositions are affected by crustal and lithospheric mantle contamination, which could also strongly attenuate an anomalous μ182W value, kimberlite samples with the highest initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios, and therefore least affected by the addition of subducted or assimilated lithospheric material, may provide the most accurate constraint on the μ182W value of the anomalous reservoir. New W isotope data for 18 kimberlites from seven regions with variable Nd-Hf isotope compositions are reported. These kimberlites, combined with data from the prior study, indicate a broad correlation between μ182W and initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios, projecting to an anomalous endmember composition with a μ182W value of ∼−8 at the highest initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios. The inferred endmember μ182W value requires that the anomalous W signature originated in a reservoir isolated from the bulk silicate Earth very early in Earth history. Similar to proposed explanations for negative μ182W values in some modern ocean island basalts (OIBs), the isotopically anomalous mantle domain was most likely either infused with core-derived W characterized by strongly negative μ182W, or created as the result of silicate fractionation during the first 60 Myr of Solar System history, for example during magma ocean crystallization. Regardless of the origin of the anomalous W, the observations support an interpretation that some kimberlites and modern OIBs may share similar mantle components probably located in the lowermost mantle.

title: Mg and Ca isotopes of phreatic groundwater on a carbonate island: implications for meteoric diagenesis of carbonates
description: Publication date: Available online 8 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Huiwen Huang, Gang Li, Yun Luo, Weihai Xu, Wen Yan
abstract: Meteoric diagenesis can significantly overprint primary geochemical signatures of marine carbonates. Constraining the associated geochemical differentiation is therefore essential for distinguishing primary signals from alteration, but remains difficult based on altered-carbonate geochemistry alone. We investigated major ion concentrations and Ca–Mg isotopic compositions (δ 44/40Ca and δ26Mg) of groundwater from Yongshu Island (southern South China Sea), a site marked by extensive freshwater–seawater mixing within its subsurface aquifers. By using Cl− as a conservative seawater tracer in a binary mixing model, the freshwater δ26Mg value of −2.1 ‰ was obtained, whereas the freshwater δ 44/40Ca value (∼0 ‰) was assumed to equal that of seawater, as it showed no correlation with Ca2+ concentration. The inferred δ26Mg and δ 44/40Ca values of freshwater are markedly higher than those expected from carbonate dissolution. Together with box modeling of meteoric diagenetic water–rock reactions, these elevated isotopic values are inferred to arise from fluid isotopic evolution under sediment-buffered conditions within the vadose zone. The newly obtained δ26Mg and δ 44/40Ca compositions of freshwater were used to model meteoric phreatic diagenesis of carbonate rocks. The modeled results can well reproduce the coupled Ca–Mg isotopic evolution observed in young meteoric water-altered carbonates from coral islands in the South China Sea and the Great Barrier Reef, Australia. These results are interpreted to reflect predominantly fluid-buffered meteoric diagenesis within the meteoric phreatic zone. Differentiating the sediment-buffered vadose zone from the fluid-buffered phreatic zone allows for a coherent interpretation of the Ca–Mg isotopic compositions in both meteoric limestones and reef-island freshwater. Elucidating Mg and Ca isotopic behavior in the vadose and phreatic zones during meteoric diagenesis will provide a robust framework for interpreting paleoenvironmental signals preserved in freshwater-altered carbonates.

title: Iron isotopes reveal the transition from magmatic to hydrothermal systems in highly evolved granites
description: Publication date: Available online 6 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yikang Quan, Jiaru Sheng, Gengxin Deng, Yan Jing, Xiangyu Yan, Fang Huang
abstract: In granitic systems, compositional variations in major elements are relatively limited, especially during the highly evolved granite stage. Although fluid influx or exsolution after saturation can drive continued magma evolution, traditional geochemical methods cannot accurately identify these processes, hindering further understanding of highly evolved granites. Here, we use iron isotope (δ56Fe) and trace element data from four-stage granites (NL-1 to NL-4) from a common transcrustal magmatic system in the Nanling Range, Southeast China, to decipher evolutionary processes of highly evolved granitic systems. The δ56Fe exhibits a systematic increase from NL-1 (0.08‰-0.19‰) to NL-2 (0.14‰-0.25‰), remains constant from NL-2 to NL-3 (0.14‰-0.24‰), and shows a large variation in NL-4 (0.07‰-0.30‰), whereas Nb/Ta, Zr/Hf, and K/Rb decrease with increasing evolution. These geochemical observations most likely reflect the magmatic-hydrothermal transition. Quantitative modeling indicates three distinct stages: (1) an early magmatic stage (NL-1) characterized by < 15% fractional crystallization of Fe-bearing minerals accompanied by < 10% fluid exsolution; (2) a magmatic-hydrothermal transition stage (NL-2 and NL-3) involving progressive magmatic differentiation (<20%) coupled with fluid metasomatism (<15%), and (3) a late hydrothermal stage (NL-4) dominated by 0–30% fluid metasomatism. Concentrations of fluid-mobile elements (e.g., Rb) increase moderately during the magmatic stage, more during the transition stage, and sharply in the hydrothermal stage. Our findings delineate two distinct stages in the evolution of highly evolved granitic magma. The early magmatic stage is governed by fractional crystallization, whereas the late hydrothermal stage is controlled by fluid metasomatism. This demonstrates that fluid is the primary driver of trace-element migration during highly evolved granites.

title: Erosion-driven changes in soil cation exchange capacity quantified using barium isotopes
description: Publication date: Available online 6 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Luke Bridgestock, Emily Stevenson, J.Jotautas Baronas, Alasdair Knight, Harold J. Bradbury, Alexandra V. Turchyn, Edward T. Tipper
abstract: Human activities have perturbed the balance between soil erosion and formation rates, driving declines in soil quality. Quantifying these soil imbalances remains challenging, especially at large scales. Here we present a novel isotope mass balance approach to quantify river catchment wide rates of change in cation exchange capacity (CEC), a key soil quality metric, in response to erosional perturbations. The approach uses differences in Ba isotope composition between river export fluxes and chemical weathering inputs to solve for rates of change of Ba storage within upstream soil exchange pools. Data for river water and suspended particulate material (SPM) samples from the Irrawaddy and Salween river demonstrate the utility of the approach. River dissolved loads and exchange pools of co-existing SPM loads feature a Ba isotope fractionation of Δ138/134Ba diss-sp = 0.23 ± 0.14 ‰. Variations in the Ba isotope composition of the sum of these two Ba pools in river outputs (δ 138/134Baout) are predominantly controlled by SPM concentration. At low SPM concentrations δ 138/134Baout are offset to higher values relative to average rocks. This is interpreted to reflect the accumulation of isotopically light Ba in upstream soil exchange pools due to CEC increases. Using a mass balance framework, catchment wide changes in CEC are quantified from the Ba isotopic data. During peak discharge conditions the Salween River basin is balanced within uncertainty of the data for its catchment wide CEC budget, while the Irrawaddy River basin features net CEC accumulation of at least 35 ± 5 meq/m2/year. Net CEC accumulation in the Irrawaddy River basin is interpreted to reflect SPM deposition in floodplains, while the CEC balance observed in the Salween River basin likely reflects the limited floodplain area of this catchment. These results demonstrate the utility of this approach to quantify river catchment wide soil quality (CEC) changes driven by human perturbations to terrestrial sediment transport.

title: Platinum occurs as α-PtO 2 nanoparticles in deep-sea ferromanganese deposits
description: Publication date: Available online 3 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jianlin Liao, Yan Li, Julien Léger, Andrea Koschinsky, Catherine Dejoie, Anne-Claire Gaillot, Irina Snigireva, Andrea Giacomelli, Stephan N. Steinmann, Olivier Mathon, Alain Manceau
abstract: Understanding how critical metals such as platinum (Pt) are enriched in marine environments is essential for advancing knowledge of their geochemical cycles and the formation of oceanic mineral resources. Pt occurs in seawater at picomolar concentrations, yet deep-sea ferromanganese (FeMn) deposits contain up to eight orders of magnitude more Pt. The mechanism behind this enrichment remains unresolved. Although FeMn deposits exhibit high Pt partitioning, their low Pt levels and the co-occurrence of multiple elements pose challenges to investigating Pt oxidation state and uptake processes using traditional spectroscopic methods. In this study, high-energy-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) was used to elucidate how Pt is sequestered at the atomic scale in FeMn crusts and nodules from the Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian oceans.
