(2) GWSA declined at −0.29 cm/yr, with significant decreases over 50.97% of the area. REOF reveals a north-south dipole—decreasing in the north while increasing in the south—reflecting contrasting hydrological controls between natural recharge and anthropogenic exploitation. (3) Natural drivers (P − E, SMSA) influence GWSA at seasonal–interannual scales, whereas exploitation dominates the long-term trend. Notably, reduced pumping has not reversed GWSA decline, suggesting cumulative loss exceeds natural recovery. (4) A 5-month phase lag exists between GRACE-derived GWSA and in-situ level. GRACE effectively captures the long-term declining trend, but short-term phase information should be interpreted with caution.

title: Hydrogeological settings shape drought impacts on river flows in Corsica, France: Evidence from multi-tracer investigations, watershed typology and past-trend analysis
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): P.A. Guisiano, S. Santoni, E. Garel, T. Leydier, F. Huneau
abstract: Study Region This study investigates 13 benchmark Mediterranean watersheds located in Corsica, France. These hard-rock watersheds are representative of contrasting hydrogeological settings ranging from coastal lowlands to mountainous granitic and metamorphic terrains, under a Mediterranean climate characterised by strong drought variability and hydroclimatic stress. Study Focus This study focuses on their hydrogeological dynamics under drought conditions, using an integrated approach combining watershed characterisation, multivariate statistical classification, tracer-based analysis (18O, 2H, 222Rn, EC), and long-term hydrological trends assessment. Multivariate analyses are used to identify hydrogeological watershed typologies and to relate morphometric, climatic, and geological attributes to their subsurface flow processes and groundwater contributions. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Four hydrogeological watershed typologies are identified, defining a gradient from climate-dominated coastal systems with limited storage and rapid flow paths to granitic groundwater-buffered systems with higher recharge efficiency, deeper flow paths, and stronger baseflow contributions, and with intermediate behaviours controlled by mountain headwaters influence or metamorphic structural constraints. Watersheds with limited groundwater storage are highly sensitive to precipitation decline and show reduced baseflow, whereas groundwater-buffered systems exhibit higher resilience and more stable hydrological regimes over time. Overall, the results demonstrate that hydrological responses to climate variability are primarily controlled by hydrogeological conditions rather than climate forcing alone, supporting process-based watershed management strategies tailored to Mediterranean environments facing increasing drought pressure and water resource vulnerability.

title: Environmental controls on the seasonal variations of evapotranspiration in a cold-temperate Larix gmelinii forest
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Shuai Hao, Qiuliang Zhang, Bing Wang, Yusheng Hao, Chuan Jin, Xuguang Tang, Yangbin Yuan, Rula Sa, Yongjie Yue, Heng Zhang
abstract: Study region This study was conducted in a natural Larix gmelinii forest in the Greater Khingan Mountains of northeastern China, near the southern margin of the Eurasian permafrost region. The region experiences pronounced freeze–thaw cycles, persistent winter snow cover, and a short growing season. Study focus Four years of eddy covariance and meteorological observations (2022–2025) were analyzed to determine how evapotranspiration (ET) regulation differed among spring thaw, growing season, autumn freezing, and non-growing season. Phase-specific correlations, piecewise structural equation modeling (SEM), and cross-year-validated XGBoost–SHAP modeling were used to characterize seasonal associations, annual hydrothermal pathways, and nonlinear transitions in environmental responses. New hydrological insights for the region Annual ET ranged from 398.8 to 486.8 mm and varied less among years than precipitation. Growing-season ET contributed 70.9–79.9% of annual ET, and spring thaw contributed 14.1–20.1%, highlighting the significance of freeze–thaw periods. Controls on ET differed among hydrothermal phases. Spring thaw ET was primarily thermally constrained, whereas growing season ET was influenced by temperature, canopy development, radiation, and soil moisture. SEM explained 82% of ET variance and identified soil temperature as the principal regulatory factor, with contributions from soil moisture and antecedent hydroclimatic conditions. XGBoost–SHAP analysis indicated nonlinear responses to soil temperature, leaf area index, soil water content, and net radiation. These findings indicate that forest water cycling transitions seasonally from freeze–thaw constraints to biologically regulated water loss.

title: Measuring hydrological functional connectivity and its associations with flood processes in river network plains: Insights from flow smoothness and continuity
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zhihui Yu, Miao Lu, Qiang Wang, Youpeng Xu, Qiaoling Dong
abstract: Study region The Central Taihu Plain, located in the core region of the Yangtze River Delta in eastern China. Study focus We propose a new indicator, Hydrological Functional Connectivity Index (HFCI), which integrates flow smoothness and continuity to quantify channel-scale functional connectivity. Using the Central Taihu Plain as a case study, we characterize the spatiotemporal dynamics of HFCI and quantify its associations with flood processes. New hydrological insights Mean HFCI in the Central Taihu Plain was 0.72 during 1970–2019, indicating generally good functional connectivity. HFCI in Wu-Cheng-Xi- Yu (WCXY) was higher than in Yang-Cheng-Dian-Mao (YCDM). HFCI declined significantly (p < 0.01) at 0.033/10a. Relatively high values occurred mainly in the interior channel networks of the WCXY and YCDM, whereas lower values were concentrated along Yangtze-facing reaches and around major urban flood control enclosure and outlet control zones. The recession rate (FE) was positively associated with HFCI, whereas peak water level (FM), water level increment (FA), and rising rate (FR) were negatively associated, particularly under higher rainfall intensities. FM showed the strongest stratified association with HFCI (q = 0.202), followed by FR (0.131), FE (0.125), and FA (0.118). These findings provide valuable insights into flood control under changing river connectivity.

title: Downscaled snow depth over the Tibetan Plateau via meteorology- and topography-informed generative adversarial network
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zhengdong Ma, Lingmei Jiang, Qingwang Wang, Yuna Jiang, Jiancheng Shi, Yueqian Cao
abstract: Study region The Tibetan Plateau (TP), often referred to as the "Water Tower of Asia," characterized by complex terrain, high altitude, and highly heterogeneous snow cover distribution. Study focus Existing satellite snow depth products over the TP often suffer from coarse spatial resolution (e.g., 25-km), limiting their utility in localized hydrological modeling. To address this spatial mismatch, we developed a Meteorology- and Topography-Constrained Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (ConvGAN) to downscale snow depth from 25-km to 5-km. Unlike purely data-driven models, this framework integrates multi-source physical forcing data (precipitation, temperature, radiation) and high-resolution elevation parameters to constrain the generative process, ensuring the outputs adhere to regional environmental dynamics. New hydrological insights for the region The proposed ConvGAN successfully reconstructs fine-scale spatial variability that coarse products miss. It accurately reproduces elevation-dependent distribution patterns and captures the critical autumn “U-shape” snow accumulation cycle, with distributional divergence as low as D KL < 0.006 in high-elevation zones under optimal configuration. The whole-plateau D KL ranges from 0.011 to 0.425 across all experimental setups, with the best overall configuration achieving D KL = 0.011. By significantly mitigating spatial uncertainties in complex topographies, the generated 7-year (2013–2019) 5-km snow depth dataset provides a highly reliable benchmark. This high-resolution product enhances our ability to monitor snow drought, predict spring snowmelt runoff, and support precise water resource management across the diverse climatic zones of the TP.

title: Two decades of terrestrial water storage change in the Northern China Farming-Pastoral Ecotone (2002–2024): Components and drivers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Tao Wang, Haitao Wei, Jing Wang, Guangyao Gao, Qingyu Feng, Hengliang Guo, Baojin Qiao, Minghui Zhang, Yongpei Zhao, Di Liu, Siyuan Wang
abstract: Study region: Northern China Farming-Pastoral Ecotone (NCFPE), China Study focus: NCFPE is a climate-sensitive transition zone where water scarcity constrains sustainable development. However, the spatiotemporal evolution of terrestrial water storage (TWS) anomalies and their components, particularly surface water storage (SWS) anomalies, remains poorly understood, limiting reliable driver attribution. We integrate GRACE/GRACE-FO gravimetry, GLDAS simulations, and lake and reservoir datasets (GloLakes and GLWS) to quantify TWS component anomalies during 2002–2024. Multi-source meteorological data and NDVI are combined with GeoDetector and grid-scale correlation analyses to identify dominant climatic and ecological controls. New hydrogeological insights for the region: TWS exhibits pronounced meridional contrasts, with increases in the northeast and southwest but persistent declines across central and southern regions, while widespread SWS gains partially offset subsurface depletion. NDVI-related dominant areas account for nearly 40% of the total area, representing about two-thirds of the effective area. Mechanisms vary spatially: precipitation compensates vegetation water use in the Songliao Basin; ecological restoration and rising demand intensified TWS losses in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region before partial recovery linked to the South-to-North Water Diversion Project; and vegetation growth combined with warming drives sustained depletion on the Loess Plateau. These findings demonstrate how ecological restoration and human interventions have reshaped regional water storage dynamics and emphasize incorporating SWS into TWS assessments for sustainable water management.

title: Hydrochemical and isotopic evidence of groundwater evolution in unconfined aquifer systems of the semi-arid Cariri Valley, Northeast Brazil
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Letycia Oliveira Venancio Uvula, Ricardo Perobelli Borba, Idembergue Barroso Macedo de Moura
abstract: Study region The Cariri Valley, located in the Araripe Basin of northeastern Brazil, hosts two stratigraphically distinct unconfined aquifer systems that constitute the primary groundwater source for domestic, agricultural, and industrial water supply in one of the largest semi-arid regions of South America. Understanding the hydrochemical evolution and recharge dynamics of these aquifers is essential for sustainable groundwater management under increasing climatic variability. Study focus This study investigated the hydrochemical and isotopic differentiation between the Missão Velha–Rio da Batateira Aquifer System and the Mauriti Aquifer using groundwater monitoring data collected in 2017 and 2018 within the Brazilian Integrated Groundwater Monitoring Network (RIMAS). Major-ion chemistry, stable isotopes (δ¹⁸O and δ²H), mineralogical characterization by X-ray diffraction, saturation indices calculated with PHREEQC, and hydrochemical indices were integrated to evaluate recharge conditions, water–rock interaction, and groundwater evolution. New hydrological insights for the region Both aquifer systems have a meteoric recharge origin but differ in hydrochemical variability and multivariate composition. The MV–RB showed broader compositional dispersion, whereas Mauriti samples occupied a more restricted domain; however, overlap between systems remained and the small Mauriti sample size limits generalization. Principal component analysis explained 63.34% of the variance in the first two components. PERMANOVA identified a multivariate group effect (pseudo-F = 4.42; p = 0.0071), while a significant dispersion test (p = 0.0376) showed that this result partly reflects the greater heterogeneity of the MV–RB. Silicate weathering and cation exchange are consistent with the mineralogical and ionic evidence, while nitrate and chloride indicate localized surface-derived influence. Stable isotope compositions plot near precipitation-derived meteoric references and support a common recharge source, with the data being consistent with limited pre-infiltration evaporation. The results refine the conceptual model of groundwater evolution in the Cariri Valley while explicitly recognizing analytical-quality and sampling limitations.

title: Stable isotopes ( δ 18 Ο H2O , δ ²H H2O ) and hydrochemical fingerprints of groundwater interactions in the Afram Plains South aquifers, Voltaian Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Christopher Vuu, Amos Tiereyangn Kabo-bah, Geophrey Kwame Anornu, Abass Gibrilla, Gabriel J. Bowen, David Saka, Emmanuel Kwabena Opoku, Cynthia Laar, Ruby Eshun, Peter Donkor, Samuel Kofi Mensah, Ebenezer Kwadwo Siabi
abstract: Study region The Afram Plains South District, situated within Ghana’s Voltaian Basin. Study focus Groundwater is the mainstay of domestic supply in this district; however, many boreholes fail during extended dry spells. This study explored aquifer recharge sources and rates using hydrochemical signatures, stable water isotopes (δ 18ΟH2O, δ²HH2O) and the Chloride Mass Balance technique. Characterizing recharge processes of groundwater in this district is critical for guiding groundwater development and management in this hydrogeologically complex setting. New hydrological insights for the region: Isotope signatures point to a meteoric origin with less evaporative overprinting before recharge. Hydrochemically, three water types emerge: Sodium Chloride (Na-Cl or Na-HCO3-Cl), Sodium bicarbonate (Na-HCO3 -) and mixed water types dominated by Na+ and HCO3 -. Recharge estimates varied from 21.4 mm/yr to 284.5 mm/yr (1.7–22.8% of annual precipitation), averaging 132.0 mm/yr (10.6%). These rates resemble those reported from other Voltaian Basin studies employing both conventional and tracer-based techniques. The limited evaporative signature coupled with recharge estimates suggests these aquifers could support sustained abstraction; however, this requires integrated monitoring of groundwater levels, abstraction rates, storage capacity, and hydrodynamic properties. This integrated approach has proven valuable and could be employed for groundwater assessment where routine hydrological records are rare.

title: Diagnosing operational functional resilience of regional water networks: A pressure-structure-function-response framework
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yalin Zhang, Xin Li, Wenyan Wu, Guohua Fang
abstract: Study region Taizhou, a coastal city in southeastern China, has developed an interconnected regional water network linking multiple local sources, transfer corridors, and service areas. The system is exposed to variable water availability, growing demand, and potential capacity losses in key conveyance components. Study focus This study proposes a Pressure-Structure-Function-Response (PSFR) framework to diagnose the operational functional resilience of regional water networks. The framework integrates supply-demand pressure, directed network structure, capacity-reduction disturbances, service retention, post-disturbance reallocation, recovery, and residual shortage risk. It is applied to the Taizhou water network under three structural scenarios, five supply-demand pressure scenarios, and four disturbance levels to evaluate system-level resilience and component criticality. New hydrological insights for the region Network interconnection improves service coverage, alternative allocation routes, and reconfiguration capacity, thereby increasing operational functional resilience. However, these gains decline under dry-flow and high-demand conditions because source availability and downstream delivery interfaces become binding constraints. As the network becomes more interconnected, component criticality shifts from local water sources toward regional backbone transfer corridors, while terminal service links remain persistent bottlenecks. The PSFR framework therefore explains not only whether resilience changes, but also where recovery is constrained, providing a practical basis for network reinforcement, emergency water allocation, and resilience-oriented planning in regional water-supply systems.

title: Interprovincial trade reshapes the imbalance of water scarcity risks between source and sink regions: Empirical evidence based on dynamic complex network modeling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xin Feng, Jia Lu, Zhiang Li
abstract: Study region This study focuses on China's 30 provincial-level administrative regions, examining cross-provincial virtual water flows and their role in reshaping the spatial distribution of water scarcity risks. Study focus This study aims to investigate asymmetric water scarcity risks between source and sink regions under interprovincial virtual water flows from a risk transfer value perspective. Utilizing Multi-Regional Input-Output (MRIO) modeling, complex network analysis (CNA), and Temporal Exponential Random Graph Models (TERGM), a risk transfer value network is constructed to analyze its spatiotemporal evolution and underlying formation mechanisms. New hydrological insights for the region Interprovincial trade exhibits bifurcated pathway effects on water scarcity risks: high-value transfer paths mitigate regional disparities, whereas low-value pathways exacerbate imbalances between source and sink regions. The network displays a "core-periphery" structure, where core regions transfer risks through unidirectional "gradient" pathways, while peripheral regions alleviate water scarcity pressures through reciprocal alliances. Risk transfer patterns demonstrate path dependency, intensifying risk accumulation along low-value pathways and rendering traditional neighborhood-based governance ineffective. These insights highlight the need for an adaptive governance framework incorporating basin ecological compensation, industrial structure optimization, and cross-regional policy coordination to achieve equitable and sustainable water risk management across China's provinces.

title: Remote sensing-based water balance model to estimate the actual ET in Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xuerui Gao, Xiuping Li, Junhao Zhao, Ai Wang, Jiajun Chen, Shuyu Zhang
abstract: Study region The Loess Plateau in China, characterized by complex topography and heterogeneous underlying surfaces. Study focus Accurately simulating continuous AET over heterogeneous surfaces at the regional scale remains a major challenge. This study developed a remote sensing-based water balance assessment tool (RWBAT) that couples vertical soil water movement with sub-basin runoff generation and concentration. The model aims to resolve the spatiotemporal evolution of AET across the Loess Plateau's complex topography and land cover, providing continuous daily AET estimates at a 10 km spatial resolution as an alternative to coarse or temporally discontinuous remote sensing products. New hydrological insight Over the past 30 years, the mean AET on the Loess Plateau was 357.73 mm, showing a spatial pattern of gradual increase from northwest to southeast. AET exhibited a mutation around 2009 and a significant upward trend during 2017–2020. Although NDVI was positively correlated with AET, the response differed markedly by vegetation type: forest AET increased significantly across 94% of its area, whereas grassland showed a significant increase in only 28% of its area. Changes in farmland, shrubland, and wetland were mostly non‑significant. Notably, the upward AET trend emerged with a ~9‑year lag after the Grain for Green Project was launched around 2000, indicating that large‑scale afforestation—not grassland greening alone—drove the regional hydrological response, and that this effect was delayed rather than immediate.

title: Predicting streamflow in heavily regulated plain river networks using physics-guided spatiotemporal deep learning models: A case study of the Four Lakes Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yufeng Wu, Qingrui Chang, Zhihong Liu, Xianqiang Tang, Rui Li, Shouliang Huo
abstract: Study region The Four Lakes Basin is a typical agricultural plain river network subject to intensive regulation by artificial sluices and pumping stations. Study focus This study proposes a hybrid streamflow prediction model, SWAT-GNN-LSTM, that integrates physical processes with data-driven methods. Using SWAT-simulated hydrological states as physically informed boundary conditions, the model jointly extracts spatial topology and time-lag effects to infer and reconstruct regulated streamflow indirectly. New hydrological insights for the region (1) The model effectively mitigates peak-flow misalignment and extreme errors caused by intensive cross-boundary pumping and internal regulation, with average NSE values of 0.77 in validation and 0.66 in independent testing across six regulated nodes. (2) Ablation experiments confirm that the spatiotemporally coupled architecture successfully reconstructs the spatial transmission and routing delays of operation-related flow responses. (3) Feature sensitivity analysis shows that the contributions of wind speed, evapotranspiration, and temperature unexpectedly exceed that of precipitation, indicating a substantial shift in the dominant driving factors of the unnatural hydrological cycle under intensive agricultural water diversion. (4) Confidence intervals generated using MC Dropout quantitatively capture plausible streamflow fluctuations under typical flood-control operation periods, thereby objectively characterizing operational margins for decision-making. This study provides a reliable approach for streamflow simulation in complex regulated basins that lack fine-resolution operational data.

title: Spatial variability and associated factors of riverbed infiltration in two intermittent rivers in arid northwestern China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Linbo Qu, Haiyang Xi, Wenju Cheng, Yuqing Chen, Yulian Hao, Zhehui Wang, Shoushi Ma, Shuzhi Ji
abstract: Study region The Heihe and Xitugou Rivers, two intermittent rivers in arid northwestern China. Study focus In the Heihe and Xitugou Rivers, we integrated shallow soil measurements, tension infiltrometer tests, and depth-resolved ground penetrating radar (GPR) attributes to compare the spatial patterns of saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks), quantify the response of unsaturated hydraulic conductivity (Ku) to decreasing suction, and identify shallow and subsurface features associated with Ks. New hydrological insights for the region Ks ranged from 0.72 to 2.31 cm·min−1 in Heihe and from 0.73 to 1.14 cm·min−1 in Xitugou. Spatial variability was greater in Heihe, whereas Xitugou consistently had higher channel-centre than bank values. For each 1 cm WC increase in tension head toward 0 cm WC, Ku increased by 21.7% (95% CI, 9.0–35.9%) in Heihe and 21.2% (95% CI, 13.5–29.4%) in Xitugou. Structural differences were concentrated in shallow sediments. In Heihe, Ks was positively associated with the log-transformed particle-size ratio ln(P2/P3). Higher Ks also corresponded to lower log-envelope values at 5.5 and 7.5 m and more homogeneous GPR textures at 6–9 m. In Xitugou, no individual shallow-soil variable showed a stable association with Ks, whereas higher Ks corresponded to lower profile-mean relative energy across 1–9 m. Overall, Ks variability reflected river-specific combinations of shallow-soil conditions and subsurface GPR features.

title: Event-scale infiltration and subsurface moisture dynamics in a fractured hillslope monitored by time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Gang Zhang, Chien-Chih Chen, Cheng-Yang Yen
abstract: Study region The Touchih right-bank slope adjacent to the Liyutan Reservoir in central Taiwan is a structurally heterogeneous fractured rock hillslope in a humid subtropical setting. Historical instability and drainage interventions indicate spatially variable groundwater responses under rainfall forcing. Study focus This study investigates event-scale infiltration, moisture redistribution, and drainage using 510 quality-controlled hourly time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) profiles acquired during multiple rainfall events. Temporally constrained inversion results were used to derive normalized relative water saturation (RWS) indicators and observation-based metrics of response lag, spatial variability, and saturation persistence. Geological information and available hourly groundwater-level observations supported hydrological interpretation, while normalized depth-of-investigation assessment constrained the principal interpretation depth. New hydrological insights for the region Rainfall-related responses differ markedly among structural domains of the slope. Fracture-influenced zones exhibit rapid wetting followed by relatively rapid drainage and short moisture persistence, whereas relatively intact or storage-dominated zones show delayed responses and prolonged moisture retention. The continuously constrained model region extends predominantly to approximately 27–30 m depth, within which spatially coherent ERT/RWS responses provide field evidence of structurally influenced hydrological heterogeneity. These findings show that saturation persistence, together with response timing, provides useful process-oriented information for monitoring fractured hillslopes under humid subtropical rainfall conditions.

title: Water-balance-based daily evapotranspiration estimation over the Yangtze River Basin driven by reconstructed daily GRACE/GRACE-FO TWSA (2002–2023)
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chuqiao Li, Yulong Zhong, Lai Wei, Hongbing Bai, Xiaolong Li
abstract: Study region: Upper and middle reaches of the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), China. Study focus: This study reconstructed daily terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) from 2002 to 2023 using GRACE/GRACE-FO data combined with precipitation and temperature, and estimated daily evapotranspiration (ETWB) based on the water balance method. ETWB was compared with the Penman–Monteith–Leuning (PML) ET and Catchment Land Surface Model (CLSM) ET to evaluate its performance at different time scales and to analyze the response characteristics of water balance and energy-driven ET estimation methods. New hydrological insights for the region: ETWB inherits strong pulse signals from precipitation, introducing high-frequency noise. Low-pass filtering (Gaussian and Butterworth) significantly improves ETWB consistency with PML ET at multi-day scales, confirming its reliability for seasonal water resource assessment. In contrast, the original daily ETWB can correspond to the fast response characteristics of CLSM ET, while low-pass filtering smooths out these physically significant high-frequency signals. At the same time, there is also a phase reversal between the two. These findings indicate that ET estimation based on water balance and energy-driven have different response characteristics. The high-frequency uncertainty of the water balance method on a daily scale is a major limiting factor for accurately estimating daily evapotranspiration.

title: How interannual hydrological variability governs thermal stratification and selective withdrawal efficacy: Insights from the lower Lancang River cascade reservoirs
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hongshi Wu, Huqing Xu, Hongxue Zhang, Jianxia Chang, Lianpeng Zhang, Yimin Wang, Jinxi Li, Yige Wang, Junting Zhou
abstract: Study region The cascade reservoirs in the lower Lancang River, southwestern China. Study focus Natural river ecosystems rely on specific thermal regimes, which are frequently disrupted by deep reservoirs releasing cold hypolimnetic water. This study investigated how interannual hydrological variability controls thermal stratification, and how selective withdrawal via stoplog gates influences downstream thermal habitats and hydropower generation. By coupling a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model with a streamwise temperature model, the thermal dynamics were simulated. A systematic assessment was then conducted to compare the thermal habitat improvement and the hydropower losses between bottom-outlet operation and selective withdrawal. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicated persistent vertical stratification in the reservoir forebay across typical hydrological years, with a stable hypolimnion temperature of 15 °C and a distinct stratified regime from May to August. Utilizing multi-layer stoplog gates shifted withdrawal flows to warmer surface layers, raising downstream temperatures by a maximum of 8.34 °C. Moreover, the thermal guarantee rate for the spawning of the indicator species (Tor sinensis) increased from 14.29% to 66.67%. This thermal habitat improvement incurred negligible hydropower losses, yielding a 0.33% reduction in total generation and a 0.058% decrease in guaranteed output. These results confirmed that coupling selective withdrawal with cascade optimization effectively balances thermal habitat suitability and hydropower generation, providing information to support reservoir management in highly regulated river basins.

title: Towards resilience-informed urban flood risk management: An improved integrated approach considering coupling effects between risk and resilience
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Jiaxuan Zheng, Guangheng Ni, Guoru Huang, Fuqiang Tian
abstract: Study region Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region Study focus Understanding urban flood risk-resilience relationships facilitates the shift from defense-oriented to resilience-informed risk management, which is essential for building resilient cities. However, existing studies primarily treat risk and resilience as independent dimensions and overlook their coupling effects, limiting identifications of areas with urgent needs and greater potential for coordinated enhancement of resilience and risk mitigation under differentiated management. This often leads to an overemphasis on high-risk-low-resilience areas while neglecting other priority areas. Building on conventional analytical frameworks that examine spatial patterns, numerical values, and spatial correlations, this study advances resilience-informed risk management by explicitly incorporating risk-resilience coupling effects. The improved approach is applied to the BTH region, a flood-prone urban system facing increasing threats from extreme events, over the period 2010–2020. Priority areas are identified and implications for resilience-informed risk management are discussed. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicate that the BTH region has been characterized by low risk but low resilience. Targeted measures should be prioritized in areas with low coupling coordination but a relatively high degree of coupling. These areas are extended from being limited to high-risk-low-resilience areas to encompass those within Medium-Low, High-Very Low, High-Low, High-Medium, High-High, Very High-Very Low, Very High-Low, Very High-Medium, and Very High-High risk-resilience classes. Routine risk management considering coupling effects can reveal potential vulnerability under extreme events.

title: Dual-mode geochemical evolution of geothermal fluids across strike-slip and pull-apart segments of the Ganzi–Litang fault, eastern Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Sihang Han, Chuanzhi Liao, Shu Hu, Yuxiang Lu, Luyu Zou, Xingyi Cai, Zhiwu Li, Guangzheng Jiang
abstract: Study region The Ganzi–Litang fault zone (GLFZ), the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau. Study focus Fault segmentation can govern the circulation and geochemical evolution of geothermal fluids, but the contrasting effects of strike-slip and pull-apart structures along plateau-margin fault zones remain insufficiently quantified. We compiled 58 water and isotope samples and 28 gas samples from the GLFZ and integrated Self-Organizing Map (SOM) classification with H–O–Sr–He–C isotopic tracing, reservoir-temperature estimation, and volatile-source apportionment to evaluate segment-specific controls on recharge, water–rock interaction, mixing, and degassing. New hydrological insights for the region Geothermal fluid evolution along the GLFZ reflects a dual-mode, segment-dependent geochemical pattern. The SOM analysis categorized the geothermal waters into three hydrochemical groups, revealing both segment-related geochemical patterns and a cross-segment shallow-circulation group. In the northern Ganzi strike-slip segment, the Group 2 geochemical signature is best explained by laterally coherent deep-circulation conduits in a granitic reservoir, yielding partial-to-full water–rock equilibrium and reservoir temperatures of 200–230 °C. In the southern Xinlong–Litang pull-apart segment, fluids (Group 1 and Group 3) are more strongly diluted by shallow cold water (57–81%) and record lower deep thermal end-member temperatures, of 140–170 °C, multi-lithological water–rock interaction, and spatially localized He–CO₂ anomalies. The geochemical patterns suggest that the northern strike-slip segment favors stable, long-residence deep circulation, whereas the southern pull-apart segment is characterized by stronger shallow mixing and localized deep-volatile anomalies. The results provide a regional framework for segment-specific geothermal development and the protection of alpine water resources in composite fault zones.

title: Physics-guided Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for extreme flood and drought flow prediction: A case study of the Upper Hanjiang River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xiaodong Li, Jieliang Guo, Yicong Dai, Tiesheng Guan, Xin Yin, Feng Wang
abstract: Study Region: Upper Hanjiang River Basin (UHRB), headwater catchment of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, China. Study Focus: Daily flow prediction underpins water resources management, yet existing deep learning methods struggle to reproduce hydrological extremes. This study proposes Deep Process Learning-Long Short-term Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (DPL-LSTKAN). Specifically, DPL-LSTKAN captures the temporal evolution of meteorological forcings and employs Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) to represent the intrinsic dependencies between meteorological forcings and runoff. Decoupled learning scheme is adopted to separately characterize extreme and normal flow regimes. In addition, Physics-guided gating mechanism dynamically assigns predictor weights according to the dominant hydrological processes. DPL-LSTKAN is applied to flow prediction in the UHRB, with particular focus on its accuracy and physical consistency under extreme floods and droughts. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: In the UHRB, hydrological extremes are controlled by antecedent catchment wetness rather than instantaneous rainfall, most strongly by soil water storage ( r = 0.59 ). Flood and drought follow distinct mechanisms: fastflow responds near-monotonically to precipitation via saturation-excess pathways, whereas baseflow scales with subsurface storage and declines toward zero during dry spells. Because fastflow is released only as storage approaches capacity, a saturation onset precedes flood peaks, reproducing peak timing within one day ( PTE = 0.83 day ) while suppressing implausible low-flow errors. These controls support reservoir scheduling, flood warning, and ecological-flow management.

title: Local factors or large-scale circulation? An investigation on controls for precipitation isotopes in a coastal monsoonal region, North China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chengcheng Xia, Junxi Lin, Tao Zhang, Wen Liu, Xiong Xiao, Junbing Pu
abstract: Study region Yellow River Delta (YRD), north China. Study focus Based on event-scale precipitation samples collected over three complete hydrological years at the Gudao site in the YRD, this study systematically analyzed the temporal variation characteristics of stable hydrogen and oxygen isotopes (δD, δ18O) in precipitation. We evaluated the influences of local meteorological factors and large-scale atmospheric circulation on isotopic variability, and explored the lagged regulatory effect of equatorial Pacific sea surface temperature anomalies (SSTA, indicated by the Niño 3 index) on precipitation isotopes between the monsoon and non-monsoon seasons. New hydrological insights The controls on precipitation isotopes at the Gudao site in the YRD present significant seasonal differences. Local meteorological factors play a major role in the non-monsoon season, explaining approximately 41% of the δ18O variation. In the monsoon season, isotopic characteristics are largely associated with the upstream rainout effect along moisture transport pathways from the Indian Ocean and western Pacific. Monsoon-season δ18O has a significant positive correlation with the Niño 3 index at a 2-month lag (r = 0.60, p < 0.05), suggesting a potential lagged modulation of equatorial Pacific SSTA on regional precipitation isotopes. These results provide new observational evidence for understanding seasonal isotopic variations and a scientific basis for interpreting isotopic records and paleoclimate reconstruction in this coastal monsoonal setting.

title: A LSTM reservoir outflow model enhanced by operation chart derives the representative reservoir operation schemes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Runting Chen, Dagang Wang, Yiwen Mei, Yongen Lin, Jinxin Zhu, Xiaoxing Qi
abstract: Study region The Xinfengjiang Reservoir in the Dongjiang River Basin, China, is a large multi-year regulating reservoir whose outflows are strongly influenced by human operation. Study focus To represent the impact of reservoir operation on streamflow dynamics, this study develops a knowledge-guided Long Short-Term Memory (KG-LSTM) model to simulation reservoir outflow. Empirical rules derived from reservoir operation chart are extracted using Classification and Regression Trees and embedded into the loss function of the standard LSTM. To further extract reservoir operation insights, KG-LSTM is further combined with an interpretability framework integrating Shapley Additive exPlanations, t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, and k-means clustering. New hydrological insights for the region The KG-LSTM achieves superior performance compared with the standard LSTM, indicating that incorporating empirical reservoir operation knowledge improves the reservoir outflow simulation. More importantly, the interpretability analysis identifies previous-month outflow as the most influential factor in current outflow determination. In particular, current inflow tends to contribute negatively to outflow during the flood season, supporting impoundment, but positively during the dry season, supporting water replenishment. Furthermore, the interpretability framework identifies six representative and situation-dependent operation schemes, which correspond to three major reservoir functions: impoundment, power generation, and water replenishment. Overall, this study provides a framework that enhances both accuracy and interpretability of data-driven reservoir modeling, offering a new avenue for operation knowledge extraction and validation.

title: Modeling hydrological responses to land-use changes associated with coal-mining subsidence: A watershed-scale PLUS–SWAT analysis
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Pingjia Luo, Yijun Jiang, Qinghe Hou, Yufan Wu, Shiyuan Zhou, Hao Chen, Li Wang
abstract: Study region Baima River watershed, Jining, China, a high-water-table region affected by underground coal mining subsidence. Study focus To quantify the hydrological responses to land-use changes associated with coal-mining subsidence, the PLUS and SWAT models were coupled to simulate hydrological responses under four future land-use scenarios: natural development, urbanization, wetland conservation, and land reclamation. New hydrological insights for the region Historical data (1990–2020) indicated a structural shift from cultivated land to construction land and subsidence-induced wetlands. Future projections showed increased surface runoff (SURQ, by up to 6.51% annually) and reduced groundwater contribution to streamflow (GWQ, by up to 9.72% annually), especially under urbanization. These deviations were concentrated during the main wet season and subsequent recession months. Across the selected return-period rainfall events, urbanization and wetland-conservation-oriented land-use change increased mean seven-day cumulative surface runoff (SURQ-7d) by 3.39% and 3.06%, respectively, whereas land reclamation produced the smallest departure from the baseline scenario. Sub-basin differences often exceeded basin-average scenario responses, indicating that watershed-scale results represent integrated scenario effects while mining-affected sub-basins can exhibit stronger localized responses. These findings support zoning-based management that combines suitable land reclamation with the conservation of stable subsidence wetlands.

title: Analysis of drought-flood abrupt alternation in China from 1981 to 2024
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yifan Li, Weiwei Shao, Jiahong Liu, Jia Wang, Zhuoran Luo
abstract: Study region The study encompasses the entire territory of China, which has been classified into seven climate regions. Study focus This study developed the daily-scale Standardized Drought-Wet Abrupt Alternation Index (SDWAI) to identify and assess Drought-Flood Abrupt Alternation (DFAA) events. Using the modified Mann-Kendall method, Sen’s slope estimator, the moving t-test, the spatiotemporal trends and evolutionary features of DFAA events across China were systematically examined. New hydrological insights for the region: This study found that during 1981–2024, the DFAA events exhibited distinct regional and seasonal characteristics at both interannual and annual scales, with a significantly increasing frequency, featuring a spatial pattern of high frequency in the southeast and low in the northwest, and summer witnessed the most frequent and severe events. A shared mutation occurring in 1991 and 1992 showed a national wet shift, interannual variability and spatial coverage of DFAA expanded, and the high-frequency areas showed characteristics of northward movement and southward expansion after each mutation. The gradient of spatial anomaly percentage of average precipitation showed moderate and less significant correlation with frequency, acting as a potential influential factor. Meanwhile, a preliminary national threshold of ±0.6 is proposed for application across different arid and humid regions.

title: Event-based 3D tracking of multi-type drought propagation in Xinjiang’s Mountain-Oasis-Desert system
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Liutianjiao Hong, Jianzhu Li, Ping Feng, Ting Zhang, Fulong Chen, Xinwang Li
abstract: Study region Xinjiang (XJ), located in northwestern China, is a prototypical arid region characterized by a coupled Mountain-Oasis-Desert (MOD) system. Study focus Conventional 2D analyses cannot fully capture the 3D spatiotemporal dynamics or complete propagation chains of multi-type droughts in arid MOD systems. To address this limitation, we used SPEI, SRI, SSMI, and SEDI to characterize meteorological (MD), hydrological (HD), agricultural (AD), and ecological droughts (ED), respectively, and developed an event-based 3D framework integrating spatiotemporal connectivity clustering with directed acyclic graph (DAG) network analysis. The framework tracks the growth, migration, and dissipation of drought events while reconstructing synchronous and lagged cross-type propagation linkages across XJ during 1960–2024. New hydrological insights for the region A total of 231 3D drought events were identified, including 55 MD, 61 HD, 83 AD, and 32 ED events; collectively, they exhibited functional-zone clustering and centroid-based directional migration, with trajectories broadly aligned with the terrain-river-oasis landscape configuration. DAG analysis revealed 43 propagation event groups, dominated by the linear cascading mode (56%), with parallel and complex modes accounting for 21% and 23%, respectively. Propagation exhibited path-dependent lag structures and asymmetric cross-system coupling, whereas network topology became more complex after 2000. Furthermore, drought propagation sensitivity showed a distinct tripartite spatial pattern: northern XJ was dominated by atmospheric forcing (P Atmo =24.1%), southern XJ by hydro-agricultural feedback (P Nexus ≈20%), and eastern XJ by the highest ecological response sensitivity (P Eco =14%). These findings establish an event-based 3D network perspective for regional drought analysis and provide new insights into nonlinear propagation mechanisms in arid MOD systems.

title: Seasonal divergence in GPP- and ET-pathway regulation of ecosystem water use efficiency across vegetation types in water-limited ecosystems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xiang Li, Kangle Mo, Guodong Jia, Lixin Chen, Zhiqiang Zhang
abstract: Study region The Loess Plateau, China, encompassing grassland, cropland, shrubland and forest ecosystems. Study focus Ecosystem water-use efficiency (eWUE) reflects carbon–water coupling, yet how environmental effects are transmitted through the carbon (GPP) and water (ET) fluxes remains poorly resolved in water-limited regions. We addressed this across the Loess Plateau (2001–2019) at sub-kilometer resolution, combining a spatial random forest, partial-derivative decomposition and conditional probability ratio (CPR) analysis to resolve vegetation-specific controls, their GPP- and ET-mediated pathways and extreme responses. New hydrological insights for the region eWUE was highest in autumn (1.39 gC·m⁻²·mm⁻¹) and lowest and largely stable in spring (1.08 gC·m⁻²·mm⁻¹; 77.34% of pixels with non-significant trend). eWUE extremes were primarily associated with VPD and DSR in spring and summer but shrublands in summer (CPR = 2.14–3.86). Pathway attribution was driver-specific rather than a uniform seasonal switch. Environmental effects were mostly transmitted through ET (f ET = 0.55–0.94) in spring. In summer, VPD shifted to GPP-mediation in all vegetation types (f GPP = 0.56–0.85), whereas AW remained ET-mediated (f ET = 0.52–0.68). DSR and PRE diverged by vegetation type, GPP-mediated in herbaceous but ET-mediated in woody ecosystems. AW switched to GPP-mediation only in autumn (f GPP = 0.55–0.90). Our findings provide a mechanistic basis for predicting eWUE responses to climate variability.

title: Nonstationary flood frequency analysis and drivers in the middle-lower Yangtze River, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chen Xu, Zhouhui Huang, Anqi Wang, Yang Xiao, Taotao Zhang, Hua Qin, Zihao Guo
abstract: Study region The middle–lower Yangtze River Basin, China, represented by four hydrological stations: Yichang, Luoshan, Hankou, and Datong. Study focus This study investigates nonstationary flood frequency and climatic and anthropogenic drivers under changing environmental conditions. Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) were used to model annual flood peaks to assess the effects of atmospheric and terrestrial covariates, by incorporating antecedent precipitation, flood-season temperature, large-scale climate indices, and reservoir regulation as physically interpretable covariates. New hydrological insights Flood-frequency nonstationarity exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity along the middle–lower Yangtze River. Statistically significant nonstationarity is identified at Yichang, Luoshan, and Hankou Stations, whereas Datong Station shows neither a significant monotonic trend nor a significant change point during the study period. An empirically selected 27–28-day antecedent precipitation window, flood-season maximum temperature (TMAX), the modified reservoir index (MRI), and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) improve the representation of nonstationary flood-frequency distributions. Reservoir regulation is more strongly associated with flood-frequency variation at Yichang Station, whereas antecedent precipitation and ENSO become increasingly prominent at the lower part of Luoshan and Hankou Stations. Nonstationary models indicate that flood quantiles generally increase with antecedent precipitation and with El Niño conditions in the preceding winter–spring but decrease with stronger reservoir regulation. Seasonally accumulated TMAX shows heterogeneous quantile effects, suggesting possibly different thermal associations between ordinary and extreme flood conditions.

title: A hybrid model integrating baseflow dynamics and ensemble deep learning for ecological flow process monitoring and early warning
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Haodong Qiu, Tian Jin, Yukun Wang, Jiaqi Tan, Chuyu Xu, Yu Qiao, Hao Chen, Saihua Huang, Yue-Ping Xu, Yuxue Guo, Hui Nie
abstract: Study region The Xitiaoxi River Basin, a highly regulated river network in eastern China's Taihu Lake Basin, was studied using daily hydrological and meteorological data (2012–2023) from five control stations. Study focus This study develops a dynamic framework for ecological flow monitoring and tiered early warning, addressing the limitations of static thresholds and the lack of predictive capacity. Baseflow was separated using the Lyne–Hollick digital filter, hydrological stages were delineated via Fisher's optimal segmentation, and stage-specific ecological flow thresholds were derived from baseflow frequency analysis using the Qp90 (90% exceedance probability) criterion. An ensemble deep learning model, incorporating precipitation, evaporation, baseflow index, reservoir releases, and antecedent hydrological conditions, was built to forecast ecological flow status up to 5 days ahead. Based on predicted flow deficits relative to thresholds, a four-level warning system was established. New hydrological insights for the region Results reveal pronounced seasonal variability in ecological flow requirements, with higher thresholds during the flood season, lower thresholds during dry periods, and intermediate thresholds during transitional stages. The pre-flood period, dry season, and ecologically sensitive stages are most vulnerable to deficits. The model achieved an average test accuracy of 89.69% over 1–5-day lead times and 84.51% at a 5-day lead time. For red warnings, precision and recall reached 91.55% and 89.08%, respectively, indicating high reliability in detecting severe deficits. This framework provides a sound scientific basis for adaptive water resources and ecological flow management in hydrologically complex river network regions.

title: Impacts of warming-induced precipitation phase shifts on soil erosion over the Qinghai-Tibet plateau
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Heng Zhao, Mengcheng Guo, Fuqiang Wang, Wenjing Huang, Huan Yang, Jiageng Hu, Lanbo Cui, Yimei Cheng
abstract: Study region The study covers the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), where climate warming is shifting precipitation from solid to liquid forms, potentially altering soil erosion risk. Study focus We estimated erosion using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation, quantified phase change with the rainfall ratio to precipitation (RRP), characterized event-scale intensity by the maximum 60-min intensity (I 60 ), and identified dominant drivers using an interpretable XGBoost-SHAP framework. New hydrological insights for the region RRP increased across most of the QTP, but its linkage with rainfall erosivity was strongly season-dependent, with the closest coupling occurring in autumn (ρ = 0.683, p < 0.001). At the interannual scale, RRP was positively correlated with I 60 (ρ = 0.710, p < 0.001), while I 60 was also positively associated with rainfall erosivity (ρ = 0.647, p = 0.002), indicating a process linkage among precipitation-phase shifts, short-duration rainfall intensity, and erosive forcing. Rainfall (38.4%) and slope (27.2%) remained the primary controls on spatial erosion heterogeneity, whereas RRP (7.8%) acted as a secondary regulator. Erosion responses shifted markedly across 4500–5500 m, where vegetation buffering weakened and sensitivity to precipitation-phase variability increased. These findings improve understanding of how precipitation-phase shifts and event-scale intensity shape erosive forcing, while supporting elevation-specific soil conservation under continued warming.

title: Characterizing spatiotemporal dynamics of hourly extreme precipitation in China with an adaptive 3D clustering approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yijia Wu, Sijia Ke, Chunyu Zhang, Han Zhou
abstract: Study region China, spanning the East Asian monsoon region and its northwestern inland transition zones, where extreme precipitation events (EPEs) show strong spatial heterogeneity and pose substantial hydrological-disaster risks. Study focus This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and propagation patterns of EPEs across China during 1985–2024. The central objective is to move beyond station-based, two-dimensional, or daily-scale descriptions and reconstruct complete precipitation-system trajectories in a continuous three-dimensional space. To achieve this, an adaptive 3D spatiotemporal clustering framework based on 3D-DBSCAN was developed and applied to ERA5 hourly precipitation data. Extreme precipitation grids were mapped into a standardized longitude-latitude-time space, while k-distance-based parameter optimization and physical constraint filtering were used to reduce subjective parameter selection and avoid artificial fragmentation of fast-moving or intermittent events. Precipitation-weighted centroids were then used to quantify event movement distance and direction, and to classify typical propagation patterns. New hydrological insights for the region The framework identified independent EPEs and revealed five dominant propagation patterns. EPEs in China show a clear northwestward movement preference, whereas southward events are infrequent and spatially limited. Northwestward events, especially ultra-long-distance events, exhibit the greatest hydrological extremeness, with longer durations, larger affected areas, and higher cumulative magnitudes. These trajectories indicate a regional “westward shift and northward leap” of extreme-rainfall activity, linked to the East Asian summer monsoon, western Pacific subtropical high, and mid-latitude westerlies.

title: Spatial structure and evolution of meteorological droughts using an intensity-field framework: A multi-timescale analysis across China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yaqi Sun, Jiejun Huang, Ximing Chen, Yanbin Yuan, Han Zhou
abstract: Study area China Study focus Accurately characterizing the spatial structure of drought is crucial for understanding drought propagation and risk assessment. Existing approaches overlook intensity effects on spatial dynamics. In this study, we propose a framework for measuring spatial extents (SPEs) of meteorological droughts that incorporates drought intensity fields (DIF). Based on the principles of spatial autocorrelation and anisotropy, we apply a semivariogram-based method to quantify the coupling between intensity and spatiotemporal structure. We quantify the climatological SPEs of meteorological droughts in China using multi-timescale (1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month) SPI derived from four high-resolution precipitation datasets (ERA5, PERSIANN-CDR, GPM, and TRMM), and analyze the spatial morphological structure and spatiotemporal evolution patterns. New hydrological insights for the regions The results show that: (1) The DIF-based method provides more accurate estimates of drought SPEs. It effectively reduces the biases inherent in the binary approach; (2) SPEs expand with increasing timescale, accompanied by an enhancement in the heterogeneity and uncertainty of spatial structure. High-impact drought areas show a southward migration trend; (3) SPEs in humid regions expand significantly at mid-term to long-term timescales, indicating the need for close monitoring of long-term drought risks in southern China. The proposed framework improves the understanding of drought spatiotemporal dynamics. It also supports research on drought migration and propagation, and provides important insights for drought monitoring, prediction, and water resource management.

title: Assessing occurrences, transformations, and source apportionment of nitrate in a riverine area (Southwestern China) using multi-parameter approaches
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhan Xie, Yunhui Zhang, Denghui Wei, Haidong Li, Lanchu Tao, Qingsong Chen, Juan Antonio Torres-Martínez, Rongwen Yao, Yangshuan Wang, Ying Wang
abstract: Study region Luolouhe (LLH) catchment in the western Yungui Plateau of southwestern China Study focus Investigating the transformation pathways and source apportionment of nitrate in regional riverine systems remains challenging due to spatial variations in topography, hydrogeology, and land use patterns. Thus, stable isotopes, the Bayesian stable isotope mixing model (MixSIAR), positive matrix factorization (PMF), and local indicators of spatial association (LIAS) were applied to elucidate the sources and contributions of nitrate (NO3 –). New hydrological insights for the region High NO3 – concentrations in surface water and groundwater were observed in the alluvial terrace in the LLH catchment. Nitrification was identified as the predominant biochemical process in both water bodies. Two water bodies in our study presented different nitrate sources. Nitrate source contributions ranked as domestic sewage and manure (DSM) (54.00% by SIAR and 62.15% by PMF)> chemical fertilizer (CF) (27.00% by SIAR and 25.51% by PMF)> soil nitrogen (SN) (17.70% by SIAR and 12.30% by PMF) in surface water. For groundwater, nitrate sources ranked as SN (52.40%)> CF (27.30%) > DSM (19.20%) by SIAR, while ranked as SN (58.74%)> DSM (21.43%)> CF (19.65%) by PMF. The non-perfect sewage discharge facilities and the surface runoff contributed to the nitrate sources in surface water. SN dominated the nitrate source due to the high background levels of nitrate in the soil profile. A proportion of nitrate fertilizer was transported into rivers while the rest percolated through the unsaturated zone and accumulated in the groundwater. The soil nitrate input hotspots identified by LISA further illustrated the spatial heterogeneity of the nitrification process. The hotspots scattered in the lower reach indicated an intense nitrification process in this region, facilitated by favorable oxidation conditions. Overall, this study enhances nitrate source apportionment methodologies and provides novel insights into the spatial variability of biochemical processes influencing nitrate concentrations at a regional scale.

title: Mechanistic drivers and spatiotemporal thresholds of socioeconomic drought in the East River Basin, China: A causal-informed explainable AI approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Fangxiu Meng, Huazhou Chen, Yao Wang, Rong Wu, Lin Liu, Tao Tang, Shengzhi Huang, Jianfeng Li, Suning Liu, Haiyun Shi
abstract: Study region The East River Basin (ERB), a critical water source for South China’s mega-cities. Study focus To address data scarcity and the predictive collapse of traditional models during extreme deficits, this study develops an integrated diagnostic-predictive framework for the Distributed Standardized Socioeconomic Drought Index (DSSEDI). High-fidelity DSSEDI forecasting (maintaining a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.774 during extreme deficits) is achieved by leveraging accessible multi-source data, overcoming sector-specific monitoring constraints. By coupling a Causal Convolutional Transformer with Shapley Additive Explanations, the framework ensures physical consistency through dual-causal constraints. Crucially, incorporating a quantile regression loss function ( q = 0.5 ) significantly outperforms Mean Squared Error-based models in capturing non-Gaussian extreme drought peaks. New hydrological insights This analysis reveals the underlying socioeconomic drought mechanisms in the ERB, which exhibits a persistent climate memory characterized by 10- to 11-month hydrometeorological lags. A critical finding is the identification of a soil moisture paradox, where high antecedent moisture paradoxically accelerates drought development via enhanced evapotranspiration under urban heat island stress. Furthermore, the modeling framework implicitly diagnoses Xinfengjiang Reservoir regulation and exposes a pronounced socioeconomic antagonism, demonstrating that rigid industrial demand acts as a persistent drought amplifier. Distinct soil moisture inflection points (750 mm for urban and 600 mm for agricultural zones) are identified as scientific triggers for adaptive management. These findings establish a threshold-driven governance paradigm for enhancing drought resilience in urbanizing regional basins.

title: Lakeshore transformation and water color dynamics: A satellite-based 23-year assessment of nine plateau lakes in Yunnan, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yuchen Wang, Yongquan Zhao, Xuejun Duan, Xiao Zhang, Xunyi Pan
abstract: Study region Nine plateau lakes in Yunnan, China. Study focus We developed an extended lakeshore utilization classification framework to categorize lakeshores as natural, agricultural, or artificial using fixed maximum shorelines. We then derived the Forel–Ule Index (FUI) of the nine lakes from MODIS to characterize water color dynamics during 2000–2022. We quantified lakeshore composition and transformation trajectories, assessed FUI trends, and examined contemporaneous and one- and two-year lagged lakeshore–FUI associations. New hydrological insights for the region Lakeshore classification achieved 98.8% overall accuracy. Four lakes exhibit intensification, two show adjustment, and three remain relative stable. Artificial lakeshore increases from 29.1% to 45.2% in Erhai, while agricultural lakeshore increases from 36.3% to 73.5% in Chenghai. Significant upward FUI trends occur in Erhai, Chenghai, Yangzong, and Xingyun, whereas Lugu exhibits a downward trend and the other lakes show no significant trends. Contemporaneous lakeshore–FUI associations is significant for natural and artificial lakeshore in Erhai and Lugu and for agricultural lakeshore in Yilong, with none supported elsewhere. The lagged analysis shows that five lakeshore–FUI associations strengthen and five weaken. These contrasting responses indicate that lakeshore transformation alone does not determine water color dynamics, which is conditioned by lake-specific environmental and anthropogenic contexts. The proposed framework supports integrated lakeshore and water color monitoring and coordinated lake–watershed management in Yunnan and comparable lake systems.

title: System-scale hydraulic trade-offs of dredging in confined urban rivers: Insights from the Tamsui basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Wan-Cheng Chen, Gene Jiing-Yun You, Gwo-wen Hwang, Jen-Yang Lin, Yu-Ju Hung
abstract: Study Region This study focuses on the Tamsui River Basin in northern Taiwan, a densely urbanized river system with limited channel expansion capacity and an extensive levee-floodway network designed for a 200-year flood standard. Study Focus This study evaluates dredging as a maintenance-based strategy for sustaining fixed flood-protection thresholds in space-constrained urban rivers where flood mitigation depends on coupled main-channel and floodway performance. A system-scale assessment using two-dimensional hydrodynamic and sediment-transport modeling examines how alternative dredging configurations influence hydraulic loading, diversion performance, and sediment adjustment under a representative 50-year flood event, with evaluation focused on a major urban bottleneck, the floodway inlet, and the downstream mainstem outlet. New Hydrological Insights for the Region The results show that dredging progressively alleviates hydraulic loading at the primary urban bottleneck, with greater relief achieved under more extensive interventions. However, simulations demonstrate that increased main-channel conveyance can reduce floodway diversion by weakening the hydraulic head driving bifurcation flow, confirming a diversion-conveyance trade-off in urban flood-routing systems. Sediment responses are strongly location-dependent, with rapid re-accumulation in confined metropolitan reaches and persistent scouring in the downstream mainstem. Together, these coupled hydraulic and sediment responses indicate that maintaining fixed flood-protection thresholds through maintenance-based dredging becomes increasingly difficult in space-constrained urban rivers.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and mechanisms of mountain-outlet runoff change on the northern slope of the Qilian Mountains during 1960–2020
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yuchen Wei, Meiping Sun, Xiaojun Yao, Shu Wang, Rongjun Wang, Shuting Niu
abstract: Study region Five major mountain-outlet basins on the northern slope of the Qilian Mountains, northwestern China: Shiyang (SY), Heihe (HH), Beida (BD), Shule (SL), and Danghe (DH). Study focus This study examines the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of mountain-outlet runoff changes during 1960–2020 and their statistically associated pathways using hydrological, meteorological, atmospheric circulation, glacier, and snow data. OPGD and PLS-SEM were used to identify dominant explanatory factors and statistical pathways linking atmospheric circulation, meteorological factors, glacier and snow water storage (GSWS), and runoff (Q). New hydrological insights for the region Mean runoff in 2000–2020 was 2.8–58.8% higher than in 1960–1999, while basin-specific abrupt-change years ranged from 1987 to 2009. Long-term increasing trends were significant only in HH, SL, and DH. Air temperature and precipitation were the main meteorological factors associated with runoff variation. Runoff in SY and HH was more closely associated with precipitation, whereas runoff in SL and DH was more closely associated with air temperature, and both factors had similar explanatory power in BD. Atmospheric circulation was statistically linked to runoff through air temperature, precipitation, and GSWS. The precipitation → Q pathway was stronger in SY, HH, and BD, whereas the air temperature → GSWS → Q pathway was more prominent in SL and DH. These findings help explain region-specific runoff heterogeneity and support differentiated water resources management.

title: Runoff response to terrace construction, vegetation restoration, and urban expansion: Case studies in the Yiluo and Upper Wei River basins
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Mingjie Yang, Yuanhong Liu, Peng Zhang, Saihua Liu, Lianqing Xue, Tao Lin
abstract: Study region This study investigates two typical semi-arid loess watersheds in China, the Yiluo River Basin and Upper Wei River Basin, where terrace renovation, vegetation restoration, and urbanization have substantially altered watershed hydrological processes. Study focus Conventional SWAT-based land-use studies often apply extreme land-use scenarios and oversimplify landscape heterogeneity. Terraces are treated as static BMPs with fixed Curve Number (CN), ignoring rainfall-driven CN variations and lowering simulation accuracy in terrace-dominated loess regions. This study uses realistic spatial land-use configurations instead of extreme scenarios and improves SWAT via slope-based terrace delineation and rainfall-intensity-dependent dynamic-CN calibration to evaluate land-use hydrological impacts and the conditional applicability of dynamic CN. New hydrological insights for the region The 2000 land-use dataset yields the best model performance (NSE = 0.8837, R² = 0.8865, PBIAS = −7.83%), superior to 2010 and 2020 datasets. Grassland expansion reduces runoff by 12.97%, much higher than the 2.49% from forest expansion, and urban expansion produces unstable interannual runoff responses. The dynamic-CN method improves daily-runoff simulation under drought and heavy-rainfall conditions, whereas static CN works better under mild stable rainfall. Terraces redistribute surface runoff into subsurface flow and baseflow with little impact on annual total runoff.

title: Potential of source-reservoir thermal regulation to alleviate low-temperature constraints on winter water conveyance in the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Lijin Liu, Xu Zhang, Youcai Tuo, Yun Deng, Fan Yang
abstract: Study region The main canal of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, China, one of the world’s largest long-distance interbasin water transfer systems. Study focus Winter low-temperature conditions and ice hazards constrain the winter water conveyance capacity of long-distance water transfer canals, yet the role of source reservoirs in regulating downstream thermal conditions remains unclear. This study developed and validated a winter water temperature model for the main canal, achieving RMSE values below 0.6°C and R² values above 0.9. Scenario experiments were conducted to assess how source-reservoir water-level rise and increased diversion discharge affect longitudinal heat transport and low-temperature constraints at the canal tail. New hydrological insights for the region The Danjiangkou Reservoir acts as an active thermal regulation node rather than only a water-supply boundary. Increased diversion discharge enhanced heat transport efficiency, reduced the longitudinal temperature gradient by 19%, and shifted the 14°C isotherm 404.8 km northward. Reservoir water-level rise strengthened the headwork thermal boundary and mainly improved near-source thermal conditions. Under suitable discharge, reservoir-induced thermal gains could reach the canal tail about 1200 km downstream. Joint regulation reduced 0–4 °C low-temperature days at BJM by 12–24%, indicating its potential to alleviate low-temperature constraints and support further evaluation of winter water conveyance capacity.

title: A progressive early warning system for flash drought based on meteorological precursors: A case study of the Dongjiang River Basin, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Qiang Huang, Lan Kong, Shaofeng Li, Shuyun Yuan, Xiaoshan Luo, Liao Ouyang, Peng Li
abstract: Study region The Dongjiang River Basin in southeast China, a critical water source region for the Pearl River Delta with a subtropical monsoon climate and frequent dry–wet transitions. Study focus Flash droughts threaten water and food security due to rapid onset, yet operational warnings remain largely single-indicator based. This study developed a progressive early warning system using pentad-scale ERA5-Land root-zone soil moisture (1950–2025). Precursors were screened through collinearity diagnosis, time-lag correlation, and random forest importance, followed by Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis, with predictive skill quantified by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) to determine warning thresholds within a two-stage regression-to-classification framework. New hydrological insights for the region Five precursors spanning three pentads prior to onset were identified. A two-pentad-ahead precipitation anomaly (P lag2, AUC = 0.74) and a one-pentad-ahead anomaly (P lag1, AUC = 0.92) formed the main warning chain, issuing L1 and L2 alerts 2 and 1 pentads ahead, respectively. Three weaker precursors (P lag3, ET/PET lag3, T lag2; all AUC ≈ 0.5) were integrated into a three-category supporting-condition score (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH). The system achieved a false positive rate of 6.3% (training) and 8.5% (validation), substantially lower than single-indicator (16.5%–18.6%) and logistic regression (16.3%–22.3%) baselines, with a higher Heidke Skill Score (0.370 vs. 0.262–0.269). Results were robust across 10 flash drought definition parameter combinations, and application to the 2019 event demonstrated timely, coherent warnings with no false alarms.

title: Contrasting roles of human water use in soil and hydrological drought propagation in the mid-upper Huaihe River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yiting Zou, Xing Yuan, Chenyuan Li
abstract: Study region The mid-upper Huaihe River Basin (MU-HRB) in China is a region characterized by strong climate variability and intensive human water use. Study focus This study examines how irrigation and reservoir regulation influence drought propagation (DP) from meteorological drought (MD) to soil drought (SD) and hydrological drought (HD) over the MU-HRB. The newly developed Conjunctive Surface Subsurface Process model version 3 (CSSPv3) with explicit representation of irrigation water source constraints, is applied to quantify the impacts of human water use on DP. The CSSPv3 model outperforms global hydrological models in terms of streamflow and soil moisture simulations over the MU-HRB. New hydrological insights for the region Human water use alters DP by modifying both pathways and thresholds. Irrigation suppresses SD, reducing its frequency by 58.8% and prolonging propagation time by 101.7%, while intensifying HD, increasing its frequency by 48.6% and accelerating propagation from MD. Reservoir regulation partly offsets streamflow depletion but does not reverse the enhanced propagation toward HD. Consequently, propagation shifts from pathways toward SD to HD. Human water use weakens the propagation of low severity MD events to SD, while lowering the threshold for propagation to HD, indicating increased sensitivity of streamflow systems. These effects are strongest in sub-basins with intensive human water use, particularly in the Huaibin-Bengbu region, and are driven by soil moisture replenishment, enhanced evapotranspiration, and streamflow depletion.

title: Spatial heterogeneity analysis of climate driving factors for spatiotemporal changes in potential evapotranspiration based on Multi‐Scale Geographically Weighted Regression and Geographical Detector
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yali Ma, Zuirong Niu, Dongyuan Sun
abstract: Study region Hexi Corridor, a representative arid and semi-arid inland region, northwestern China. Study focus To overcome the limitations of previous studies in terms of the spatial heterogeneity of the driving factors influencing potential evapotranspiration (PET) changes, and to address the issue of spatial non-stationarity of PET caused by climatic factors, this study exploratively introduced the Geographical Detector (GD) and Multi-Scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR). We analyzed the spatial-temporal distribution pattern of PET in the Hexi Corridor region, and revealed the spatial heterogeneity distribution characteristics of the driving factors at the grid cell scale. At the same time, important climatic factors with significant influence were identified, as well as the dual-factor driving mechanism. New hydrological insights for the region PET showed an increasing trend from southeast to northwest, with a significant increase accounting for 18.08%, a non-significant increase accounting for 57.86%, and a non-significant decrease accounting for 24.06%. In most areas of the Hexi Corridor, PET showed an increasing trend (75.94%). The precipitation and wind speed are the main factors causing spatial variations in PET. Any interaction between two factors is manifested as bi-variable enhance and nonlinear-enhance. The synergy of the two factors can enhance the explanatory power of a single factor for the spatial differentiation of PET. The influence of elevation on PET has a global characteristic, while the influence of meteorological factors has a stronger local dependence. The PET in the northwest of the Hexi Corridor is significantly affected by wind speed and temperature, while in the central and eastern parts, it is significantly inhibited by precipitation and relative humidity.
