In the southeast, PET is positively promoted by the sunshine duration. In most areas of the Hexi Corridor (86.21%), PET will show a continuous increasing trend in the future, while in some local areas in the west and east (13.79%), there will be a continuous decreasing trend.

title: Sub-monthly volumetric evolution of the supraglacial lakes in Northeastern Greenland based on the topographic depression method
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Huihui Zhao, Baojin Qiao, Mingcheng Hu, Jikun Liu, Jing Li, Haiyan Liu, Xin Li
abstract: Study region Supraglacial lakes on the northeastern Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) during the melt seasons (May–September) from 2018 to 2025. Study focus This study develops a multi-parameter inversion framework for supraglacial lakes by integrating multi-source remote sensing data and machine learning. Using Landsat-8 multispectral bands and indices combined with ArcticDEM, a machine learning model is constructed to map the supraglacial lake area. Lake volume is estimated via the terrain depression method. The framework enables high-temporal-resolution (sub-monthly) monitoring of supraglacial lake area and volume over a decadal scale. A key innovation is the quantitative analysis of altitudinal shifts in the spatial distribution of supraglacial lakes at high temporal resolution, along with region-specific attribution of climatic drivers. New hydrological insights The inversion reveals that the coverage of supraglacial lakes in high-elevation regions increased from less than 10–25% during the study period. Quantitative climate attribution shows significant elevation‑dependent heterogeneity: in mid‑elevation regions, temperature‑driven surface meltwater flux contributes 42.45% to changes in supraglacial lake volume, surpassing precipitation as the dominant factor; in high‑elevation regions, snowmelt recharge and surface runoff inputs are the primary drivers. This framework provides a scientifically robust technical solution for sub‑monthly dynamic monitoring of supraglacial lakes, filling the gap in high‑frequency, long‑term hydrological observation on the GrIS.

title: Characteristics of soil moisture dynamics and recharge pattern in alpine meadows under nitrogen addition conditions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zongjie Li, Fang Liu, Bowen Wang, Yixuan Wang, Juan Gui, Xiaxia Li, Zexi Chen
abstract: Study region Alpine meadows in the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (Shaliu River Basin), a permafrost-affected cold region sensitive to nitrogen deposition and climate change. Study focus Nitrogen addition can alter soil structure and hydrological processes, yet its impacts on soil-water dynamics and source partitioning in alpine meadows remain unclear. A two-year field experiment (2023–2024) with four nitrogen levels (0, 5, 10, 15 g m⁻² yr⁻¹) was conducted. Stable isotopes (δ²H, δ¹⁸O), LC-excess, and End-Member Mixing Analysis (EMMA) were used to trace soil-water origin, infiltration pathways, and source contributions under varying nitrogen inputs. New hydrological insights for the region Nitrogen addition significantly shifted infiltration regimes from preferential flow under control conditions to piston-flow dominance under N5 (May and July-September) and sustained piston flow under N10-N15 (June-September). (2) Precipitation supplied 34–46% of soil water, while underground ice and supra-permafrost water each contributed 26–33%, with seasonal switching from precipitation dominance (May-July) to increased frozen-ground inputs (August-September). (3) Higher nitrogen enhanced late-season supra-permafrost contributions and altered evapotranspiration partitioning. (4) Moderate nitrogen input (5 g m⁻² yr⁻¹) most effectively maintained piston-flow-dominated infiltration, enhanced deep percolation, and stabilized soil-water interactions, whereas excessive nitrogen reduced water-use efficiency and altered source contributions.

title: Application of an ANN model integrating station network distribution and water level increment principle in flood season water level prediction of Taihu Lake basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhongtian Zhang, Hao Qin, Qiang Xu, Huiming Zhang, Xinyi Wu, Li Liu, Yong Min, Xu Zhang, Wenhai Yang, Qinghua Liang
abstract: Study region The Taihu Lake basin is a typical plain river network area in eastern China, characterized by extremely gentle terrain, dense river-lake systems, intensive human activities, and complex hydrological interactions. The region is highly vulnerable to flooding during the flood season due to its flat landscape, concentrated rainfall. Study focus This study constructs controlled BP-ANN models with the spatial distribution of hydrological stations and real-time water level increment information. Five ablation BP-ANN models are established to quantify the contributions of water level increment, PLS fusion and multi-station data. SHAP method was adopted to interpret outputs for level prediction. The core focus is to find reliable method to improve water level prediction under complex hydrological conditions, reduce peak errors, and enhance the reliability of regional flood forecasting systems. New hydrological insights for the region Among all developed models, the single-station method provides the optimal compromise between prediction performance and model complexity. The multi-station method yields accuracy gains only for a small subset of stations with strong hydrological connectivity and introduces redundant features for most plain-river-network sites. The upstream and mid-plain areas show different confluence patterns affected by runoff and backwater. The findings support zoned intelligent forecasting for plain river networks, and can serve as a reliable way for flood control and regional hydrological services in the plain river network regions.

title: Environmental thresholds and lagged rainfall effects on stem sap flow in dryland shelterbelt trees
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yali Jia, Yiben Cheng, Xinle Li, Zhiming Xin, Jingwen Li, Zixuan Yuan, Lixia Chu
abstract: Study region This study was conducted at Xinhua Forest Farm, located in the desert–oasis transition zone of the Ulan Buh Desert, northwestern China, where mean annual precipitation and evaporation are approximately 132 and 2032 mm, respectively. Sap flow of Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica, Ulmus pumila, and Elaeagnus angustifolia was monitored during the 2024–2025 growing seasons. Study focus Generalized additive mixed models and distributed lag non-linear models were used to quantify nonlinear sap-flow responses to solar radiation (SR), vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and soil water content (SWC), and to assess lagged rainfall effects under different antecedent soil-moisture conditions. New hydrological insights for the region Cumulative sap flow was 1189.44, 1313.75, and 1849.44 kg for P. sylvestris, U. pumila, and E. angustifolia, respectively. Sap flow responded nonlinearly to all three environmental drivers (P < 0.001). The SR turning points were 323.0, 323.0, and 333.1 W m⁻²; the VPD turning points were 2.814, 1.763, and 2.223 kPa; and the SWC turning points were 0.0810, 0.0968, and 0.0586 m³ m⁻³ , respectively. Post-rainfall responses lasted 2–4 h in P. sylvestris, approximately 10 h in U. pumila, and more than 15 h in E. angustifolia. Their magnitude and duration depended strongly on antecedent SWC. These findings show that rainfall use by shelterbelt trees is jointly regulated by species-specific environmental thresholds and antecedent soil moisture.

title: Revealing the mixed driving mechanism of hydrological disaster risk in the Dongting Lake Basin based on an improved risk index
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Pai Liu, Feng Li, Qianqian He, Yonghong Xie, Mingming Geng, Bikram Manandhar, Heng Jiang, Yue Xu, Siyuan Yue, Yuhe Zhang, Xin Weng
abstract: Study region Dongting Lake Basin, China Study focus This study focuses on assessing basin-scale hydrological disaster risk and disentangling its underlying mixed driving mechanisms. Two core objectives are defined: (1) assessing basin-scale hydrological disaster risk through satellite-derived surface water observations, and (2) quantifying the individual and combined contributions of climate variability, economic development, and vegetation dynamics to hydrological disaster risk. We develop a hybrid framework for basin-scale hydrological disaster risk assessment, which integrates satellite imagery, spectral water indices (including NDWI, MNDWI, and SPWI), and machine learning algorithms. Further, we conducted multiple attribution analysis using multiple linear regression and SHAP interpretation analysis based on random forest to quantify the long-term driving mechanism of hydrological disaster risk. New hydrological insights for the region This study found the hydrological disaster risk in the Dongting Lake Basin has shown inconsistent trends, with an overall decreasing trend. In the study area, approximately 79.56% of the basin experienced a reduction in risk, while 20.44% exhibited an increase. The increase in risk is related to the increase in precipitation within the basin and the transition of land use from forest areas to farmland. However, changes in GDP, land use changes, and vegetation greening offset the hydrological disaster risks caused by increased precipitation in most regions. These findings provide a scientific foundation for water resource management and hydrological risk mitigation strategies.

title: Lake–aquifer connectivity controls groundwater dynamics in a multi-aquifer system within a typical floodplain
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hanxiao Wang, Fu Liao, Guangcai Wang, Xianglong Chen, Ziwen Zhang, Luoyao Xiong, Peng Sun, Yongzhen Fu
abstract: Study region The study was conducted in the Poyang Lake floodplain, China, where a vertically stratified multi-aquifer system interacts with Poyang Lake, a seasonal lake (Candou Lake), regional lateral flow, rainfall infiltration, and artificial ponds. Study focus This study investigates the drivers of groundwater level dynamics in a vertically stratified aquifer system at small spatial scale (<30 m). High-frequency groundwater monitoring, cross-correlation analysis, wavelet analysis, and numerical groundwater flow modeling were integrated to identify aquifer-specific responses to hydrological and anthropogenic controls. New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater dynamics presented pronounced vertical heterogeneity within < 30 m. The shallow aquifer was mainly controlled by rainfall infiltration and Candou Lake recharge. The intermediate aquifer was connected to both Candou Lake and Poyang Lake, but Candou Lake exerted stronger control during the flood period. The deep aquifer was alternately influenced by Poyang Lake recharge and regional lateral flow: the lake recharge initiates groundwater rise, whereas lateral recharge controlled peak groundwater levels. Model simulations confirmed that Candou Lake provides greater recharge to the shallow and intermediate aquifers than rainfall and Poyang Lake, respectively, while Poyang Lake initially dominated recharge to the deep aquifer. Artificial ponds elevated groundwater levels in shallow and intermediate aquifers, maintained high levels during the dry season, and enhanced local recharge. These findings highlight the necessity of high-resolution, multi-aquifer characterization to support groundwater management in floodplains.

title: Distribution and source apportionment of groundwater nitrate contamination in shallow and deep aquifers of the Hebei Plain: A combined interpretation of PCA-APCS-MLR, hydrochemical methods, and land use characteristics
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Pan Bi, Manni Chao, Ruinan Liu, Guanxing Huang, Zhichao Li, Ziting Yuan
abstract: Study region Hebei Plain, China Study focus Groundwater nitrate contamination is a global concern, and methods for its source apportionment are generally complicated. This study aims to investigate the distribution of nitrate in shallow and deep groundwater across different land use types in the Hebei Plain, and to estimate the relative contributions of potential nitrate sources via the integration of principal component analysis-absolute principal component score-multiple linear regression (PCA-APCS-MLR), conventional hydrochemical methods, and land use information. New hydrological insights for the region Proportions of high-nitrate (> 50 mg/L) groundwater (PHNG) in shallow aquifers in both of piedmont and littoral plains were 5 times or more that in shallow aquifer of the central plain and deep aquifer of various sub-plains. In the piedmont plain, PHNGs in shallow aquifers in both of bare and urban lands were more than 50%, followed by woods-grasslands (43.8%), agricultural lands (27.6%), and rural areas (18.8%); by contrast, the PHNG in deep aquifers in urban lands was 40% and > 10 times that in other land use types. In the central plain, the PHNG in shallow aquifers in rural areas was > 9 times that in agricultural lands. This is opposite to the littoral plain where the PHNGs in shallow aquifers in agricultural lands was 1.6 times that in rural areas. The relative contribution results calculated by PCA-APCS-MLR suggest that manure and septic sewage are preliminarily inferred as the dominant potential sources (58.8%) of nitrate in shallow groundwater of the piedmont plain, followed by mixed sources (25.8%), fertilizers (11.7%), natural sources (2.3%), as well as domestic sewage and nitrification in vadose zones (1.4%). A considerable proportion of mixed sources for groundwater nitrate in the piedmont plain indicates that overlapping nitrogen sources cannot be fully separated by the PCA-APCS-MLR model. In contrast, fertilizers (40.6%) and manure (37.7%) are inferred to be the two major contributors to nitrate in shallow groundwater of the littoral plain. This study reveals that the combination of PCA-APCS-MLR, conventional hydrochemical methods and land use information serves as a cost-effective approach to assess source contributions of groundwater nitrate in large alluvial plains such as the Hebei Plain. It should be noted that this method has limitations in distinguishing overlapping nitrogen sources, and the results require comprehensive interpretation.

title: A multiscale dynamic network-based method for radar precipitation nowcasting: A case study in the Yiluo River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yingrui Li, Qiting Zuo, Tao Li, Yihu Ji
abstract: Study region Yiluo River Basin, China Study focus Accurate and timely precipitation nowcasting is essential for mitigating rainstorms and floods. This study proposes a Multiscale Dynamic Nowcasting Network (MDN-Net) that integrates temporal and motion features for radar echo extrapolation and quantitative precipitation estimation. A four-dimensional evaluation framework is also developed to comprehensively assess nowcasting performance from multiple perspectives. New hydrological insights for the region (1) MDN-Net significantly improves strong echo extrapolation and outperforms the other models at lead times of 1.5–2 h. (2) For quantitative precipitation estimation, MDN-Net accurately captures the observed temporal evolution of rainfall, although cumulative precipitation is slightly overestimated. It achieves the smallest RBIAS magnitude (-2.05% to −3.51%), indicating superior robustness and generalization capability. (3) Module analysis demonstrates that MDN-Net with the feature fusion module maintains stable performance across thresholds and lead times. Specifically, F1-score increases by 44.3% and 35.1% at 1.5 h and 2 h lead times compared with U-Net and Flow U-Net, respectively. Overall, by integrating temporal sequence and motion features, MDN-Net provides a more comprehensive and accurate representation of precipitation systems, significantly enhances spatiotemporal perception, and improves nowcasting performance, offering a promising framework for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of precipitation nowcasting and supporting disaster prevention and water resource management.

title: Uncovering the impact of catchment attributes in regionalized models through explainable artificial intelligence
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xianghuan Kong, Shanhu Jiang, Chunsheng Yang, Miao He, Bang Yang, Jiabin Zhang, Mao Li, Liliang Ren
abstract: Study region 531 ungauged basins in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Study focus: We propose XNLSTM, an interpretive framework combining regionalized Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) modeling, 10-fold basin cross-validation, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, including Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), the Morris method, and permutation feature importance (PFI), to examine how catchment attributes affect runoff prediction in ungauged basins. The framework jointly uses multiple XAI methods to reveal interpretational variability and identify catchment attributes with relatively stable importance across methods. It then trains models under different catchment attribute configurations derived from the XAI-based interpretation results and interprets fold-specific models to assess the stability of catchment attribute importance across basin splits and configurations. New hydrological insights for the region: SHAP, Morris, and PFI produce different rankings for the same LSTM model, but p_mean, aridity, and other catchment attributes remain consistently important. Across the three XAI rankings, climatic and topographic attributes are consistently more important than soil, geological, and vegetation attributes for overall runoff prediction. Using more catchment attributes, and using attributes with higher XAI-derived importance, improves cross-basin generalization. However, lower ranked attribute combinations show slight tendencies to reproduce low-flow and high-flow metrics closer to observations. Importance rankings are relatively stable for all-attribute models but change more clearly when models use attribute subsets. Attributes such as elev_mean, pet_mean, and soil_conductivity remain important across basin splits and configurations.

title: Responses of seasonal baseflow to climate warming in an alpine mountain basin: Insights from GAMLSS modeling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Bing Bai, Ping Wang, Shiqi Liu, Mingming Feng, Yichi Zhang, Tingting Wang, Qiwei Huang, Irina S. Danilovich, Sergey P. Pozdniakov
abstract: Study region The Kaidu River is a cryosphere-fed inland river in the central Tianshan Mountains of arid northwest China, sustaining downstream oases, irrigated agriculture, and Bosten Lake. Study focus We examined seasonal baseflow responses to warming during 1961–2020 and an abrupt regime shift. Daily streamflow for 2009–2020 was reconstructed with a Long Short-Term Memory model, baseflow was separated using nine methods centered on the Eckhardt filter, and monthly controls were quantified with Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape. New hydrological insights for the region Baseflow averaged 77.6 m3/s (68% of streamflow), indicating strong groundwater buffering by the Quaternary aquifer. Around 1996, annual streamflow and baseflow increased by 24% and 22%, respectively, and the shift was reproduced by all nine methods. Antecedent wetness was significant from April to November, revealing persistent groundwater memory. Climate–baseflow coupling followed four seasonal phases: storage-dominated spring, climate-sensitive summer, storage-controlled autumn recession, and an early-winter transition. Over 1961–2020, a 1°C increase in temperature was associated with 8.6% higher July baseflow; stratified analyses further showed that temperature emerged as a significant July driver only after 1996. These findings reveal strong groundwater memory and an increasing influence of warming on warm-season baseflow, with implications for downstream water supply in the Yanqi Basin.

title: Multi-isotope tracing reveals nitrate and sulfate sources and fate across contrasting activity zones in a semi-arid basin of northern China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chang Yue, Ruizhong Gao, Limin Duan, Tianke Su, Xixi Wang, Tingxi Liu, Guoqiang Wang
abstract: Study region The Dahei River Basin, a semi-arid basin in northern China. Study focus In semi-arid surface water-groundwater systems, nitrate (NO3 –) and sulfate (SO4 2–) are jointly influenced by natural processes and anthropogenic activities, yet how their sources, transformations, and export vary across contrasting activity zones remains insufficiently understood. Integrating hydrochemistry, multiple stable isotopes, a Bayesian isotope mixing model, and representative-section flux analysis, this study investigated the source compositions, transformation processes, and export differences of NO3 – and SO4 2– in the Dahei River Basin. New hydrological insights for the region: Results showed greater SO4 2– enrichment in high-activity zones, whereas NO3 – exceedance was more prominent in low-activity zones. In low-activity areas, NO3 – mainly originated from manure and sewage (35.2%) and soil organic nitrogen (27.7%), whereas high-activity areas showed more mixed NO3 – sources. For SO4 2–, sulfide oxidation and manure and sewage were major sources in both zones, contributing 29.8–36.6% and 24.0–24.8%, respectively. Nitrification dominated NO3 – transformation, whereas SO4 2– transformation reflected overlapping effects of sulfide oxidation and mineralization, together with contributions from evaporite dissolution. At nested sections in the low and high activity zones, downstream annual cumulative NO3 – and SO4 2– fluxes were 3.16 and 8.41 times the upstream values, respectively, reflecting flow accumulation and combined natural and anthropogenic influences. These findings support zone-based source control and tailored water environment management in semi-arid basins.

title: Widespread intensification of rainfall erosivity over the Loess Plateau in a warmer world
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chu-Nan Zhang, Meng-Zhuo Zhang, Weidong Guo
abstract: Study region The Loess Plateau of China hosts the world’s most extensive and thickest loess deposits. The porous, fragile loess and complex climate cause severe soil erosion here, making it one of the most severely eroded areas in the world. Study focus The rainfall erosivity (RE) serves as the active factor that leads to its change. This study assesses future changes in RE across the region based on 23 sets of statistical downscaling datasets under three SSP-RCP scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicate that over 97% of the region will experience significantly increased RE, following a northwest-to-southeast increasing gradient, and areas with historically high RE intensify the most. Regarding the regional mean, annual RE is projected to rise by 25.7%, 21.9%, and 27.8% during 2041–2070 against 1985–2014 under SSP1‐2.6, SSP2‐4.5, and SSP5‐8.5, respectively. By 2071–2100, these values will reach 24.2%, 28.3%, and 53.5%. Seasonally, May and September will contribute most to the annual increase. The projected RE increase is dominated by more frequent and intense moderate and heavy rainfall. These findings reveal a shifting erosion regime across the Loess Plateau, with potential impacts on ecosystem stability, water resource distribution, and flood risk management. This regional assessment could provide a basis for evaluating future risks and for developing integrated strategies for soil conservation, water resources management, and ecosystem protection under a changing climate.

title: Fault-controlled hydrogeochemical spatial evolution revealed by machine learning around the 2010 Ms 7.1 Yushu earthquake zone
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hongyi He, Zhi Chen, Qingyong Luo, Bihong Fu, Zihan Gao, Yili Luo, Zhikeng Huang, Zhaofei Liu, Ke Zhang, Weiye Shao, Ying Li
abstract: Study Region: The Ganzi-Yushu fault zone (GYFZ) is an active strike-slip fault on the eastern Tibetan Plateau, separating the Bayan Har and Qiangtang blocks. Study Focus: Active strike-slip faults can act as barriers and conduits for groundwater, making them important settings for understanding how seismic deformation redistributes meteoric recharge and deep volatiles. In the GYFZ, along-strike fault coupling, the 2010 Yushu rupture, and heterogeneous lithologies require clarification of how fault architecture controls groundwater circulation and hydrochemical differentiation. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Hydrochemical, water-isotope, gas-isotope, and unsupervised machine-learning evidence (Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)) from 31 water samples and 9 gas-sampling sites shows the GYFZ is compartmentalized. Stable isotopes indicate meteoric recharge, but circulation is partitioned by mechanical state. Highly coupled locked sectors preserve dilute meteoric Cluster 2 waters and limit vertical exchange with deep fluids. Ruptured and coupling-transition domains provide conduits for deeper, warmer Cluster 1 fluids, producing SiO2, Na+, Cl-, and HCO3 - enrichment and variable volatile input (CO2 = 1.02–99.04%; Rc = 0.10–0.51 Ra). Cluster 3, represented by GQNY, records a local sulfate-rich flow path through evaporitic and carbonate lithologies; its SO4 2- enrichment reflects mineral availability and hydrological connectivity rather than CO2-driven acidity. Thus, fault coupling determines conduit-barrier behaviour, whereas lithology controls the reaction fingerprint, explaining localized volatile-bearing anomalies along the fault.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and hydroclimatic contributions associated with drought–flood abrupt alternation in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Ying Xue, Lei Zou, Jun Xia, Chengjian Liu, Si Hong
abstract: Study region Yangtze River Basin of China Study focus This study examines the spatiotemporal patterns, seasonality, periodic variability, and hydroclimatic contributions of drought–flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) in the Yangtze River Basin during 1961–2023. Drought-to-flood (DF) and flood-to-drought (FD) events are identified using a standardized DFAA index (DFAAI) constructed from consecutive monthly standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) values. Trend, hotspot, spectral, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses assess their frequency, intensity, evolution, and associated predictors. New hydrological insights for the region DFAA frequency and intensity exhibit distinct spatial patterns, indicating that the recurrence and severity of rapid water-balance reversals are not spatially uniform across the Yangtze River Basin. High-frequency areas occur mainly in the middle–lower basin and lake regions, exceeding 10 events per decade, whereas the strongest events cluster along the Sichuan Basin margin. Basin-mean linear trends are weak, but DFAA variability strengthened after 2000. DF events span June–October, while FD events concentrate in July–September and show stronger synchronization among sub-basins, reflecting different monsoon-season pathways of moisture recovery and depletion. DF and FD frequencies show recurrent 3–5-year variability, whereas intensity contains longer-period components. SHAP results indicate that rapid precipitation and humidity changes are most consistently associated with the initiation of water-balance reversals, while temperature and radiation conditions contribute more strongly to their intensity, especially for FD. Large-scale circulation indices mainly modulate the background climate state.

title: A cascaded deep learning framework for improved forecasting of drought-flood abrupt alternation events in the Hanjiang River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yubing Wang, Si Chen, Kedi Fang, Tiancheng Wang, Heng Hu, Rui Xia, Min Wang, Hai Liu
abstract: Study region The Hanjiang River Basin (HJRB), a meteorologically and topographically complex region in China. Study focus Drought-Flood Abrupt Alternation (DFAA) events threaten water security, yet their prediction remains challenging because of highly nonlinear dynamics and pronounced zero inflation in meteorological records. This study employed the Standardized Drought-Wetness Abrupt Alternation Index (SDWAI) to identify DFAA events and used SHAP to reveal their driving mechanisms. A cascaded framework integrating a parallel convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) classifier, wavelet decomposition, and ensemble regression was developed. By separating event identification from conditional intensity estimation, the framework reduced the influence of non-event samples. New hydrological insights for the region The CNN-LSTM classifier achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.67 and module obtained the best performance (R² = 0.91). The complete cascade framework achieved an overall R² of 0.58 and reduced the peak underestimation commonly observed in conventional zero-inflated regression models. Spatiotemporal analysis revealed distinct phase-locking characteristics of DFAA events, with downstream and southeastern HJRB identified as hazard hotspots. Drought to flood transitions occurred mainly during spring and summer, whereas flood-to-drought transitions increased markedly during late autumn and early winter. Local precipitation and potential evapotranspiration dominated DFAA evolution, while the Arctic Oscillation primarily regulated the large-scale atmospheric circulation background. These findings demonstrate the potential of cascaded deep learning frameworks for regional DFAA forecasting and adaptive water resource management.

title: Impacts of tropical cyclones on episodic transport of water and suspended sediment in mountainous catchments: A case study from Hainan Island
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Caifeng Liu, Wei Jiang, Shanshan Deng, Yangyang Yong, Tingwu Gu, Yuchen Shi, Siqi Du, Ting Yang, Kefu Yu
abstract: Study region Hainan Island, China, focusing on three major rivers: the Nandu, Changhua, and Wanquan River basins. Study focus Tropical cyclones (TCs) are key drivers of episodic riverine material fluxes in coastal mountainous regions. However, their quantitative role in regulating water discharge and suspended sediment discharge (SSD) in tropical island basins remains poorly constrained. Based on 64 years (1960–2023) of daily hydrological records, this study quantifies TC-associated contributions to water discharge and SSD and examines how TCs modify water–sediment transport. New hydrological insights for the region Quantitative analysis indicates that TCs exert a substantial influence on water discharge and SSD, contributing 4 ± 4% to 8 ± 6% of annual water discharge and 11 ± 10% to 30 ± 27% of annual SSD on average, with contributions reaching 91–95% of SSD in extreme years. Their influence on SSD is markedly stronger than on water discharge, indicating a pronounced sediment-routing enhancement. Sensitivity to TC forcing varies substantially across basins and these inter-basin differences are jointly regulated by TC characteristics, basin geomorphology (such as area and slope), and reservoir regulation. The identified water–sediment response regimes further highlight the nonlinear nature of sediment transport under TC forcing. These findings refine the understanding of extreme-event-driven material fluxes and provide a critical basis for managing flood risks, reservoir operations, and soil conservation in tropical island river systems.

title: Quantifying precipitation-induced changes in the proportion of nitrate inputs and their role in karst processes: Evidence from stable isotopes and water chemistry
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Wei Zhang, Zhongfa Zhou, Hui Dong, Jijuan Wang, Yi Huang, Xiaoduo Wang, Huijing Wei, Yang Bai, Mingyang An
abstract: Study region The study region is located within Shuanghe Cave National Geopark, China. Study focus Global warming has intensified extreme rainfall events, yet existing carbon cycle models generally overlook nitric acid weathering processes modulated by rainfall, leading to biased estimates of karst carbon sinks. In this study, conventional physicochemical parameters of water bodies, δ15N- NO 3 − , δ18O- NO 3 − and δ13C-DIC were measured simultaneously. Using the MixSIAR model, we distinguished the dynamic changes in nitrate source contributions before and after rainstorms, quantitatively estimated the proportion of carbonate weathering driven by nitric acid, elucidated the mechanism by which intensive rainfall-driven nitrogen input reduces the karst carbon sink, and corrected the biases inherent in traditional karst carbon-sink assessment methods. New hydrological insights After heavy rainfall, the proportion of anthropogenic nitrate increased markedly - by 37% in June and 22.4% in October - with higher nitrogen leaching intensity in June (agriculturally dominated) than in October (domestic-pollution dominated). Notably, the overall proportion of carbonate weathering attributed to nitric acid declined following rainstorms: from 8.24% to 7.14% in June, and from 4.96% to 3.56% in October. Under heavy storm conditions (daily rainfall ≥ 50 mm), the contribution of nitric acid to carbonate weathering is weakened by rainwater dilution. Therefore, for shallow karst watersheds, it is unwarranted to categorically conclude that rainfall promotes nitric-acid-mediated carbonate weathering; instead, the evaluation framework for weathering processes and carbon-sink effects should be further refined under different rainfall intensity scenarios.

title: Synchronously considering spatial dependence and temporal persistence into a deep learning based method for improving soil moisture spatial resolution
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yanqing Yang, Jinqian Xia, Zhenxin Bao, Jiujiang Wu, Wei Zhao
abstract: Study region The Huai River Basin is a major agricultural region in central-eastern China, characterized by a monsoon climate, strong seasonal precipitation variability, and frequent drought–flood alternation. High-resolution soil moisture (SM) information is therefore essential for regional hydrological applications. Study focus A hybrid convolutional long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) framework was developed to downscale the European Space Agency Climate Change Initiative (ESA CCI) SM product. Meteorological, vegetation, and topographic predictors were integrated, while ESA CCI data and dense in situ observations jointly constrained model training. Predictor combinations, model structures, and target resolutions were systematically evaluated. CNN–LSTM outperformed CNN-only and LSTM-only models, achieving an overall correlation of approximately 0.79 and an unbiased root mean square error (ubRMSE) of 0.041 m³/m³. Extended triple collocation showed that the 5 km product reached a median correlation of 0.91 and a median RMSE of 0.018 m³/m³, outperforming ERA5 and SMAP. New hydrological insights for the region Multi-day accumulated precipitation explained SM variability better than daily rainfall, indicating clear antecedent-rainfall memory. Precipitation mainly controlled wetting–drying transitions, whereas vegetation and terrain regulated spatial redistribution and water retention. The lower accuracy at 1 km than at 5 km revealed scale dependence, suggesting that excessively fine downscaling may introduce unsupported spatial variability. Overall, the 5 km product more reliably preserved basin-scale SM gradients and seasonal dynamics.

title: Non-iterative coordination method for multi-objective flood control operation of a reservoir group based on equivalent projection theory
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Bin Wang, Yukun Fan, Xinyuan Qian, Chengjing Xu, Ran Mo, Sunyu Xu, Zixin Song, Yiwen Wang, Jieyu Li, Ping-an Zhong
abstract: Study region The middle Yellow River Basin (MYRB) Study focus In real-time flood control operation, high-dimensional nonlinear models challenge timely decision-making. Conventional iterative decomposition–coordination methods suffer from slow convergence in dimensionality reduction. This study proposes an efficient multi-reservoir flood control optimization method (EOM-EP) by coupling a non-iterative coordination framework based on equivalent projection theory (EP) with parallel computing. Numerical experiments demonstrate its accuracy and computational efficiency. Application to typical flood events in the MYRB further highlights upstream-downstream risk transfer mechanisms and flood regulation roles of mainstem and tributary reservoirs. New hydrological insights for the region (1) The non-iterative global coordination mechanism of EOM-EP is applicable to flood control operation of reservoir groups at different scales, and, compared with the Lagrange method, its performance becomes increasingly superior as the dimensionality of decision variables increases. (2) A significant upstream–downstream risk conflict exists between the reservoir group and the Huayuankou section in the MYRB, and balanced objective weights favor reservoir-group spatiotemporal synergy in flood storage and release while mitigating imbalanced risk allocation. (3) Reservoir operation strategies depend on flood spatial composition. The Xiaolangdi reservoir dominates mainstem floods (P1); tributary-dominated floods (P2) require consideration of Hekoucun reservoir risk and compensatory regulation by tributary reservoirs; and concurrent floods (P3) require strengthened coordination to reduce peak superposition. The system flood-control risk across scenarios ranks P2 > P3 > P1.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and nonlinear associations of snow phenology with environmental factors in the forest-steppe ecotone of the Greater Khingan Mountains
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Weijie Zhang, Yiyang Zhao, Hengzhi Guo, Yingjie Wu, Jiuji An, Shuaijie Liang, Shuang Zhao
abstract: Study region The western slope of the Greater Khingan Mountains, northeastern China, represents a climate-sensitive forest–steppe ecotone where seasonal snow processes strongly influence regional hydrological and ecological dynamics. Study focus Using a 1-km snow phenology dataset derived from Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (AVHRR) observations during the 1982–2019 hydrological years, this study investigated the spatiotemporal variations of snow cover duration (SCD), snow cover start date (SCS), and snow cover melt date (SCM). Modified Mann–Kendall trend analysis, Pearson correlation analysis, cross-wavelet analysis, and an annual pixel-based eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)–SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework were applied to characterize snow phenology changes and quantify the temporal variations in model-based contributions of environmental factors. New hydrological insights for the region Snow cover duration decreased significantly at a rate of −0.42 d/a, mainly associated with delayed snow cover onset (SCS: +0.46 d/a), while SCM showed only a weak decreasing trend (−0.046 d/a), indicating an asymmetric seasonal response of snow phenology. Temperature showed significant statistical associations with SCD and SCM, whereas total precipitation exhibited spatially heterogeneous relationships with snow phenology. The annual XGBoost models achieved moderate predictive performance, with spatial cross-validation R² values of 0.52, 0.40, and 0.56 for SCD, SCS, and SCM, respectively. SHAP analysis revealed that environmental contributions varied among years and snow phenology indicators: precipitation and NDVI frequently contributed substantially to SCD variation, NDVI showed increasing relative contributions for SCS after the mid-2000s, and the contribution structure for SCM varied among years. These findings indicate that snow phenology changes in this transitional cold region are closely associated with temporally varying environmental factors rather than a single dominant factor, providing new insights into seasonal snow storage changes and potential hydrological responses in cold regions.

title: Hydrothermal-hydrological conditions control water dissolved organic carbon of the central Qinghai-Xizang Plateau permafrost regions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yu Wang, Cunlin Xin, Yuzhong Yang, Ligang Kang, Yindong Wang, Sai Dong, Helin Yao, Chen Lei, Junjie Zhai
abstract: Study region The Beiluhe Basin in the interior of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP), a high-altitude permafrost region sensitive to climate warming. Study focus Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a primary pathway for terrestrial carbon transfer to aquatic ecosystems. Compared to the Arctic, the coupling mechanisms between active layer hydrothermal processes and DOC in different water components in the interior QXP remain poorly understood. This study investigates DOC dynamics in streams, thermokarst lakes/ponds, and groundwater from 2020 to 2023. By integrating meteorological data, soil hydrothermal conditions, and groundwater level and temperature, we analyze the regulatory mechanisms of hydrothermal conditions and active layer thawing on DOC export across different water components. New hydrological insights for the region Results reveal a distinct asynchronous response mechanism. Thermokarst lakes/ponds act as early responders, peaking in DOC during the thaw initiation period driven by surface flushing. Conversely, streams and groundwater act as late responders, reaching maximum DOC concentrations in the post-thaw period due to the lagged release of deep soil carbon caused by active layer deepening. This vertical hydrothermal lag of the active layer and water level fluctuations regulate hydrological connectivity and DOC transport pathways. These findings are essential for accurately simulating the carbon cycle and predicting climate feedback effects in the QXP permafrost region.

title: Dynamic compensation for flood and sediment regulation in the Yellow River using a digital twin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yuntao Feng, Changgao Cheng, Jun Ma
abstract: Study region This study examines the 128-km Xiaolangdi–Huayuankou reach of the middle and lower Yellow River, China. Reservoir releases affect Huayuankou after a travel-time lag and interact with sediment transport and channel-bed adjustment. Study focus We develop a digital twin-enhanced bi-level multi-agent framework in which the basin authority sets a time-varying sediment-flushing subsidy and the reservoir operator selects release and sediment-control responses. The hydrodynamic-sediment digital twin serves as a state-transition and feasibility operator within a nested real-coded genetic algorithm–particle swarm optimization procedure. The framework is evaluated using a 240-h reconstruction of the 2021 Autumn Flood under centralized coordination, decentralized operation without compensation, and decentralized operation with dynamic compensation. New hydrological insights for the region Downstream risk depends on reservoir-response timing relative to flood-wave propagation, not on inflow magnitude alone. Without compensation, Huayuankou water level peaks at 94.14 m and remains above the 93.56-m threshold for 49 h, while cumulative sediment evacuation is about 15,000 t. Dynamic compensation lowers the peak to 93.45 m and increases sediment evacuation to about 22,500 t, 50% above the no-compensation case and close to the centralized benchmark of 23,500 t. Local perturbation tests indicate that reoptimization moderates the tested inflow and sediment-load effects, whereas higher electricity prices increase required compensation. These findings apply only to the reconstructed event and tested ranges.

title: An integrated data decomposition and feature selection–based hybrid machine learning framework for enhanced hourly wastewater inflow forecasting at a wastewater treatment plant in Oahu, Hawaii
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Jinwook Lee, Sayed M. Bateni, Dongkyun Kim, Changhyun Jun, Roger Babcock, Shohreh Azizi
abstract: Study region The Sand Island Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP), the primary wastewater management facility on Oahu, Hawaii. Study focus Wastewater inflow (WI) is a critical variable for efficient WWTP management. This study developed a hybrid framework for hourly WI forecasting at lead times of 1–48 h, integrating Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) with two feature selection methods—K-Best (KBest) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)—combined with a Cascade Forward Neural Network (CFNN), selected as the base learner after outperforming Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks. Historical WI and hour of day were the only inputs. The resulting VMD-KBest-CFNN and VMD-RFE-CFNN were compared with the standalone CFNN. New hydrogeological insights for the region The hybrid models outperformed the standalone CFNN, with VMD-RFE-CFNN most accurate in validation (most recent 25% of the 2018–2024 record): NSE of 0.9991–0.9422 and RMSE of 0.0129–0.1030 m³ /s across lead times. On the two-year test set (unseen data; May 2024–April 2026), the model retained NSE ≥ 0.9351 and RMSE ≤ 0.1549 m3/s up to the 24 h lead time and, unlike the standalone model, preserved accuracy for high-flow events. Under Oahu's separate sewer system and stable subtropical climate, WI is dominated by the anthropogenic diurnal cycle, enabling accurate forecasts from a parsimonious input set. These findings can support forecast-based plant operation, from real-time pump and aeration control to day-ahead planning.

title: The impacts of winter storms on sediment dynamics and shear front variability in the Yellow River Delta
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Shuai Cong, Houjie Wang, Zhenye Zhang, Yanhao Liu, Naishuang Bi, Jinya Xu, Chenghao Wang, Xiao Wu
abstract: Study region Yellow River Delta (YRD), China Study focus Delta evolution exhibits pronounced seasonal variability―seaward progradation in summer due to high sediment supply and weak ocean dynamics, versus winter retreat dominated by storm activity. However, winter storm impacts on sediment dynamics remain insufficiently understood relative to summer processes, limiting systematic assessment of delta evolution. This study combines a well-validated numerical model with in-situ observations to investigate rapid sediment dynamic responses of the YRD to winter storms. New hydrological insights Winter storms trigger substantial sediment resuspension in nearshore areas (bottom SSC peaking at 32.5 kg/m3) and enhance alongshore transport by an order of magnitude. East of the estuary, intensified southward coastal currents replace normal tidal alternation, eliminating inner-ebb-outer-flood shear fronts while prolonging and strengthening inner-flood-outer-ebb ones. Although total shear front duration remains comparable to that under calm conditions, increased intensity restricts offshore dispersal and promotes southward export. Wind direction critically modulates transport: sediment is consistently delivered to southwestern Laizhou Bay under all storm directions, while in the northern delta, transport shifts westward during northeasterly storms and reverses under northerly/northwesterly winds. Storm-driven processes account for ~68% of winter southward sediment flux, a contribution amplified by increasing storm frequency and duration. These findings establish winter storms as a key forcing in the YRD’s “Winter-Transport” phase, shaping its seasonal sediment redistribution, with implications for deltaic management under climate change.

title: Quantifying glacier and snowmelt contributions to runoff in the Indus River Basin using a high-resolution hydrological modeling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zahoor Ahmad, Zhijie Zhang, Wanchang Zhang
abstract: Study region The Indus River Basin extends from the glacierized Hindu Kush–Karakoram–Himalaya region to the arid plains. Snow and glacier melt strongly regulate upper-basin runoff, while downstream flows sustain extensive irrigation and water supply for more than 300 million people. Study focus This study quantifies snowmelt and glacier-melt contributions to IRB runoff during 2011–2020 by separately applying the fully distributed Infiltration Excess and Saturation Excess Soil-water Integration version 3 (ESSI-3) model and its glacier-process-enhanced version (GESSI-3) at 1-km spatial resolution. ESSI-3 represents terrestrial hydrological processes, whereas GESSI-3 additionally simulates glacier mass balance, snowmelt, and glacier melt. Both models were evaluated against observed discharge, while GESSI-3 was further assessed using independent datasets for evapotranspiration, terrestrial water storage, snow depth, and glacier thickness. New hydrological insights for the region For the period 2011–2020, glacier melt contributed 40.41% of annual runoff, exceeding the 25.92% from snowmelt; together, they accounted for 66.32%. Snowmelt contributions attained 20.70–21.78% during April–May, whereas glacier melt exceeded 40% during August–September and remained 39.74% in October. Collectively, meltwater supplied 55.50% of August runoff. Over the decade, snowmelt contribution declined from 36.05% to 21.05%, while glacier-melt contribution increased from 19.22% to 51.65%, concurrent with a glacier thinning of 152–160 mm/y. These findings indicate that runoff is increasingly dependent on diminishing glacial-storage, thereby worsening the basin's long-term water-security vulnerability.

title: Integrating error decomposition and feature-based diagnosis for multi-source precipitation estimates in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Min Zhu, Zhehui Shen, Yuhang Zhang, Hao Wu, Mingze Ding, Bin Yong
abstract: Study region Yangtze River Basin, China. Study focus This study presents an integrated diagnostic framework that combines four-component error decomposition with feature-based analyses of error amount, frequency, and intensity. The component-feature framework is applied to seven representative multi-source precipitation estimates (MPEs) spanning four major product categories. Using a gauge-based reference, spatial and temporal variations in the error components are systematically examined across the plateau, complex-terrain, and plain subregions of the basin. New hydrological insights for the region Among the satellite-based products, CMORPH and GSMaP exhibit broadly consistent error characteristics, featuring the smallest total biases and the strongest detection skill within the component-feature framework. IMERG exhibits a nearly balanced distribution of positive and negative hit biases (39% vs. 37%), which helps offset systematic errors. In contrast, PERSIANN shows the weakest detection skill and the largest intensity biases among the satellite products, consistent with the limitations of infrared-based retrievals. Regional differences are observed for specific products and error components, mainly reflected by spatial variations in false-alarm frequency for MSWEP and ERA5, with pronounced contrasts between high- and low-elevation regions. The monthly variations of these error characteristics also exhibit regional contrasts. Additionally, MSWEP exhibits intermediate error characteristics while maintaining the most stable monthly proportions among the four error components. SM2RAIN is characterized by persistently high false-alarm frequencies (>30%) together with pronounced hit-negative bias intensity across the basin, indicating a distinctive error structure among the evaluated MPEs. Overall, this component-feature framework provides a structured basis for understanding precipitation uncertainty and may support more informed use of MPEs.

title: Alarming decline of Iran’s Ramsar convention wetlands
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Mohammad Milad Salamattalab, Roohollah Noori, Mohsen Shahmohammad, Dongkyun Kim, Changhyun Jun, Sayed M. Bateni, Mehran Mahdian, Majid Hosseinzadeh, Seyed Mostafa Siadatmousavi, Mohammadreza Vesali Naseh, Kiana Mohammadi, Rabin Bhattarai, Peiman Kianmehr, Frederic Huneau, Yunlin Zhang, Soroush Abolfathi, Qiuhong Tang
abstract: Study region Iranian wetlands and lakes listed in Ramsar Convention Study focus Iran ranks second globally after Greece in wetland loss, with six of its wetlands listed on the Montreux Record. Despite this status, substantial gaps remain in quantifying long-term national wetland decline, associated economic losses, and the dominant drivers of desiccation. Here, we present the most comprehensive assessment to date of wetland loss in Iran over the past four decades (1986–2023), analyzing 23 Ramsar Convention-listed wetlands. We integrate Landsat 5/7/8 imagery processed with multiple water detection indices, Otsu-zero and Otsu-dynamic thresholding, Canny edge filtering, and stratified random sampling for validation. Methodological robustness is further confirmed through comparison with NASA-OPERA products and true-color images. New hydrological insights for the region We found that only six small wetlands have maintained near-natural conditions, while the remainder have experienced substantial shrinkage. Overall, wetland water-surface area declined by more than 57%, from 11,539 km2 during the baseline period (1986–1995) to 4921 km2 in 2023. This loss appears to be closely associated with state-led policies prioritizing agricultural self-sufficiency, resulting in extensive surface water diversion, groundwater over extraction, land-use changes. While our correlation analysis shows these associations, it does not establish causality, and the findings should therefore be interpreted as indicative rather than definitive. Economically, Iran now forfeits approximately US$2.415 billion annually in wetland-derived ecosystem services, while achieving a comparatively modest increase of about US$1.3 billion per year in agricultural value added. These policies are closely linked with widespread depleted aquifers across 421 of 609 national plains and disrupted river flows nationwide. The widespread desiccation of Iranian wetlands has generated profound environmental, economic, social, and public health consequences. Our findings underscore the urgent need for systemic water governance reforms to prevent further irreversible wetland loss.

title: Imbalance of internal nutrient retention in a typical eutrophic plateau lake associated with ecological water replenishment and its implications
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xue Wu, Yancai Wang, Ying Zhang, Qifeng Zhu, Lei Dong, Lixin Jiao, Jia He
abstract: Study region The Dianchi Lake, Kunming, Yunnan Province, China. Study focus Ecological water replenishment (EWR) is widely applied to improve lake hydrology and water quality, yet its effects on internal nutrient cycling in eutrophic lakes remain unclear. This study investigated sediment nutrient retention changes and mechanisms in Dianchi Lake after a decade of EWR, aiming to elucidate the decoupled responses of sedimentary nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) cycling to hydrological regulation and lake restoration. New hydrological insights for the region After EWR, hydraulic residence time (HRT) decreased by ~50%, while total N (TN) and total P (TP) concentrations declined, and dissolved oxygen (DO) increased in water column. Enhanced hydrodynamics and oxygenation accelerated sediment organic N mineralization, increasing ammonium (NH₄⁺-N) potential diffusive flux by 62%. In contrast, sediments shifted from a P source to a sink, with soluble reactive phosphorus (SRP) fluxes turning negative. Meanwhile, sediment dissolved organic matter (DOM) became more humified, transitioning from protein-like to humic-like dominance. These physicochemical changes were further reinforced by ecosystem recovery. Consequently, the water-column TN/TP ratio increased significantly, while sediment TN/TP and potentially mineralizable N/P ratios declined by 48.01% and 58.28%, respectively. These results reveal a decoupling of sediment N and P cycles under hydrological regulation, characterized by enhanced N release but preferential P retention, highlighting the need for coordinated N and P management strategies for sustainable lake restoration.

title: Explainable dynamic hybrid fusion method of remote sensing and land surface model data for soil water estimation in high mountainous areas
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Lanhui Zhang, Jiaxin Xu, Qi An, Wenli Zhao, Kaifeng Long, Chansheng He
abstract: Study region Heihe River Watershed, a high mountainous region in Northwest China Study focus This study proposed an Explainable Dynamic Hybrid Data Fusion (XDHDF) method that leverages remote sensing products and model simulations to adapt to high mountainous areas, and employed Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to elucidate the nonlinear impacts of environmental factors on soil water dynamics. New hydrological insights for the regions The XDHDF method achieves a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.983, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.019 m³ /m³ , and a Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) of 0.982, significantly outperforming existing data fusion methods in high mountainous areas. The fused product accurately captures spatial patterns and temporal persistence, demonstrating a strong capability for geographic extrapolation. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals distinct non-linear controls. Two critical elevation thresholds (~2900 m and 3700 m) govern changes in soil water content (SWC): SWC decreases with elevation below 2900 m due to transpiration offsetting precipitation, increases between 2900 m and 3700 m due to net water accumulation, and the impact of elevation weakens above 3700 m because of permafrost and ice effects. Additionally, a U-shaped relationship between SOC and SWC indicates higher SWC at both low ( 4.6 g/kg) SOC levels, highlighting SOC as an integrative indicator of soil hydraulic properties. These non-linear patterns cannot be captured by traditional linear correlation analysis.

title: Moisture-dependent erodibility and flooding potential of alluvial clay and peat soils in Selangor, Malaysia
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Azlan Shah Nerwan Shah, Nor Shahidah Mohd Nazer, Zulaikha Nabila Ahmad Pua’ad, Anis Syazwani Jamsus, Nabila Nurina, Mohd Hariri Arifin
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Quaternary alluvial plains of Selangor, Malaysia. Flood-driven erosion in these urbanizing tropical monsoon catchments remains poorly understood despite high vulnerability to interacting hydraulic forces, rainfall, and varying soil moisture. Study focus Controlled flume experiments evaluated cohesive clay and peat soils under three rainfall intensities (16, 42, 105 mm/h), three slopes (0°, 15°, 30°), and five moisture levels (0%–40%). Measured detachment rates and excess-shear metrics, examined by principal component analysis, identified a primary hydraulic forcing axis and a secondary moisture-influenced soil-state axis for precise determination of sediment transport control. New hydrological insights for the region The soils display distinct behaviours with important hydrological implications. Dry clay is highly erodible with a critical shear stress of 8.02 Pa and detaches 1.3 times faster than dry peat. Above 30% moisture, mineral swelling and matrix sealing increase clay thresholds to 17.50 Pa, reducing erodibility by two orders of magnitude and detachment by 11.5-fold. This response alters runoff dynamics during intense rainfall. Conversely, peat thresholds increase from 19.43 Pa under dry conditions to 44.11 Pa under wet conditions, though erodibility declines only modestly. This trend promotes continuous fibrous sloughing and greater surface water retention than clay, potentially contributing to prolonged inundation and elevated sediment transport. These empirical parameters support process based geomorphic models and enhance the understanding of flooding potential in tropical climates.

title: Assessment framework of main functions of water conservation using a multi-variable calibrated WEP-L model
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Dongdong Wang, Yangwen Jia, Cunwen Niu, Jiajia Liu, Junkai Du, Yaobing Sui, Chunfeng Hao
abstract: Study regions The water conservation area in the Yellow River Basin (YRB WCA) of China, a key ecological function zone with high annual runoff coefficients. Study focus Most water conservation (WC) function assessments in large basins focus on quantity. This study proposes a new framework for evaluating both the quantity and three main functions. A distributed hydrological model calibrated with multi-variable data was used to improve accuracy. New hydrological insights for the regions WC quantity significantly decreased only in Region II (Southern Wei River tributaries). Across all regions, vegetation ecological water use (WC-f1) generally improved, flood reduction (WC-f2) remained stable, while baseflow enhancement (WC-f3) weakened only in Region II. Precipitation and NDVI were primary driving factors of WC quantity, with positive effects except in central Region I (above the Lanzhou area). Temperature, evapotranspiration, and DEM also influenced the three functions. In addition, changes in forest, cropland, and built-up areas since 2000 had strong localized influences on WC-f1 and WC-f2, though their overall impacts were weak. Vegetation restoration strategies should vary by downstream water demand and functional priorities: reduce vegetation cover in central Region I to enhance WC quantity; increase vegetation cover in southeastern Region I and Region III (the Yiluo River Basin) to enhance WC-f2; reduce grassland area in northern Region I and western Region II to enhance WC-f3.

title: Analysis of meteorological to hydrological propagation characteristics of drought-to-flood abrupt alternation events in near-natural catchments
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Jiahui Gu, Yifei Zheng, Jiali Guo, Kunteng Zhang, Jijun Chen, Jie Chen, Shreedhar Maskey, Huiting Chen, Xin Xiang, Chengyun Wang
abstract: Study region This study focuses on 1034 near-natural catchments grouped into eight hydroclimatic-physiographic types using climatic, topographic, soil, and hydrological attributes. Study focus Drought-to-flood abrupt alternation (DTF) may not directly translate from meteorological anomalies into streamflow hazards because catchments can filter, delay, or amplify atmospheric signals. Meteorological DTF (M-DTF) and hydrological DTF (H-DTF) events were identified using standardized weighted precipitation and runoff indices. A one-to-one event-matching framework was used to quantify propagation rate, delay, and intensity evolution from M-DTF to H-DTF. We evaluated the statistical associations of these metrics with meteorological forcing and catchment attributes. New hydrological insights for the region M-DTF events were more frequent, abrupt, and severe than H-DTF events, whereas H-DTF events persisted 2.9 times longer on average. Across the analyzed catchments, the mean catchment-level PR within the adopted 90-day matching window was 12%, consistent with substantial catchment filtering. Warm-humid and runoff-responsive catchments had higher propagation rates and shorter delays, whereas high-elevation and snow-dominated catchments had weaker and delayed propagation. Abruptness and severity were attenuated in 70% and 77% of catchments, respectively, although arid, low-runoff catchments sometimes showed greater hydrological severity than their matched meteorological events. These findings provide an empirical basis for regional DTF risk assessment and the future development and evaluation of streamflow-oriented early-warning approaches.

title: A multi-source adaptive transfer learning model integrating spatiotemporal environmental perception for runoff prediction in data-scarce basins of the Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhongfeng Zhao, Xueni Wang, Leike Zhang, Xuehua Zhao, Xueping Zhu, Wenjun Cai, Jing Xie
abstract: Study region The study area is located on the Loess Plateau of China. The catchments controlled by the Ganguyi, Hejin, Huaxian, Sanmenxia, and Wenjiachuan hydrological stations are selected as source basins, whereas the catchments controlled by the Tongguan and Yanchuan stations are designated as data-scarce target basins. Study focus To overcome data scarcity constraints and enhance physical plausibility, a multi-source adaptive transfer learning model integrating spatiotemporal environmental perception (termed Transformer-LSTM-MATL) is proposed. Based on the Transformer-LSTM model, this model first creates a heterogeneous prior knowledge base with a variety of source basins. A dynamic attention mechanism is incorporated to characterize the evolving environmental conditions in the target basin. By tracking multidimensional environmental features, the model dynamically adjusts the contribution of different source basins, which allows more flexible knowledge transfer than conventional single-source or static transfer approaches. Ultimately, through effective aggregation of multi-source knowledge, the runoff prediction accuracy in data-scarce basins is significantly improved. New hydrological insights for the region Evaluations in two typical data-scarce basins of the Loess Plateau demonstrate that the multi-source transfer model achieves Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values exceeding 0.8. Compared with single-source transfer models and direct prediction models, NSE increases by 9.77%-168.23%, while the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) decreases by 21.25%-56.56%. Meanwhile, the Pearson correlation coefficient (R) improves by 1.23%-25.75%. Further analysis of the attention weights indicates that their spatiotemporal variation is closely related to basin landscape characteristics and seasonal hydrological regimes. This pattern suggests that the fusion preferences of the model are generally consistent with hydrological understanding rather than being driven solely by statistical fitting. Overall, by accomplishing a comprehensive validation from simulation metrics to hydrological plausibility, a robust runoff prediction model balancing high predictive accuracy and physical interpretability for data-scarce basins is presented in this study.

title: Decoupling climate and anthropogenic drivers of hydrological alteration in the Yellow River Basin: A hybrid deep learning framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Bowen Xue, Qianyun Chen, Yicheng Fu, Yanhui Liu, Xiuzhi Chen, Amjad Khan
abstract: Study region Yellow River Basin, China. Study focus While the impacts of climate change and human activities on river systems are widely recognized, decoupling their highly non-linear interactions in heavily engineered basins remains computationally and analytically challenging. This study addresses this gap by proposing an advanced hybrid deep learning framework that integrates multiscale statistical diagnostics, the Range of Variability Approach (RVA), a Particle Swarm Optimization-Long Short-Term Memory (PSO-LSTM) model, and Random Forest (RF) algorithms. This framework incorporates rigorous convergence validation for PSO optimization, multi-method cross-validation for change-point detection, and comprehensive collinearity diagnostics. This integrated approach is employed to systematically evaluate longitudinal hydrological alterations and precisely attribute the drivers of runoff evolution from 1960 to 2020 across the basin. New hydrological insights Across the Yellow River Basin, abrupt runoff reductions and the magnitude of hydrological alteration amplify consistently from headwaters to estuary, superimposed on a basin-wide 11–14 year climatic periodicity. A distinct spatial dichotomy governs driving mechanisms: climatic factors dominate runoff generation in the upstream source area, whereas cumulative anthropogenic interventions – including reservoir regulation and large-scale vegetation restoration – drive over 80% of the runoff decline in the middle and lower reaches. Widespread vegetation greening and land-use transitions have fundamentally shifted the basin’s blue-green water balance toward enhanced evapotranspiration, dampening peak flows and exacerbating downstream water scarcity. Upstream inflow acts as the absolute controlling factor for downstream hydrology; after removing its cascading effect, local climatic drivers remain dominant in the source area but contribute only marginally to downstream runoff. These findings clarify the full-basin longitudinal pattern of hydrological alteration and its spatially heterogeneous drivers, addressing a long-standing knowledge gap for the Yellow River Basin. They provide direct, actionable scientific support for differentiated water resource management and targeted ecological restoration planning across reaches, underpinning sustainable water security strategies for this water-scarce, highly engineered basin.

title: Flood redistribution and hydraulic responses to controlled levee breaching in highly Leveed urban rivers
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Shunyu Xiao, Jingming Hou, Yongping Yang, Liping Ma, Donglai Li, Jiahao Lv, Baojun Guan, Yanhong Wang, Haobo Qiu, Yue Ren, Chao Li, Junduo Gao
abstract: Study region Study region: The upper reach of the Ganjiang River in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, China, where rapid urbanization and extensive levee systems have increased exposure to extreme flood hazards. Study focus A coupled 1D-2D hydrodynamic model (GAST) was applied to simulate an overtopping scenario (MY) and three controlled levee-breach scenarios (A, B, C) under 50-, 100-, and 500-year flood events. Breach discharge, downstream hydraulic responses, and spatiotemporal inundation were analysed to quantify how breach location and flood magnitude influence flood redistribution and downstream flood propagation. New hydrological insights for the region Controlled levee breaching modifies flood redistribution between the river channel and adjacent floodplains, with downstream hydraulic responses jointly regulated by breach location and flood magnitude. Upstream breaches produced the greatest downstream peak attenuation, reducing peak discharge by 3.87–10.31% and peak water level by 0.26–0.93 m through earlier redistribution of channel flow. In contrast, peak-delay mechanisms evolved with flood magnitude, as floodplain storage increasingly influenced flood-wave propagation during larger floods. Controlled levee breaching also reshaped the spatial distribution of flood hazards, increasing inundation area by 10.89–39.50% and inundation volume by 28.22–150.33% within receiving areas while reducing downstream flood impacts. These findings advance process-based understanding of flood redistribution in highly leveed urban rivers and provide transferable insights into downstream hydraulic responses in highly leveed river–floodplain systems with comparable channel–floodplain hydraulic controls.

title: Multi-layer aquifer hydrogeological responses to deep coal mining and their controlling mechanisms: A hydrochemical and multi-isotope coupling study
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): He Cui, Limin Duan, Hao Pan, Shen Qu, Tingxi Liu
abstract: Study region The Dahaize Coal Mine lies on the southern margin of the Mu Us Sandy Land, a key part of the large coal energy base in northern Shaanxi, China. Study focus Deep coal mining severely disturbs regional groundwater stability, yet the long-term and multi-scale responses of hydrogeological functions of multi-layer aquifers in mining areas remain poorly understood. This study combines hydrochemical approaches with multiple isotopic tracers (δ2H, δ18O, δ34S, δ18Osulfate, and 222Rn) to elucidate spatiotemporal evolution features and dominant driving mechanisms of multi-layer aquifer hydrogeological functions across the whole coal mining cycle. New hydrological insights for the region Phreatic water (PW) and Anding Formation confined water (ADCW) maintained stable hydrogeological functions. PW was mainly affected by sulfate leached from coal gangue under rainfall infiltration, while ADCW was slightly improved owing to weakened vertical leakage recharge. By contrast, Zhiluo Formation confined water (ZLCW) suffered severe functional degradation driven by expanding water-conducting fracture zones (WCFZs). WCFZs lowered hydraulic gradients, slowed groundwater flow and promoted evaporite dissolution. As preferential flow pathways and geochemical reaction interfaces, WCFZs strengthened hydraulic connectivity between ZLCW and mine water (MW), accelerated cation exchange, carbonate dissolution and radon emission, and caused simultaneous enrichment of SO 4 2 - , δ18O, δ34S, and 222Rn in the two aquifers. This study deepens the understanding of the driving mechanisms for the hydrogeological functional evolution of aquifers in mining areas.

title: Uncertainty assessment of non-stationary stage-discharge relationship with hydrodynamic extensions across flow regimes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Cheng-Wei Yu, Bo-Han Chen
abstract: Study region: Asia Pacific region, Taiwan. Study focus: Accurate discharge estimation in river systems is fundamentally hindered by the scarcity of high-flow measurements and the complexities of channel non-stationarity. This study introduces an integrated framework that reconciles historical in-situ observations with hydrodynamically derived synthetic relationships to bridge critical data gaps. We employ a dual-methodology paradigm, utilizing both a Bayesian inference model (BaRatin) and a fuzzy regression framework to simultaneously address probabilistic variability and inherent measurement uncertainty. This approach ensures a comprehensive evaluation across the full spectrum of flow regimes at two gauging stations in the Wu River Basin. New hydrological insights: This research explicitly incorporates high-flow extensions generated via the Height Above the Nearest Drainage (HAND) method into the uncertainty assessment, offering a physically consistent approach that utilizes hydraulic constraints rarely explored in rating-curve literature. Results demonstrate that while uncertainty is most pronounced under low-flow conditions due to channel irregularities, the bounds converge significantly to within ± 35%–75% in high-flow regimes. The Bayesian method effectively captures structural errors in complex channel–floodplain reaches, whereas fuzzy regression offers a computationally efficient alternative for data-scarce scenarios. Notably, integrating HAND-based hydrodynamic information reduces high-flow bias and enhances the continuity between empirical and synthetic segments. This framework establishes a statistically defensible basis for discharge estimation, significantly improving uncertainty quantification in both gauged and ungauged catchments.

title: Future runoff responses to dynamic coal mining expansion and climate change in China's Kuye river basin using a modified hydrological model
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Guoxin Sun, Dengfeng Liu, Bo Ming, Guanghui Ming, Jinkai Luan, Qiang Li, Fubo Zhao, Mohd Yawar Ali Khan, Fiaz Hussain, Xiaohui Jiang
abstract: Study Region The Kuye River Basin (KRB), an intensive coal-mining watershed in the middle reaches of the Yellow River, China. Study Focus Despite relatively stable precipitation, the KRB has experienced substantial runoff decline, suggesting strong mining impacts on watershed hydrology. Conventional hydrological models often fail to represent mining-induced surface alteration and groundwater leakage. This study developed a modified SWAT-M model by defining mining areas as an independent land-use category. A multi-basin comparative analysis was conducted to identify the causes of runoff decline, and future runoff (2031–2100) was projected under 16 combined climate–land-use scenarios derived from seven CMIP6 models and the PLUS model. New Hydrological Insights for the Region During the major mining-expansion period (1990–2010), the standardized runoff depth at Wenjiachuan declined at −4.10 mm/a, substantially exceeding the decline in the less-disturbed Jialu River Basin (−1.36 mm/a), indicating that mining-induced hydrological disturbance is a major driver of runoff reduction. Explicit representation of mining areas improved model performance; during 2011–2020, NSE increased from −0.13 to 0.41 at Wangdaohengta and from 0.02 to 0.44 at Wenjiachuan. Future runoff was primarily controlled by climate forcing and generally increased with higher radiative forcing. Relative to the historical period, runoff at Wangdaohengta ranged from −49.75% to + 26.1%, whereas runoff at Shenmu and Wenjiachuan remained below historical levels under all scenarios, with a maximum reduction of 67.0% at the basin outlet.
